# Dulja — Plan Contracts (Phases 0B–9)

**Date:** 2026-09-05 · **Version:** **2026-09-07** (amended in two rounds — round 1 from the six Phase 0/1 plans, round 2 from 2A, 2B, 2C and 9A; both change lists are §4.18; cite this value in every plan header's *Contracts version* line) · **Status:** binding for every plan written after Plan 0A · **Spec:** `docs/spec/rebuild-spec.md` v1.2 (cited as `spec:LINE`) · **Fixed input:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-04-dulja-phase-0-foundations.md` (Plan 0A, cited as `plan0A:LINE`; its SQL is executed and verified on PostgreSQL 18 — everything it *Produces* is immovable).

---

## 1. Purpose and how to use this document

**Thirty** slice plans across nine phases (0B, 0C, 0D, 0E and 1–9 — the inventory is §6.4) will be written in parallel by engineers who cannot see each other's work. This document fixes, once, every **name, shape and boundary** those plans share: slice ids and file names, migration and ADR number ranges, the TypeScript signatures of the posting service, `withTenant`, `Money`, the error envelope, the permission catalogue, the job helper, the sync messages, every table the spec names beyond migration 0001, every shared literal namespace (document-type codes §4.14, **account codes §4.15**, **report codes and dataset ids §4.16**, **`fixtures.ts` helpers §4.17**), and the rule for who owns a contested table. **Every plan writer reads this document before the spec; every reviewer checks a plan against it; every name here is frozen.** A plan that needs a different name, a different column, a different signature or a different migration number changes *this document first* (one PR, reviewed) and only then the plan. Where the spec is silent this document invents exactly one convention and marks it **convention (not in spec)**; where the spec contradicts itself the resolution is stated once in §4 with the citations. Nothing in this document re-opens decisions D1–D27 (spec:114–142) or decides any owner-pending ⚠️ item — those are listed in §2.12 and are each isolated into one droppable task per plan.

---

## 2. Plan catalogue

### 2.0 How the catalogue is organised

**Slice id and file name.** Every plan is one *slice* `<phase><letter>` written to `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-dulja-phase-<phase><letter>-<slug>.md` (the writing-plans skill's `YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md` form; the date is this document's date so the whole generation sorts together after Plan 0A). Letters run in dependency order within a phase; `A` is the entry slice.

**Phase 0 letters.** Plan 0A's roadmap (plan0A:36–53) and its final `CLAUDE.md` (plan0A:2906–2909) already name **0B** = API core (Supabase Auth + `withTenant`, permission catalogue, `Money`, dimensions/custom-fields API, pg-boss) and **0C** = Supabase + Cloudflare + seed CLI + Electron + i18n shell + observability. Each is ~25 tasks at Plan 0A grain, so each is split at the sizing ceiling. The meanings of 0B and 0C are kept; the overflow becomes two new letters:

| Plan 0A name | Contracts slices | Split rule |
|---|---|---|
| Plan 0B | **0B** (identity, `withTenant`, errors, idempotency, permission catalogue, admin endpoints, root `tests/` tree) + **0D** (`Money`/`Quantity`, currency + rates, dimensions/custom-fields API, pg-boss, catalogue lints, `seed/roles.ts`) | 0D is everything in Plan 0A's "0B" that Phase 1 consumes as a library rather than as an HTTP surface |
| Plan 0C | **0C** (Supabase, Cloudflare, seed CLI, observability) + **0E** (i18n shell, `packages/ui`, `apps/backoffice`, Electron shell, PDF-engine spike) | 0E is everything in Plan 0A's "0C" that runs on the desktop |

The last task of 0B rewrites the "Current phase" section of `CLAUDE.md` to name all four (see §3.8). Execution order is **0B → 0D → 0C → 0E** (0C's infrastructure tasks may start after 0B; its seed task needs 0D).

**Sizing.** Every slice targets **10–15 TDD tasks** at the Plan 0A grain (one table group or one service seam per task, failing test first, commit per task). Where the Part V reader's estimate exceeded 15 the slice is split here (Phase 2 into three, Phase 6 into four, Phase 7 into three, Phase 8 into four) — a plan writer who finds a slice growing past 15 tasks stops and amends this catalogue rather than growing the plan.

**What a task and a slice cost, in lines.** Plan 0A is **2,947 lines for 12 tasks** (its Tasks 1–12 begin at plan0A:110, 218, 380, 578, 823, 1080, 1547, 1889, 2131, 2426, 2599, 2824) — about **246 lines per task** at the grain every plan here must match. So a 12-task slice is ~3,000 lines and a 15-task slice ~3,700. Both are writable; the number is given so a writer can tell early whether a slice is really 15 tasks or is 15 task *headings* over 20 tasks of work. **A plan whose draft passes ~3,700 lines while tasks remain unwritten is over the ceiling in substance even if the count says 15** — stop and amend this catalogue. The five heaviest slices — the ones whose Delivers list is longest against a 15-task bound — name their split point in the card (**3A, 4A, 6A, 6B, 8A**) so the writer who hits it does not have to invent one. Any other slice that overruns amends this catalogue the same way. A split creates `<id>′` with the same file-name convention, inherits the tail of the parent's migration and ADR ranges, and is recorded here in the same PR.

**Definition of done.** Each phase's Part V "Definition of done" cell (spec:2286–2296) is quoted **verbatim** on the first slice of the phase and its clauses are assigned to slices under "This slice's share". A phase exits only when every slice's share is green in CI (spec:87).

**Acceptance tests and coverage rows.** Each Part VI test (spec:2419–2457) and each §3.0.4 row (spec:1040–1067) has exactly **one owning slice** — the slice whose completion makes every clause of the test runnable (for a row: whose completion closes the row). Other slices that exercise the test list it under "Re-runs". The full matrices are in §6.

**Owner decisions.** Every owner-pending item (spec §5.3, the ⚠️ rows, the changelog *Confirm*/*Decide* rows, Part VII) has an id `OD-nn` in §2.12. A slice that depends on one carries it under "Owner gates", and **the plan isolates each into exactly one task** — written as "owner provides X; verify with `<exact command>`" with a local (Testcontainers / stub) equivalent — so it can be dropped or swapped without touching neighbouring tasks. No plan waits on an owner decision to be *written*; only that one task waits to be *executed*.

**Migration and ADR numbers.** Each slice owns a closed range (§3.4, §3.9). A slice writes only inside its range; the runner applies whatever is unapplied in version order, so ranges need not be applied in numeric order across parallel phases.

### 2.1 Phase 0 — Foundations (slices 0B, 0D, 0C, 0E)

Phase 0 row of the phase table, verbatim (spec:2286): **Scope** "Monorepo + CI, Cloudflare Container + Worker skeleton, tenancy + RLS, Supabase Auth integration, RBAC, append-only audit log, Electron shell for the back office, i18n/RTL shell, currency & rate service, dimension framework, custom-field service, migration tooling, ledger-integrity job skeleton (§5.0)". **Definition of done** "A tenant is created, users invited, roles assigned; every write audited with server-supplied actor; the tenant-isolation suite passes against every endpoint". **Phase 0 exit** (spec:2327): "every row above green (0.1 → 0.7, 0.7b, 0.8 → 0.15), plus acceptance tests 12, 13 and 14 passing in CI. Only then does Phase 1 (the ledger) begin." **Binding exit gate (union of spec:2327 with the Done-when cells of 0.6 and 0.7, spec:2315–2316):** every §5.0 row green **and** tests 11, 12, 13, 14, 27 pass in CI **and** the catalogue-integrity, incompatible-pair, auditor-read-only, expired-assignment and one-query assertions of test 36 pass against the Phase 0 catalogue. Plan 0A has already closed 0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.8, 0.15 and the table halves of 0.2, 0.7, 0.10.

### 2.4 Phase 3 — Inventory (slices 3A, 3B, 3C, 3D)

Phase 3 row, verbatim (spec:2289). **Scope:** "Items, exact-rational UoM, warehouses, **lots with expiry**, variants, movements, **cost layers**, **landed cost allocation** through an import-shipment document, **sales and purchase orders** (non-posting, open-quantity tracked), **goods receipt with GRNI accrual**, **delivery orders**, certificates and permits attached per lot, **stock counts with variance posting**, **two-step inter-branch transfers with an in-transit state**, **expiry write-off**, free-of-charge lines, price lists, valuation (§3.0.4). Serials only if §3.0.3 confirms them." **Definition of done:** "Back-dated purchase recosts only forward, in bounded time, with a visible adjustment entry; FEFO picking returns the earliest-expiring lot; a landed-cost allocation changes unit cost and every downstream margin; a stock count posts only the variance; goods in transit are in neither warehouse's on-hand and in the company's total".

The §5.3 "Phase 3" row (spec:2404) — "Confirmation of every ⚠️ row in §3.0.3 and §3.0.4, and the v1 costing method (§3.4)" — is **OD-05/OD-06/OD-07/OD-08** in §2.12. Phase 3 plans are written against the spec defaults (AVCO; no serials, BOM, consignment, commissions, project costing; food is batch-tracked) with the conditional items as isolated tasks.

### 2.9 Phase 8 — HR & Payroll (slices 8A, 8B, 8C, 8D)

Phase 8 row, verbatim (spec:2294). **Scope:** "§3.10: employee master and sensitive data, effective-dated compensation and pay components, statutory schemes as versioned verified rate tables, PAYROLL / PAYROLL_PAYMENT / EMPLOYEE_ADVANCE document types and statutory remittances, payslips and monthly schedules, `employee_ytd` projection, a minimal leave register ⚠️ *(only if the owner confirms — §3.10.1, Part VII item 14)*, attendance events, termination flow, five HR reports". **Definition of done:** "The business's real monthly payroll runs in Dulja **in parallel with the legacy system for one month**: every gross, statutory and net figure matches the legacy run and the authorities' calculators to the cent, or every difference is explained in writing and accepted by the owner; the run posts through the posting service under pinned policy and rate-table versions; Σ payslip net = salaries-payable credit; each scheme's schedule = its payable to the cent; preparer ≠ approver is enforced by the data layer; `employee_ytd` rebuilds bit-identically". Sequencing (spec:2301): depends on Phases 1, 2 and 4; "may start as soon as Phase 4 is green and run alongside Phases 5–7"; "must be complete before Phase 9".

**Statutory-rate rule for every Phase 8 plan:** "This document states no rate, threshold, ceiling or formula" (spec:2080). No plan, test, fixture or seed file in the repository contains a real Malaysian EPF/SOCSO/EIS/PCB figure until the owner's accountant-signed tables arrive (OD-23); golden tests run on a **clearly synthetic** rate table named `SYNTHETIC-TEST-v1` (§4.12.4). Real tables enter only as `packages/db/seed/my/statutory/<scheme>/vN.json` with `source`, `loaded_by`, `verified_by`.

- `EMPLOYEE` dimension type with one value per employee, created by trigger on `employee` insert (§4.12.7); every PAYROLL ledger line carries BRANCH (home branch, `dimensions.required`) and EMPLOYEE (spec:2101); chart-of-accounts seed additions `chart-of-accounts/8b-payroll.json` (§4.15) with their fixed codes — **`5300` salaries expense, `2400` salaries payable, `1400` staff advances, `2411`–`2414` statutory payable per scheme and `5311`–`5314` employer-contribution expense per scheme in `EPF`, `SOCSO`, `EIS`, `PCB` order** — and the same seed task sets `pay_component.expense_account_id`, `statutory_scheme.payable_account_id` and `employer_expense_account_id` from those codes, so 8C's `PAYROLL_PAYMENT` and `EMPLOYEE_ADVANCE` resolve `2400` and `1400` without seeding anything of their own.
- calculate → submit → approve → post on the shared state machine; R3: a compensation change effective in the period of a `submitted`/`approved` run returns it to `draft` with `reason = 'compensation_changed'` (spec:2174); refusal of unverified/out-of-range tables (`ERR_PAYROLL_RATE_TABLE_UNVERIFIED`, test 29); missing statutory input fails naming the employee (`ERR_PAYROLL_INPUT_MISSING`, test 33; SAH-011); manual statutory override line with reason + `entered_by`, flagged and listed at approval (spec:2087); proration; unpaid-leave deduction quantity.
- Test 38 through `accounting.period.reopen` with reason, audited and reported (spec:2179, 2456).
- `tests/golden/payroll/` on `SYNTHETIC-TEST-v1` (byte-identical lines, entries, payslip data — test 33's mechanism); test 28 (PAYROLL vs hand-keyed JOURNAL).
- Codes `hr.payroll.read`, `hr.payroll.prepare`, `hr.payroll.approve`, `hr.payroll.post`; and the `hr` row of the attachment download map, `hr → hr.payroll.read` (§4.5.8), which could not be written before this code existed.
- **`employee_ytd` is not written here.** The table is 8C's (migration 0092) and 8C owns the `postDocument` step-12 MERGE (§4.12.8); this slice's payslip and YTD figures come from posted `payroll_line` rows.
- **Employer contributions are not a `pay_component.kind`.** `pay_component.kind` is `earning | deduction` (spec:2079, §4.6.1); the employer share of a scheme is selected in the PAYROLL policy by `when: { "line.share": "employer" }` with `account.from: "line.scheme.expense_account"` (spec:2101), and `line.component.kind` in the policy schema admits the same two values.

**This slice's share of the DoD:** "the run posts through the posting service under pinned policy and rate-table versions; preparer ≠ approver is enforced by the data layer".

### 2.10 Phase 9 — Migration (slices 9A, 9B)

Phase 9 row, verbatim (spec:2295). **Scope:** "Importer reading the live Sahlisoft Firebird database → Dulja. Items, customers, suppliers, open balances, open documents, batch/expiry positions, **employee master and current-tax-year YTD** (§5.1 items 11–12)." **Definition of done:** "Trial balance **and** stock valuation match the source on the cut-over date, and the difference on every recomputed figure is explained (§5.1); each employee's imported YTD reconciles to their last legacy payslip".

#### 9A — Extraction, profiling, reconciliation reports, legacy catalogues

Writing a `VouItemRow`/`BillItemRow`/`EmployeeRow` here would mean transcribing column lists nobody has confirmed against a live database, and every value crosses the seam as text because the reader casts every scaled-numeric and date column to `varchar` (hazard 3, spec:2041). **9B invents none either** until a live `scope`/`profile` artefact has been read, and records that reading in its ADR if it then wants named shapes.

- Cut-over decision inputs for the owner (suspense treatment — §5.1 #2; POS history — Part VII #10).

### 2.11 Phase 10 — Other verticals (deferred; no plan)

Phase 10 gets **no plan**. Verbatim (spec:2296): scope "Fixed assets and depreciation (manual JOURNALs until then), service contracts and maintenance, purchase-requisition and PO-approval workflow. **Do not build in v1.** The clinic, school and aviation modules should very likely never be built."; definition of done "Each vertical ships and upgrades independently of the core"; header (spec:2282) "Phase 10 (other verticals) is **deferred indefinitely** — build it only if a paying customer ever asks"; sequencing (spec:2302) "Do not start Phase 10 until Phases 1–3 have been running in production for a customer." Consequences that bind the v1 plans: depreciation is a manual `JOURNAL` (Phase 1); sales and purchase orders carry "no approval workflow (that stays Phase 10)" (spec:1050); `BillOfMaterials`, `SerialUnit` and Party kinds `student | dealer` (spec:1169, 1181–1182) are **reserved names only** — `party.kind` admits them as enum labels so no migration is needed later, but no v1 plan creates a `bill_of_materials` table and `serial_unit` exists only if OD-07 confirms serials (F-16).

## 3. Frozen conventions

Everything in this section is stated once. Plans cite it by section number instead of restating it.

### 3.1 Repository layout and the dependency rule (spec §5.2)

**6B amendment A3.** `@dulja/db/staff/pin` is the sole production database-package subpath allowed in `apps/pos`: `packages/db/package.json` exports `"./staff/pin": "./src/staff/pin.ts"`. Keep the existing server barrel unchanged; never bundle the PostgreSQL driver into the till. Desktop imports POS build outputs only, by filesystem path, with channel names supplied as data. Remove the obsolete named test-helper allowance to API terminal-auth when A2 moves signing into sync.

The layout is spec:2352–2387 (reproduced in Plan 0A's tree for the parts that exist). **Dependency rule, verbatim (spec:2389):** "`domain` imports nothing from the other packages. `db` and `contracts` import `domain`. `api`, `worker`, `pos`, `backoffice` import from packages, never from each other. `desktop` imports only build outputs. Anything that violates this is a bug in the architecture, not a style issue."

**The second, intra-package rule, verbatim (spec:2366)**, stated of `packages/domain` inside the same §5.2 tree: "`payroll/`: the statutory calculators and the rate-table JSON schema (§3.10); **core never imports HR**." It binds every Phase 8 plan and the posting evaluator: `packages/domain/src/**` may not import from `packages/domain/payroll/**`; the reverse is allowed. The shapes the evaluator needs from the HR world (`PayComponentRef`, `SchemeRef`, `PayrollLineRef`) are therefore declared **in core**, in `packages/domain/src/posting/evaluate.ts` (§4.4.2), and `packages/domain/payroll/`'s own richer types satisfy them structurally — 8B maps onto them and imports nothing back.

Both are enforced by `scripts/lint/rules/dependency-rule.ts` (0B) over every `import` in `apps/**` and `packages/**`, which checks the cross-package tiers of spec:2389 **and** the `packages/domain/src/**` → `packages/domain/payroll/**` prohibition of spec:2366.

**Package names (frozen).** Plan 0A fixed only `@dulja/db`. The rest follow the same rule — `@dulja/<directory name>`, `private: true`, `type: module`, TypeScript source exported directly (no `dist/`) unless the package is a deployable:

**The seed is reachable only through the `@dulja/db/seed` subpath, never through the main barrel — settled (round 2).** `packages/db/src/index.ts` carries **no** `export … from "./seed…"` of any depth. 0C's `tests/regression/sah-039.test.ts` asserts exactly that (`expect(barrel).not.toMatch(/from ["']\.\/seed/)`), because `packages/db/src/seed/auth-admin.ts` imports `@supabase/supabase-js` and a barrel re-export would put the service-role admin client on the import graph of every `apps/api` and `apps/worker` module that imports `withTenant`. **The regex catches a deeper path too**, so `export * from "./seed/document-types";` is a violation of it even though `document-types.ts` imports no Supabase itself — and the depth is not the point: a barrel that re-exports one seed module today re-exports the next one by copy-and-paste. **Additional directories (convention, not in spec):** `scripts/lint/` (custom CI lint rules — §3.7.5), `docs/runbooks/` (restore drill, cut-over), `packages/db/seed/my/<pack>/` sub-packs `chart-of-accounts/`, `dimensions/`, `fiscal-periods/`, `document-types/`, `templates/`, `reports/`, `tax/`, `statutory/<scheme>/` (spec:2080, 2368). Root `package.json` `workspaces` becomes `["packages/*", "apps/*", "tests"]` in 0B — turbo's `test` pipeline (plan0A:259–266) only sees workspace packages, so `tests/` must be one. **0C appends `"infra"`, making it `["packages/*", "apps/*", "tests", "infra"]`**: `infra/` carries its own Vitest suite over the Dockerfile, the entrypoint script and the wrangler config, and turbo's pipeline only sees workspace packages.

**Workspace scripts contract (from Plan 0A, plan0A:224, 259–266):** every workspace exposes `typecheck` and `test` (and `build` if it emits `dist/`); `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` at the root must stay green after every task; `lint:rules` is added by 0B and joins CI after `bun run lint`.

### 3.2 Naming, identifiers, time, money (spec §3.9 — verbatim, binding)

- **Identifiers** (spec:2037): "`uuidv7()` server-side for everything (time-ordered, index-friendly). The POS generates a `uuidv7` at the till for each ticket (the `uuid` npm package or Bun's built-in), carried as `document.client_ref`. Never a sequential integer as a public identifier; never reuse; never rewind (SAH-021)."
- **Time and dates** (spec:2039): "All timestamps `timestamptz`, stored in UTC. Every company has a `timezone` (`Asia/Kuala_Lumpur` for the first customer). **`effective_date` is a `date`, entered by the user, and is the accounting date** — it is never derived from `posted_at`. Fiscal period is resolved from `effective_date` at posting and stored on the row. Hijri display is a presentation concern via `Intl`; storage is always Gregorian."
- **Money** (spec:2041): "`numeric(19,4)` in Postgres. In TypeScript, `Money` is an opaque type wrapping `decimal.js`, carrying its currency; the compiler rejects adding MYR to USD. Display rounding applies the currency's policy at render time; **stored base amounts are never recomputed on read.** No `number` type ever holds a monetary value — a lint rule enforces it."
- **Quantities** (spec:2043): "`numeric(19,6)`. Unit conversions are exact rationals `(numerator bigint, denominator bigint)`, never floats (SAH-066). Quantity is stored once, in the item's base unit; the entered unit and quantity are kept for display."
- **Naming** (spec:2045): "`snake_case` everywhere in SQL; **singular** table names (`ledger_entry`, not `ledger_entries`), matching §3.8; enum types singular. TypeScript: `camelCase`, types `PascalCase`. Bilingual names on master data as `name_en` / `name_ar` columns — not a JSON blob." **Application to inconsistencies in 0001 (plan0A:1568):** `role`, `account`, `document_type` carry `name_en`/`name_ar`; `dimension_type`/`dimension_value` gain `name_ar` in 0D (migration 0007); `tenant`, `company`, `pos_terminal` keep a single `name` — they are proper names, not translated labels (**convention, not in spec**). Every new master-data table with a translated label uses `name_en text not null, name_ar text`.
- **Enumerations** (spec:2047): "Postgres `enum` for closed sets the code branches on (`document_status`, `period_status`, `account_type`). A lookup table for open sets the user extends (`document_type`, `dimension_type`, `tax_code`)." New closed sets in this document are `text` columns with a `CHECK (col in (…))` rather than Postgres enums **when a later phase is expected to add a label** (CHECKs can be altered in one file; enum labels cannot be used in the file that adds them — §3.4.4). The four 0001 enums stay enums.
- **Deletion** (spec:2049): "Financial rows: never — reversal only. Master data: `archived_at`, never `DELETE`. HR master data: archived, never deleted; a terminated employee keeps every payroll line and payslip for the statutory retention period. Genuine deletion exists only for drafts and for the GDPR/PDPA erasure workflow, and both write an audit row first."
- **Error codes** (spec:2051): "Every error the API can return has a stable string code `ERR_<DOMAIN>_<REASON>` (`ERR_LEDGER_UNBALANCED`, `ERR_PERIOD_NOT_OPEN`, `ERR_STOCK_INSUFFICIENT`), a human message naming the specific entity, and a remedy. Codes are enumerated in one file; a code no code raises fails the build (the inverse of SAH-084)." The one file is `packages/contracts/src/errors.ts` (§4.2.4).
- **Database access** (spec:2053): "Every query — reads included — runs inside `withTenant(tx => …)`, which opens the transaction and issues the two `set_config(…, true)` calls before anything else. A lint rule forbids bare `db.` calls. Without this RLS silently returns zero rows (§3.8)."
- **API** (spec:2055): "`/v1/…`. Cursor pagination. `Idempotency-Key` header required on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. `application/problem+json` errors. OpenAPI generated from Zod, committed, diffed in CI."
- **Localisation** (spec:2061) and **Logging** (spec:2063) apply verbatim; Plan 0A's `no-console` rule is the logging lint; the override glob `packages/*/src/cli.ts` (plan0A:301) means **every CLI lives at `packages/<pkg>/src/cli.ts`** — the seed is a sub-command of `packages/db/src/cli.ts` (0C), the importer CLI is `packages/importer/src/cli.ts` (9A). No plan widens the override. **The one admitted escape (0C):** the Cloudflare Workers runtime has no `process.stdout`, so `apps/edge/src/log.ts` carries a single inline `// oxlint-disable-next-line no-console` with its reason on the line. An inline disable with a reason is the only form permitted; a second config override glob is not.

### 3.3 The never / always lists (spec §0.2) and the binding union with the §3.8 linter

**Never**, verbatim (spec:97–104): "**Never**, at any phase, for any reason: write to a ledger or movement table outside the posting service; represent money as a float, anywhere, including in TypeScript; build SQL by string concatenation (SAH-036/037/069); issue DDL from application code (SAH-053); disable an invariant, constraint or trigger "temporarily" (SAH-027, 041, 053); gate an audit write on any flag (SAH-030); hard-code a package version into a source file — the lockfile owns versions."

**Always**, verbatim (spec:106): "**Always**, for every new table: `tenant_id`, an RLS policy, `created_at`, a migration, and a test that a second tenant cannot see it. For every new endpoint: Zod schema, OpenAPI entry, idempotency on unsafe methods, and a tenant-isolation test. For every UI screen: verified in both text directions before merge."

**Binding form for a new table = the union of spec:106 and the linter rules of spec:1370 as Plan 0A implements them (plan0A:2599–2671):** `tenant_id`; RLS enabled **and forced**; a policy named exactly `tenant_isolation`; `id uuid primary key default uuidv7()` unless the table is a join/counter table listed in `NO_ID_TABLES`; `created_at timestamptz not null default now()` unless listed in `NO_CREATED_AT_TABLES`; an `audit_row` trigger unless listed in `AUDIT_EXEMPT`; `stamp_<col>` for every `*_by` column; composite FKs `(tenant_id, <parent>_id)` to every tenant-scoped parent; a migration with a hand-written down; a two-tenant test. The exemptions are exactly the set memberships pre-declared in §3.5.3 — a plan that needs a new exemption changes this document first.

**The `*_by` naming rule (convention, not in spec; forced by the 0A linter).** A column name ending `_by` means *"the acting principal, stamped by the server"* and nothing else. The `stamp_actor` rule fires on **every** such column that lacks a `stamp_<col>` trigger (plan0A:2755–2758) and has no exemption set, and §3.5.2 requires zero violations — so a `*_by` column without the trigger cannot ship, and with the trigger it is overwritten by `app.current_actor()` on insert (plan0A:2373–2376). A column that records *whom an action is attributed to* — a cashier on a terminal-synced shift, a supervisor on an override — is therefore **never** named `*_by`: it is `<role>_principal_id` (`opened_principal_id`, `closed_principal_id`, `cashier_principal_id`, `supervisor_principal_id`) or, on `document`/`document_event`, the existing `attributed_to`. Naming it `*_by` would either fail the linter or silently replace the attributed person with the acting one, which is SAH-044 in the opposite direction.

Additional interpretations frozen here: `sql.unsafe` is permitted in **three places in `src/`, plus Plan 0A's two test-tier `roles.sql` loaders — five homes in all (corrected in round 4; the "exactly three" this sentence used to claim was already false in the tree Plan 0A shipped)**. The three in `src/`: the migration runner (plan0A:19), the pg-boss transactional-enqueue adapter (§4.2.6, which forwards pg-boss's own parameterised statement with bound values) and the importer's Firebird reader (which never touches Postgres through it). The two in the test tier: **`packages/db/test/harness.ts` (plan0A:476) and `packages/db/test/roles.test.ts` (plan0A:553)**, each applying `packages/db/roles.sql` with `admin.unsafe(readFileSync(ROLES_SQL, "utf8"))` — a checked-in `.sql` file read from disk, the identical case to `migrate.ts`. Plan 0A is immovable, so both are on `no-sql-concat`'s `UNSAFE_ALLOW` (0B Task 12) with the reason on the line, and `harness.ts` is in `sah-036`'s allowed subset so the two lists agree. Every other statement is a `postgres.js` tagged template or a Drizzle query.

Rules: a slice writes only inside its range and never renumbers; unused numbers stay unused (gaps are fine — `discover()` sorts whatever exists); a slice that needs more numbers amends this table. The runner (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, plan0A:698–766) applies every unapplied file in version order, so a range from a later phase may be applied before an earlier one's during parallel execution (Phase 8 alongside 5–7); no plan may assume `max(version)` equals its own last number. Production is forward-only (spec:2057); `down` exists for CI and local development.

**⚠️ PROPOSAL, not settled text — a remediation branch is not a slice, and this table has no row for one.** Every rule above addresses a *slice*: "a slice writes only inside its range", "a slice that needs more numbers amends this table". The phase-0 review remediation branch (PR #3) is not a slice — no card in §2, no Delivers list, no range — and it shipped three migrations. **0008 was legitimate**: inside 0D's range, labelled *spare*, therefore available, and the 0D card now records the occupant rather than changing an allocation. **0009 and 0010 were not.** They were 0C's and 0E's *reserved* numbers, and "unused numbers stay unused (gaps are fine)" is precisely what a reserved number is. The collision has one cause: a branch with no range of its own took the numbers that looked free. **Nothing is broken today** — both slices are complete and neither will add a migration — but the hole stays open for the next review-fix branch, and by then the slice whose reserved number it takes may be unwritten rather than finished.

**The rule this document should adopt, for the owner to approve or replace.** A branch that is not a slice — a remediation, a review fix, a security patch — takes a migration number the way an overrunning slice does: **it amends this table first, in the same PR, allocating from the tail and naming the branch that owns the number.** The tail is **0105 onward**: 0001–0104 are all allocated above, so "take the next free number" has no referent below that, and a branch that reads the rule as licence to grab an unwritten slice's number has misread it. It may take a slice's number only where that number is labelled *spare*; it never takes one labelled *reserved*, which is a slice's standing declaration that it may still need one. Applying a tail number before the ranges beneath it exist is already admitted by the Rules paragraph above — the runner applies whatever is unapplied in version order and no plan may assume `max(version)` is its own last number — so the only constraint on a tail-allocated file is the ordinary one: it may depend on nothing that has not been applied. **§3.9 needs the same rule for ADR numbers**, and for the same reason: ADR 0020 was the last unused number in 0E's range and the same branch spent it.

**What this branch should have done, recorded so the precedent is in the register and not only in a commit message:** 0008 as it did, and **0105** and **0106** in place of 0009 and 0010, allocated by an amendment here. It did not. The three migrations are committed and applied — `packages/db/test/migrations.test.ts` rolls back to 0007 and replays, which now carries all three files and compares constraints, columns, indexes, policies and triggers across the round trip, **locally**, since `@dulja/db` is one of the four workspaces `.github/workflows/ci.yml` cannot run on a Windows runner — and §3.4.1's own "never renumbers" forbids repairing it now. **The register changes; the files do not.**

#### 3.4.2 File names

Up file `packages/db/migrations/NNNN_<verb>_<noun>.sql` matching `/^(\d{4})_([a-z0-9_]+)\.sql$/` (plan0A:704 — lowercase letters, digits and underscores only; no hyphens, no capitals); down file `packages/db/migrations/NNNN.down.sql` in the same directory; `discover()` throws if the down is missing. Verbs used in this document: `create`, `alter`, `add`, `seed`, `grant`, `expand`, `contract`.

**Permission-seed file names (settled 2026-09-07).** The rule is `NNNN_seed_permission_phase<slice id, lower-cased>.sql` — the slice id **including its letter**: `phase1b`, `phase2a`, `phase2b`, `phase3a` … `phase8d`. This is what every card in §2 except two already says, what §3.6.3 requires, and what the written 1B plan ships (`0015_seed_permission_phase1b.sql`). **Two grandfathered literals, and no others:** 0B ships `0002_seed_permission_phase0.sql` and 1A ships `0014_seed_permission_phase1.sql` — those two plans are written against those exact names, in their file trees, their tasks, their commit steps and 0E's consumed-interfaces list, so the names stand. Every one of the remaining twenty-four slices uses the rule with its letter; a slice that finds itself wanting a letterless name has misread this paragraph.

**A file whose name understates what it does is renamed, not left (round 2).** §3.4.2's rule that the name says what the file does binds the *card's expected name* as well: where a card guessed a short name and the written plan found the file had to carry a second thing, the longer name wins. Two settled instances: 2A's **`0018_alter_document_party_fk_and_document_type_module.sql`** (the `document.party_id` FK and the `document_type` additions) and 2B's **`0023_grant_document_draft_delete_and_add_series_gaps.sql`** (the DELETE grant, both draft-only guards, and `app.series_gaps`). Both cards in §2.3 now state the long name. **Round 7 adds 4A's `0045_alter_party_and_document_add_credit_terms.sql`** under the same rule (3A's `0031`, round 4, is another): the card guessed `0045_alter_party_add_credit_control.sql`, and the file also adds `document.payment_term_id` and creates `app.assert_credit_available()`; the §2.5 card states the long name.

#### 3.4.3 What one migration file may do

Each file runs whole in **one transaction** (`tx.unsafe(fileContents)` then the ledger insert — plan0A:735–747). Consequences: no `create index concurrently`, no `vacuum`, no `create database`; DDL and data changes may be mixed. **One migration per PR** (spec:2057) — a slice with four migrations is at least four PRs. Every statement carries a comment naming the SAH-/spec reference it serves (plan0A style, plan0A:89, 974). SQL keywords lowercase; section banners `-- ── N. title ───`.

#### 3.4.4 Enum extension gotcha (binding)

`alter type … add value` is legal in a transaction but **the new label cannot be referenced until that transaction commits**; because a file is one transaction, a migration that adds a label to `app.document_status`, `app.principal_kind`, `app.period_status` or `app.account_type` **and** uses it (default, CHECK, insert) in the same file fails under this runner (derived from plan0A:741). Rule: add the label in migration N, first use it in migration N+1 — or model the vocabulary as a `text` + `CHECK` column (§3.2 Enumerations). No slice in this document adds an enum label.

#### 3.4.5 Down files

Every object the up file creates has a drop, in reverse dependency order, except extensions (plan0A:1058–1059, 2581). `drop function … cascade` is the accepted way to remove that function's triggers (plan0A:1518). `alter default privileges … revoke` precedes any `drop schema` (plan0A:2574–2576). `app_meta` and `app_meta.schema_migration` are never dropped (they belong to the runner). A down file that creates a schema outside `app` (`pgboss`, 0D) drops it with `cascade`. After `down(sql, dir)` to 0 there must be zero tables in schema `app` (plan0A:2505–2506) — so a later migration that adds a column to a 0001 table drops **only that column** in its down, never the table.

**A permission-seed down file cannot remove the role grants it orphans, and that is a property of the schema rather than an omission (recorded once, round 3; it applies to every `NNNN_seed_permission_phase<slice>.sql` from 0B onward).** Three facts, each verifiable: (1) `app.role_permission.permission_code references app.permission(code)` has **no** `on delete` action (plan0A:1325 — the default is `NO ACTION`) and referential-integrity checks bypass RLS, so on a database where a grant names one of the deleted codes the `delete from app.permission` raises SQLSTATE 23503; (2) the grants cannot be deleted from the migration either — `app.role_permission` carries `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` through `app_meta.enable_tenant_rls`, which forces RLS **for the table owner too**, and §3.4.8's consequence is that "a migration file with no `set_config` sees zero tenants and cannot write them", so a `delete from app.role_permission` there would silently affect **zero** rows; (3) nor can the file discover the tenants to set a context *for* — `app.tenant` is itself forced with `using (id = app.current_tenant())` (plan0A:980–981), so the migrator enumerating it sees nothing. **The rollback therefore carries a precondition instead of a workaround: a permission-seed down is reversible only against an unseeded database** — which is exactly where §3.4.6's generalised reversibility test exercises every down file — and on a database where `bun run seed --tenant <id> --only roles` has run, the operator removes the grants per tenant first (a seed-tier act, with `set_config('app.tenant_id', …)`) and **re-runs `--only roles` after re-migrating**. The task that ships such a migration states the precondition on its rollback command. **Never "fix" this by disabling or dropping the policy, temporarily or otherwise** — that is forbidden outright (SAH-027, SAH-041, SAH-053) and is a review-blocking finding. 6A's `0062.down.sql` (eleven codes) and 6B's `0063.down.sql` (three) are the two written instances; both say so in the file.

#### 3.4.6 Generalising Plan 0A's reversibility test (0B Task 1 — exact text)

`packages/db/test/privileges.test.ts` (plan0A:2502–2509) hard-codes `[1]`. 0B replaces that test body with:

```ts
  it("up → down → up reproduces the schema byte for byte (task 0.3 acceptance; §3.9 'reversible')", async () => {
    const before = await schemaFingerprint(db.admin);
    const applied = await listApplied(db.migrator);                       // ascending: [1, 2, …]
    expect(await down(db.migrator, MIGRATIONS_DIR)).toEqual([...applied].reverse());
    const [n] = await db.admin<{ n: number }[]>`select count(*)::int as n from information_schema.tables where table_schema = 'app'`;
    expect(n!.n).toBe(0);
    expect(await up(db.migrator, MIGRATIONS_DIR)).toEqual(applied);
    expect(await schemaFingerprint(db.admin)).toBe(before);
  });
```

and extends `schemaFingerprint` (plan0A:2445–2456) with two further catalog queries so a down that forgets an enum label or a grant fails the test: `select t.typname, e.enumlabel, e.enumsortorder from pg_enum e join pg_type t on t.oid = e.enumtypid where t.typnamespace = 'app'::regnamespace order by 1, 3` and `select table_name, privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where grantee = 'app_rw' and table_schema = 'app' order by 1, 2`. `listApplied` is imported from `../src/migrate` (already exported — plan0A:2802).

#### 3.4.7 Expand/contract and live tables

Any change to a table that holds production rows is two PRs: **expand** (add nullable column / new table / new index) and **contract** (drop the old column) in a later slice, never one file (spec:2057, 2236). 2C demonstrates it on `document` (test 25). Renaming a column is forbidden; add-and-backfill instead.

#### 3.4.8 Migrations versus seed-pack data (convention, not in spec)

**Global rows** (`app.permission`) are migration data (hand-written `insert … on conflict (code) do update set module = excluded.module, mutating = excluded.mutating, description = excluded.description`). **Per-tenant rows** (`role`, `role_permission`, `document_type`, `posting_policy`, `print_template`, `report_definition`, `tax_code`, `statutory_rate_table`, `pay_component`, chart of accounts) are **seed-pack data**: `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` applies to `app_migrator` too (spec:1366), so a migration file with no `set_config` sees zero tenants and cannot write them. They live as JSON under `packages/db/seed/<pack>/…`, are applied per tenant by `bun run seed --tenant <tenant_id> [--only <sub-pack>]` (idempotent, `on conflict do nothing` on the natural key — spec:2002), and re-applying the seed against staging after deploy is a release-runbook step. The "reviewed diff" the spec wants for role permissions (spec:2152) is the diff of `packages/db/seed/roles.ts`.

Two rules follow from the pack being applied more than once, in more than one phase:

- **A sub-pack whose owning slice is later than the pack's first application is not in the pack until that slice ships**, and that slice applies it with `bun run seed --tenant <id> --only <sub-pack>` as a task of its own. **The CLI's `--only` flag dispatches to one loader module per sub-pack (`packages/db/src/seed/<sub-pack>.ts`), and the slice that introduces a sub-pack ships its loader in the same PR** — 0C builds the CLI, the flag and the `chart-of-accounts` and `fiscal-periods` loaders; **1A ships the `document-types` loader** (with `packages/domain/document-type-seed.schema.json`, §4.3.7 — 0C cannot write a loader for an envelope whose policy schema does not exist yet); 2C `templates`, 5A `tax`, 7A `reports`, 8A `statutory`. A slice that adds rows to an existing sub-pack (every §4.15 contributor after 0C) adds a **file**, never a loader. **The Phase 0 loader names are exactly `roles`, `dimensions`, `fiscal-periods`, `chart-of-accounts`, in that application order** (`SUB_PACKS`, §4.2.13, 0C); `roles` is TypeScript data in `packages/db/seed/roles.ts` and has no directory under `my/`, the other three are sub-pack directories. A later slice's loader widens the `SubPack` union and the `SUB_PACKS` array additively and exposes a `PackLoader` (§4.2.13) — that is the shape the `--only` flag dispatches to. `packages/db/seed/my/` at Phase 0 is therefore `chart-of-accounts/` and fiscal periods and nothing else; `document-types/` arrives with 1A (JOURNAL), `templates/` with 2C, `tax/` with 5A, `reports/` with 7A/7B, `statutory/` only with OD-23. A slice never seeds a row into a table a later slice creates, and never seeds a policy naming a permission code its own slice has not introduced (F-21, §4.4.1).
- **A policy version is `on conflict … do update`, not `do nothing` — unless a posted document pins it.** `posting_policy` upserts on `(document_type_id, version)` and updates `definition` and `effective_from`; every other per-tenant row keeps `do nothing`. Without this a placeholder seeded on staging in an early phase would silently survive the real definition arriving later, and the phase's tests would pass locally and fail on staging. **Amended by the Phase 2 review pass (ADR 0087, migration 0106):** a version that a `document` or a `ledger_entry` already pins is what those rows were posted under (SAH-013, spec:1753) and never changes — the loader refuses the drift with a `SeedError` naming the fix (bump `policyVersion`), and the `posting_policy_pinned` trigger refuses any other path. The placeholder case is unchanged: nothing has posted under a placeholder.

#### 3.4.9 Drizzle (ADR-0002, plan0A:598–617)

Drizzle Kit is **not** installed by 0A. 0B adds `drizzle-orm` and `drizzle-kit` to `packages/db`, `packages/db/drizzle.config.ts`, and `packages/db/src/schema/<table>.ts` typed mirrors of the 0001 tables used for **reads** in `apps/api`; every slice that creates a table adds its mirror file in the same PR as the migration.

**The mirror is the diff source, exactly as ADR-0002 decided and spec:2057 requires.** ADR-0002 is titled "Apply SQL migrations with a 60-line runner; **keep Drizzle Kit as the diff generator**" and decides (plan0A:611–612): "Drizzle Kit stays in the toolchain for `drizzle-kit generate` schema diffs **from Phase 1 onward**; its output is committed as a numbered file and applied by this runner after human review, as §3.9 requires." spec:2057 says the same in one line: "Drizzle Kit generates the up; a human reads the SQL before merge." So the working loop for every slice from 1A on is: **edit the mirror → `drizzle-kit generate` → rename its output to `NNNN_<verb>_<noun>.sql` in this slice's range → hand-edit it** (every migration in this document mixes PL/pgSQL, `app_meta` procedure calls, policies and comments that no generator emits, so hand-editing is the norm, not the exception) → **hand-write `NNNN.down.sql`** → human review → merge. What ADR-0002 replaced is Drizzle's *applier* and its journal file, not its generator: the committed SQL file is what runs, and `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` is what runs it. Migration 0001 stays hand-written (plan0A). All writes on ledger/movement/projection tables are `postgres.js` tagged templates (D7 "raw SQL for posting/costing").

### 3.5 Extending the schema linter, audit/immutable/stamp attachments, privileges

#### 3.5.1 The new-table recipe (from Plan 0A, plan0A:1284–1296, 2523–2541)

1. `create table app.<name> (id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), <the table's own columns>, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), unique (tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, <parent>_id) references app.<parent>(tenant_id, id))`;
2. `call app_meta.enable_tenant_rls('app.<name>');`
3. `call app_meta.attach_audit('app.<name>'[, mode, key_cols]);` unless the table is in `AUDIT_EXEMPT` (then the plan adds it to that set in `packages/db/src/lint-schema.ts` in the same PR);
4. `call app_meta.attach_stamp('app.<name>', '<col>_by');` for every `*_by` column (and for `document_event.actor_id` — spec:1370);
5. if immutable: `create trigger <name>_immutable before update or delete on app.<name> for each row execute function app.forbid_change();` + `revoke update, delete on app.<name> from app_rw;` + add to `IMMUTABLE`;
6. `app_rw` receives `select, insert, update` through default privileges (plan0A:2564) — no grant statement; DELETE only per §3.5.4;
7. if the table has a branch key — **or is one of the five stock tables of §4.5.6 Form C; a `warehouse_id` on its own does not qualify** — and 6C's migration 0068 has landed, attach the matching **`branch_isolation` form of §4.5.6**: Form A for a NOT NULL `branch_id`, Form A″ for `warehouse` itself (Form A plus the in-transit exception), Form A′ for `home_branch_id`, **Form B** (`branch_id is null or app.actor_in_branch(…)`) for a *nullable* `branch_id`, where NULL means "every branch", Form C (`app.actor_in_warehouse(company_id, warehouse_id)`) for a warehouse-keyed stock table. Tables created before 0068 receive it in 0068, which names them explicitly: Form A `document`, `pos_terminal`, `pos_cashier`, `branch_pos_policy`, `attendance_event`, **`terminal_enrolment`, `needs_attention`**; **Form A″ `warehouse`** (Form A plus `kind = 'in_transit' or …`, without which no branch can dispatch into or receive from an in-transit warehouse — and Form C reads this table, so its exception must live here); Form A′ `employee` when 0064 ran first; Form B `price_list`, `promotion`, **`catalogue_tombstone`**; Form C `inventory_movement`, `stock_on_hand`, `cost_layer`, `stock_valuation`, and `cost_consumption` through its movement. **`document_line` never gains a branch key** (§4.3.4); its separate restrictive `document_parent_visibility` policy enforces visible parent `document` rows (§4.5.6);
8. Drizzle mirror file (§3.4.9); the two-tenant test; drops prepended to the down file.

#### 3.5.2 Linter rules and how a slice adds one

**6C amendment A2.** `BRANCH_ISOLATION_EXEMPT = new Set(["role_assignment_branch"])` is the closed exemption set for `branch_isolation_policy`. Branch grants must not recursively invoke their own branch predicate. The separately registered document-line parent-visibility guard also receives restrictive-policy linter coverage; it is not another exemption or branch form.

The rule catalogue after 0A is plan0A:2741–2778 (`tenant_id`, `rls_enabled`, `rls_forced`, `tenant_isolation_policy`, `id_column`, `created_at`, `extra_permissive_policy`, `stamp_actor`, `audit_trigger`, `immutable_privileges`, `immutable_trigger`, `composite_fk`). Rules added later, each with the slice that adds it and its exact `rule` string:

| Rule | Added by | Violation condition |
|---|---|---|
| `branch_isolation_policy` | 6C (with migration 0068) | a table in schema `app` that has a `branch_id` **or `home_branch_id`** column, **or is one of the five stock tables `inventory_movement`, `stock_on_hand`, `cost_layer`, `cost_consumption`, `stock_valuation`** (an explicit list, held in the rule as `BRANCH_ISOLATED_BY_WAREHOUSE`), has no policy named `branch_isolation`, or that policy is PERMISSIVE. `employee` keys its branch as `home_branch_id` (§4.6.2). The stock tables are named explicitly rather than keyed on `warehouse_id` because `document_line` also has a `warehouse_id` and must **not** carry the policy (§4.5.6) |
| `sensitive_gate` | 8A | `app.employee_sensitive` has no RESTRICTIVE policy named `sensitive_gate` |
| `relkind_partition` | 1B | the linter's and RLS test's `relkind = 'r'` filters become `relkind in ('r', 'p')` so a future partitioned `ledger_entry` (plan0A:2037) stays visible (plan0A:1718 gap) |

Every rule keeps the `Violation { table, rule, detail }` shape (plan0A:2610) and the shipped schema must report **zero** violations after every migration.

#### 3.5.4 `app_rw` DELETE grants (pinned list in `privileges.test.ts`, plan0A:2476–2485)

| After | DELETE held on | Granted by |
|---|---|---|
| 0001 | `idempotency_key`, `role_permission`, `role_assignment_branch` | 0A |
| 0023 | + `document`, `document_line` — guarded by `document_delete_draft_only` (BEFORE DELETE on `document`, `ERR_DOC_NOT_DRAFT` unless `status = 'draft'`) **and by `document_line_delete_draft_only` (BEFORE DELETE on `document_line`, executing `app.forbid_line_delete_unless_draft()`, same code)**; `document_line` also cascades from `document` | 2B |

**This list is complete for v1 — 2B is the only slice that extends it.** spec:2049 admits genuine deletion in exactly two cases, "for drafts and for the GDPR/PDPA erasure workflow, and both write an audit row first", and spec:1987–1988 pins the grants to `idempotency_key`, `role_permission`, `role_assignment_branch` (matched by plan0A:2476–2485). 2B's grant is the drafts case. Everything else — `saved_view` included — is archived with `archived_at` (§4.11.2). 7A adds no grant; it **re-asserts the pinned list** in `privileges.test.ts` and changes nothing else.

**The child needs its own guard, and 2B ships it (round 2, a correction).** The grant on `document_line` is what lets the draft-editing path replace lines; without a BEFORE DELETE trigger on the child, `app_rw` could delete a *posted* document's lines one row at a time and the parent's guard would never fire. `app.forbid_line_delete_unless_draft()` reads the parent's status and raises the same `ERR_DOC_NOT_DRAFT`; the cascade from `document` is unaffected, because a cascade fired by an already-admitted parent delete sees a draft parent.

Each granting slice updates the pinned expectation in `privileges.test.ts` to exactly the new list — after 0023 that list, in `order by table_name` order, is `["document", "document_line", "idempotency_key", "role_assignment_branch", "role_permission"]`. No other table ever grants DELETE; archival is `archived_at`.

### 3.6 Permission codes and role grants

#### 3.6.1 The catalogue module

`packages/contracts/permissions.ts` (the spec's literal path, spec:2135; plan0A:1311) with the shape in §4.2.5. Rules: codes match the DB CHECK `^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$` with `module` as the first segment (plan0A:1314–1318); `module ∈ admin | accounting | inventory | hr | pos` — **the `permission.module` CHECK is closed; no v1 slice adds a module** (report codes live under `accounting.report.*`, `pos.report.read`, `admin.data.export`). The action vocabulary is the spec's list (spec:2142) **plus** `assign`, `read_sensitive`, `verify`, `own`, `close_any`, which the spec's own catalogue uses (C2 resolution); `request` is in the list and unused. Each entry carries `phase` (the slice id that introduced it) so the build check can report "code introduced in 3A has no handler".

#### 3.6.2 Every permission code the spec names, by module and introducing slice

| Module | Slice | Codes | `mutating` |
|---|---|---|---|
| admin | 0B | `admin.user.manage` · `admin.role.manage` · `admin.role.assign` · `admin.company.manage` · `admin.audit_log.read` | all true except `admin.audit_log.read` |
