#### 3.6.3 Seeding and the build checks

- **`app.permission`** (global, no RLS, read-only for `app_rw` — plan0A:1254): each introducing slice ships `NNNN_seed_permission_phase<slice id, lower-cased>.sql` — the slice id **with its letter** (`phase1b`, `phase2a`, …), exactly as §3.4.2 settles it, with 0B's `0002_seed_permission_phase0.sql` and 1A's `0014_seed_permission_phase1.sql` as the two grandfathered literals — inserting its codes (`on conflict (code) do update`); the down deletes exactly those codes. A CI test in `packages/db/test/permission-catalogue.test.ts` (0B) asserts, after all migrations, that the set of `(code, module, mutating)` in `app.permission` equals the set exported by `permissions.ts` — both directions.
- The one exception is 8D's two ⚠️ hr.leave.* rows, which 0096 inserts so the whole OD-13 gate is one file and one task (A9). (8D, round 19; OD-13 answered **build** on 2026-11-07, so 0096 ships.)
- **Handler ↔ catalogue** (spec:2135; test 36): `scripts/lint/rules/permission-catalogue.ts` (0D) collects every `PERMISSION.<code>` / `requirePermission('<code>')` / `principalHas('<code>')` reference in `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, `apps/pos`, `packages/sync`, `packages/db/src` and fails the build if a catalogue code has no reference or a reference names no catalogue code. Codes evaluated only at the till (`pos.price.check`, `pos.shift.own`, `pos.attendance.clock`) are referenced in `apps/pos`.
- **R6 / R7** (spec:2177–2178): `scripts/lint/rules/role-seed.ts` (0D) reads `packages/db/seed/roles.ts` and fails when a seeded role other than `admin` holds both codes of any `INCOMPATIBLE_PAIRS` entry whose two codes are both present in the catalogue (a pair with an absent code is skipped — F-21), when `auditor` holds a code with `mutating = true`, or when a role holds a code not in the catalogue. `permission.mutating` is also enforced at route registration: a route whose method is unsafe cannot be gated by a `mutating = false` code (`ERR_ROUTE_GATE_READONLY` at boot) — **except** a gate marked `markWriteFreeGate` on a route `REPLAY_BY_RERUN` lists (§4.2.5, §4.2.9; 2C, recorded in round 10, ⚠️ awaiting the owner's review as a widening of this control), **and** `accounting.report.export` on a gate marked `markExportRequestGate` on a route `EXPORT_REQUEST_ROUTES` lists — today only `POST …/reports/{code}/runs` (7A Task 12, ADR 0067 decision 6, ⚠️ awaiting the owner's review as a widening of this control).

#### 3.6.4 Role grants (`packages/db/seed/roles.ts`)

Shape in §4.2.5. The nine roles are `admin`, `accountant`, `user`, `warehouse`, `branch_manager`, `cashier`, `hr_payroll`, `auditor`, `pos_terminal` (spec:2156–2164; OD-04). `admin` is computed: every catalogue code except `pos.ticket.sell` and every `pos.sync.*` (spec:2000, 2156). `pos_terminal` holds exactly `pos.sync.pull`, `pos.sync.push` and the role code is a fixed literal in `assert_assignment_kind` (plan0A:1416). Each introducing slice extends the `permissions` arrays for the roles the spec's table gives that authority (spec:2157–2163) in the same PR as its catalogue entries. **The grants recorded so far, so no slice has to re-derive one from the spec's table** (`admin`'s array is computed from `PERMISSIONS` and is never edited): **1A's seven (round 4, 1A amendment A7, landing with 1A Task 4)** — **`accounting.account.manage`, `accounting.ledger.read`, `accounting.period.close`, `accounting.journal.create`, `accounting.journal.post` → `accountant`** (spec:2157 — chart of accounts, journals and their posting, and period close; **not** period reopen), **`accounting.journal.create` → `user`** (spec:2158 — the clerk drafts and may not post; reading the chart needs membership only) and **`accounting.ledger.read` → `auditor`** (spec:2163, non-mutating only); **`accounting.period.reopen` is granted to no seeded role but `admin`**, which `adminPermissions(catalogue)` computes. Then **`accounting.report.read` → `accountant` and `auditor`** (1B; spec:2157 gives head office the bookkeeping surface and spec:2163 gives the auditor "ledger, documents, reports"; `mutating: false`, so R7 (spec:2178) holds; **not `user`**, whose spec:2158 row names no report, and **not `branch_manager`**, whose Z-report is 6D's `pos.report.read`) — landed in `packages/db/seed/roles.ts` by 1B Task 1 and recorded in this sentence only by round 10. Then **`accounting.party.manage` → `user`** (2A; spec:2159 gives the back-office clerk party maintenance) and **`accounting.document.reverse` → `accountant`** (2B). Then Phase 3's reads, both non-mutating so R7 (spec:2178) holds for every role that gets one: **`inventory.item.read` and `inventory.stock.read` → `accountant`, `user`, `warehouse`, `branch_manager`, `auditor`** (3A; spec:2157–2160 and 2163 — the catalogue and stock are read by head office, the clerk, the store, the branch and the auditor, and spec:2159 denies the store the item master and prices, so the store gets the two reads and nothing else) and **`inventory.cost.read` → `accountant`, `warehouse`, `branch_manager`, `auditor`** (3B — valuation and cost layers; **not `user`**, because the clerk has no costing authority in spec:2158). **Both sets were landed in `packages/db/seed/roles.ts` by 3A and 3B and recorded in this sentence only by 3C Task 0** — 3A has no Task 0 and 3B's had already shipped; the tree is the authority for what is granted and this sentence is the register that stops a later slice re-deriving it. Then — from 3C, all four derived from spec:2159 — **`accounting.purchase.create` → `accountant` and `user`**, **`accounting.purchase.post` → `accountant`**, **`inventory.receipt.create` → `warehouse`** and **`inventory.receipt.post` → `warehouse`**. 3C's own note on the two roles that get nothing: `accountant` does **not** receive `inventory.receipt.*` (spec:2159 gives receipt posting to the warehouse), and `branch_manager` receives neither pair — its "receiving transfers" is 3D's `inventory.transfer.*`. All four are `mutating`, so R7 (spec:2178) keeps every one of them off the auditor. Then — from 3D, derived from spec:2158–2160 — **`accounting.sales.create` → `user`**; **`inventory.transfer.create`, `inventory.transfer.post`, `inventory.count.create`, `inventory.adjustment.create` → `warehouse` and `branch_manager`**; **`inventory.adjustment.approve` → `accountant`** (3D). All six are `mutating`, so R7 (spec:2178) keeps every one of them off the auditor. Then — from 4A Task 2, derived from spec:2157–2158 — and **4A**: **`accounting.sales.post`, `accounting.receipt.create`, `accounting.receipt.post`, `accounting.payment.approve`, `accounting.payment.post`, `accounting.credit_limit.override` → `accountant`**, and **`accounting.receipt.create`, `accounting.payment.create` → `user`** (spec:2157–2158). **`accounting.payment.create` is deliberately NOT on `accountant`**: it is the first half of `INCOMPATIBLE_PAIRS`' `["accounting.payment.create", "accounting.payment.approve"]`, which `scripts/lint/rules/role-seed.ts` skips while either code is absent from the catalogue — so 4A Task 2 is the change that makes that pair live in CI, and adding the code to `accountant` fails `bun run lint:rules` by design. **`accounting.credit_limit.override` goes to no seeded role but `accountant`** (spec:2158 denies it to `user` in terms; spec:2159–2160 give `warehouse` and `branch_manager` no AR/AP authority), and `document_event_override_guard` (§4.5.3) still requires a principal other than the document's creator to record it. All seven are `mutating`, so R7 (spec:2178) keeps every one of them off the auditor. Then — from 4B Task 2, derived from spec:2157 ("bank reconciliation") — **`accounting.bank.reconcile` → `accountant`** (4B), and to no other seeded role but `admin`'s computed grant; it is `mutating`, so R7 (spec:2178) keeps it off the auditor. **`pos.ticket.sell`, `pos.ticket.discount`, `pos.ticket.return`, `pos.customer.create` → `cashier`**; **those four plus `pos.ticket.void`, `pos.ticket.return_blind`, `pos.ticket.override`, `pos.needs_attention.resolve` → `branch_manager`**; **`admin.terminal.manage` → `admin` only** (6A). `pos_terminal` keeps exactly `pos.sync.pull` and `pos.sync.push`, and 6A seeds no other role. The grants follow spec:2160–2161: branch managers override others' tickets as a second principal and resolve needs-attention; cashiers sell, discount within limits, return against an original and quick-create customers, and may not blind-return, void or override their own tickets. Then — from 6B Task 4, derived from spec:2160–2161 — **`pos.price.check`, `pos.shift.own`, `pos.attendance.clock` → `cashier` and `branch_manager`** (6B): the cashier prices, opens and closes its own shift and clocks in and out at the till, and the branch manager holds everything a cashier may. `pos.price.check` is non-mutating; neither role is `auditor`, so R7 (spec:2178) is untouched; and none of the three is a member of `INCOMPATIBLE_PAIRS`, so R6 cannot trip (`tests/invariants/phase-6b-pinned.test.ts` pins both arrays). Then — from 8D Task 8 (⚠️ OD-13 answered build, round 19 A14), derived from spec:2085 and spec:2162 — **`hr.leave.record` and `hr.leave.approve` → `hr_payroll`** (migration 0096): HR enters entitlements and records leave, and a principal other than the employee decides it; the officer holds both because R4 (spec:2175) refuses their OWN leave per row in the data layer, and `INCOMPATIBLE_PAIRS` is not extended (spec:2177's list is closed). Every later introducing slice adds its row to this sentence in the same PR.

The seed CLI (`bun run seed --tenant <id> --only roles`, 0C) applies the diff per tenant idempotently as the system principal (so `forbid_self_grant` and `keep_last_admin_*` hold); a release-runbook step re-runs it on staging and production after each phase deploy.

### 3.7 Tests

#### 3.7.1 Layout

| Location | Content | Created by |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/<pkg>/test/*.test.ts` | unit and DB-level tests of that package (Plan 0A style: one file per topic, `startDb()` per file) | each slice |
| `apps/api/test/routes/<module>/<resource>.test.ts` | route tests through `createApp()` with a Testcontainers DB | 0B onward |
| `tests/invariants/tenant-isolation.test.ts`, `ledger-balance.test.ts`, `projection-rebuild.test.ts`, `audit-chain.test.ts` | the suites spec:2059, 2375 names; run on every PR | 0B (tenant-isolation), 1B (the other three) |
| `tests/regression/sah-NNN.test.ts` | one file per Part I defect (§3.7.3) | first-touching slice |
| `tests/golden/<area>/<case>/input.json` + `expected.json` + `tests/golden/<area>.test.ts` | committed fixtures for costing (3B), tax (5A), payroll (8B, synthetic) | owning slice |
| `tests/staging/*.test.ts` | a **second Vitest project** in the `tests` workspace, run against a deployed URL and **skipped when `STAGING_BASE_URL` is unset** — only clauses that can be true of a deployed system belong here | 0C |
| `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` | Playwright against staging, both text directions (spec:2377) | 0E |

`tests/package.json`: `{ "name": "@dulja/tests", "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json", "test": "node ../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run", "test:e2e": "playwright test" } }`; `tests/vitest.config.ts` mirrors Plan 0A's (plan0A:428–437) with `include: ["invariants/**/*.test.ts", "regression/**/*.test.ts", "golden/**/*.test.ts"]`, `testTimeout: 60_000`, `hookTimeout: 180_000`, `fileParallelism: false`. Tests run under Node 24 via Vitest (D5); Bun runs everything else. Tests connect as `app_rw` / `app_migrator` through `startDb()` — never as superuser for behaviour under test (plan0A:389). Concurrency tests interleave two real connections (spec:2266) — `db.rw` opened twice with `max: 1` each.

#### 3.7.2 The tenant-isolation harness (test 12) and the bypass suite (test 11)

`tests/invariants/tenant-isolation.test.ts` (0B) iterates `ROUTES` (§4.2.7): for every registered route and every job name in `JOBS` (§4.2.6) it performs the route's canonical request as tenant A against rows owned by tenant B and asserts a 404/403 with zero rows touched (the RLS `with check` refusal surfaces as `ERR_RLS_DENIED`). Every slice that adds a route or job supplies its probe as an entry in `tests/invariants/probes.ts` keyed by the route's `path` (§4.2.7) — the harness fails the build if a `ROUTES` entry has no `PROBES` entry, or a `PROBES` key matches no route. The probe lives in the test tier, never on `RouteModule`, because `IsolationProbe` uses `Db`/`Seed` from `@dulja/db/test` and a production route module must not depend on Testcontainers (§3.1). `tests/invariants/auth-bypass.test.ts` (0B) attempts the bypass shapes: forged `X-Tenant-Id`/`X-Actor-Id` headers, JWT with `aal1`, expired JWT, wrong issuer, `sub` with no membership, `set_config` in a query parameter, a body field named `tenant_id` differing from the session, a `Idempotency-Key` replay across principals, direct `app_rw` writes without `set_config`.

#### 3.7.3 Regression files — ownership rule (convention, not in spec)

**Phase 6A verification exception (2026-10-09).** Earlier blanket assertions in SAH-033, SAH-047 and SAH-083 must account for explicitly registered Phase 6 additions without weakening their invariants. SAH-033 pins the sole enrolment-resolver exception to its exact table, SELECT operation, app_auth role and hash/expiry/redemption-bound security-definer function; all other extra permissive gates remain refused. SAH-047 verifies ticket permission codes at their registered apply-time principal_has gates rather than pretending each is an HTTP route gate. SAH-083 retains universal failure statuses for actual Problem responses; only the registered per-ticket and unsupported-message batch wrappers (`ERR_SYNC_TICKET_REJECTED`, `ERR_SYNC_MESSAGE_UNSUPPORTED`) have registry status 200, and the standalone Problem mapper must surface either as 422. Existing historical codes and assertions remain covered; each change gains positive checks for the narrow exception.

`spec:2059` requires one `tests/regression/sah-NNN.test.ts` per defect touched; forty-plus defects are touched by several slices. Rule: **the first slice in execution order that touches a defect creates the file** with `describe("SAH-NNN <Part I heading> — <slice id>", …)`; every later slice **appends** a `describe("… — <slice id>", …)` block to the same file and never edits an earlier block. Suffixed file names (`sah-009-pos.test.ts`) are forbidden. The catalogue cards in §2 list "creates" and "appends to" per slice; the defects reader's roll-up (input-defects §2.2) is the source.

**Two corollaries the cards depend on.**

- **A slice with no fixed position in execution order never "creates".** §6.3 lets **9A** run "any time after 0B", so "first in execution order" is undefined for it. 9A therefore **always appends, create-if-absent**: its task creates the file if it is not there and appends its `describe` block if it is, and its block asserts nothing about what other blocks exist. Because a `describe` block is order-independent, both orders produce the identical file. Every other slice has a fixed position and follows the plain rule.
- **A conditional defect's creator is named in advance**, so an owner decision landing does not leave an orphan append. The conditional files and their creators: **052, 056, 057** — 3A (OD-07, with `serial_unit`); **055** — 7B (OD-06, with the stock-ageing report); **086** — **6B** (D18, with the peripheral task); **024** — 1A, created immediately and marked `it.skip` with the reason until OD-27 answers Part VII #6. If the decision is *no* the file is never created and no slice appends to it, which is why the creator must be the slice that owns the conditional work rather than a later consumer.

**Plan 0A-proven defects (25):** 003, 012, 013, 021, 024 (partial), 026, 029, 030, 031, 032, 033, 034 (one-query), 035, 040, 041, 042, 044, 050, 051, 053, 070, 072, 073, 074, 080 have data-layer proof in `packages/db/test/` but no regression file. **0B creates the file for 24 of them** (026, 034, 035 as full files because 0B's identity and catalogue work touches them; the other 21 as thin files whose single `it` re-runs the minimal scenario through `@dulja/db`'s production `withTenant` — or, for linter/privilege facts, calls `lintSchema` / reads `information_schema` — and cites the 0A test by path); **1A creates `sah-024`** marked `it.skip` with the reason until OD-27 answers Part VII #6. 0B also creates sah-023, 045, 065, 071, 075, 087 — structural facts 0A fixed without a dedicated test (audit `seq`, restrictive policies, no dead trigger branch, tree via recursive CTE, object naming, clean-runner build). Later slices append.

**Conditional defects (created only when the owner decision lands), each with its named creator:** 052, 056, 057 (serials — OD-07, **3A creates**; 6A appends its two-terminal serial race), 055 (FIFO — OD-06, **3B creates** with the FIFO layer path; 7B appends the stock-ageing report), 086 (POS hardware — D18, **6B creates**), 024 (⚠️ spec:427 "Confirm before rating" — **1A creates** it marked `it.skip` with the reason until OD-27 answers Part VII #6). Tests 20 and 21 guard no SAH and test 15/39 guard root causes — their files are named for the test (`tests/invariants/` for 15 and 39 clauses, `tests/e2e/` for 20/21) not `sah-`.

#### 3.7.4 Golden fixtures

`tests/golden/<area>/<case>/input.json` is a document set in the `DocumentSnapshot` shape (§4.3.2); `expected.json` is the `PostingPlan` (costing, payroll) or the rendered return (tax) — byte-compared. A change to any formula shows as a diff in the expected file (spec:2264). Payroll fixtures use only `SYNTHETIC-TEST-v1` until OD-23 (§4.12.4).

#### 3.7.5 Custom lint rules (`scripts/lint/`)

`scripts/lint/run.ts` loads every `scripts/lint/rules/*.ts` (`export const rule: LintRule = { name, run(files: SourceFile[]): LintViolation[] }`), prints violations as `<file>:<line> <rule> <detail>` and exits 1 on any. **Its `ROOTS` are `["apps", "packages", "scripts"]`** — `tests/` is deliberately outside every lint root, which is what lets `tests/support/ledger.ts` (§4.17) write `ledger_entry` directly in a thin regression file; a slice that adds `tests` to `ROOTS` must put `tests/support/**` on `posting-only-tables`'s allow-list in the same PR. The `SourceFile`/`LintViolation`/`LintRule` types live in `scripts/lint/types.ts` (`SourceFile { path; text; lines }`, `LintViolation { file; line; rule; detail }`).

**`dependency-rule`'s two named-allowance sets — the mechanism, and every entry in it (round 4, 0B).** A rule that admits no exception would refuse imports this document itself mandates, so `scripts/lint/rules/dependency-rule.ts` carries two allowance sets, **each entry carrying its reason on the line**, and nothing wider than the entries below. A slice needing a third entry amends this paragraph in the same PR as the import.

- **`ALLOW`** — the cross-package **tier** check, keyed **`<file path>|<package root>`** (a named file, never a `packages/*/test/**` carve-out, so `packages/domain/test/**` reaching `@dulja/db` is still caught). One entry: **`packages/db/test/permission-catalogue.test.ts|@dulja/contracts`** — §3.6.3 freezes that path for the both-directions catalogue check while `packages/db`'s tier is `["@dulja/domain"]`, so the test this document mandates would otherwise be a lint violation on a Plan 0A-shaped tree 0B may not edit.
- **`ESCAPE_ALLOW`** — the **relative-path escape** check, keyed `{ from: <importing directory>, to: <target prefix>, why }`. `ALLOW` cannot serve it: it is keyed on a `@dulja/*` package root, and these imports are relative (`../../../../tests/…`). The entries are the one-way door §4.17.1 describes, and **both root prefixes are listed, because the register above §4.17.1's closing sentence puts `grantAdmin`/`problemOf`/`sharedApi`/`fullRegression` in `tests/support/api.ts` while `postJournal` is in `tests/invariants/support/post-journal.ts`**: `apps/api/test/**` → `tests/invariants/support/` and → **`tests/support/`**; `apps/worker/test/**` → `tests/invariants/support/` and → **`tests/support/`**; and **`packages/db/test/**` → `tests/invariants/support/`** (3B amendment A21(c), for `postInventoryDocument`). The door is one-way and narrow: `apps/api/src/**` or any other production path reaching `tests/` is still a violation. The other half of the mechanism is one `include` entry in the consuming workspace's `tsconfig.json`, added by the slice whose test first makes the import; no `package.json` dependency is added in that direction (it would close a cycle in the workspace graph turbo walks).

**May a root `tests/**` file import `apps/api/test/support/app.ts`? Settled once, round 3, because two frozen plans read the question differently.** Three facts decide it. (a) **Mechanically it is not refused.** `dependency-rule` runs over the `ROOTS` above, so a file under `tests/` is outside every lint root and no rule inspects its imports — 6A's `tests/invariants/support/pos.ts` ships exactly such an import and is green. (b) **§3.1's tier table is the intent, and it is narrower**: the `tests` workspace reaches `@dulja/api` through its two entry points (`.` and `./routes`), never through a test-support file, and the one allowance §4.17.1 records runs the **other** way (`apps/*/test/**` → `tests/invariants/support/**`). (c) The two readings only ever collide over *what kind* of import it is. **The settlement:** a **type-only** `import type { StartedApi }` from that file is **permitted** — it is erased at compile time, creates no runtime coupling and no bundling edge, and 6A's `pos.ts`, 6C's `staff.ts` and 7C's `reports-7c.ts` all rely on it. A **value** import (`startApi` itself) from a `tests/**` file is **discouraged**, and its replacement is **0B's memoised `sharedApi()` in `tests/support/api.ts`** — the `tests` tier's own door to a running API — whose consumers **must not call `api.stop()` on it**, because it is shared. **If `ROOTS` is ever widened to include `tests`, every such value import is converted to `sharedApi()` in the same PR** (and `tests/support/**` joins `posting-only-tables`' allow-list, per the paragraph above). **6C's note is right and is not the side to fix**: its conclusion — that a test needing `startApi()` belongs in `apps/api/test/routes/`, which already holds the allowance it needs — is the shape every later slice should copy, and 7C followed it. 6C is wrong only if read as "the lint refuses it today"; it does not, and that is (a).

Rules and owners: `no-bare-db` (0B: in `apps/**` and `packages/**/src/**`, a tagged template whose tag is `db` or `sql`, or any member access on an identifier `db`, is a violation; only `tx` may tag SQL. **Both patterns admit an optional generic-argument list between the identifier — or the member name — and the backtick or call**, because every postgres.js query in this codebase is written ``sql<Row[]>`…` `` or ``db.admin<Row[]>`…` ``; a pattern demanding the backtick immediately after the identifier would match none of them and make spec:2053 a no-op. Allow-list — files: `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, `with-tenant.ts`, `client.ts`, `jobs/enqueue.ts`, **`packages/db/src/lint-schema.ts`** (Plan 0A's schema linter reads the catalogue with a `sql`-tagged template before any tenant exists); **`packages/db/src/sync/identity.ts`** (6A — calls the two SECURITY DEFINER doors that run before a tenant is known, `app.resolve_principal` for a terminal and `app.resolve_enrolment` for a one-time code, exactly as `with-tenant.ts` does), **`apps/api/src/routes/accounting/einvoice-transmissions.ts`** (5B — the two `SELF_TRANSACTED` cancel/poll handlers, round 12 amendment 13 and PR 11 review); directories: `packages/db/test/**`, **`apps/*/test/**`** (`apps/api/test/support/app.ts` legitimately constructs the pool it hands to `createApp`), **`scripts/lint/**`**); `no-sql-concat` (0B: `.unsafe(` with a non-literal argument outside the allow-list, or a `+`/template concatenation producing a string containing `select|insert|update|delete|where` — test 27); `dependency-rule` (0B: §3.1; 6A adds the tier `packages/sync` → `['@dulja/domain', '@dulja/contracts']`); `forbidden-log-fields` (0B: logger call object keys matching `/token|password|authorization|card|pin|secret/i`); `no-number-money` (0D: in `packages/domain`, `packages/contracts`, `apps/**`, a property, parameter or variable whose name matches `/amount|price|cost|debit|credit|total|balance|rate|tax|net|gross/i` typed `number` is a violation — `Money`, `Quantity`, `Decimal` or `string` required); `permission-catalogue` and `role-seed` (0D: §3.6.3); `posting-only-tables` (1A: an `insert`, `update`, `delete` or `merge` statement naming `app.ledger_entry`, `app.ledger_entry_dimension`, `app.inventory_movement`, `app.cost_layer`, `app.cost_consumption`, `app.account_balance`, `app.stock_on_hand`, `app.tax_transaction` or `app.employee_ytd` (added by 8C with the table) is allowed only in `packages/db/src/posting/**`, `packages/db/src/costing/**`, `packages/db/test/**` and **`scripts/lint/rules/**`** (the rule's own test fixtures contain the protected table names inside DML strings, and `scripts/` is inside the runner's `ROOTS`) — the mechanical half of the spec's "never write to a ledger or movement table outside the posting service"; the async projections `party_ageing`, `item_profitability` and `stock_valuation` are **not** in this list: they are rebuilt by their pg-boss jobs, not by the posting service); `error-codes` (0B: §4.2.4 — **its scan roots are `apps/**`, `packages/**/src/**`, `packages/db/migrations/**` and, from 8B's amendment A16, `packages/domain/payroll/**`**, the last because that directory is outside `src/` by design and holds the only raise of 8B's two codes).

### 3.8 Commits, PRs, AGENTS.md

Conventional commits with the scope = workspace or area (`feat(api)`, `feat(db)`, `feat(domain)`, `feat(worker)`, `feat(pos)`, `test(regression)`, `docs(adr)`, `chore(ci)`, `chore(seed)`), body optional, every commit ending with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>` (plan0A:28). Commit subject for a plan task: `<type>(<scope>): <summary> [<slice> T<n>]`, e.g. `feat(db): add account_balance MERGE [1A T5]`. One migration per PR (spec:2057); small PRs; the PR template of Plan 0A (plan0A:2868–2880) is unchanged and every PR ticks it; pushing to GitHub is the owner's call, not part of any task's definition of done (plan0A:2927). **ADR trigger:** any decision not in spec §0.3 gets an ADR (`docs/adr/NNNN-<kebab-slug>.md`, Plan 0A format plan0A:189–203); anything touching money semantics, security, the data model or the sync protocol is written **as a proposal and asked** before implementing (spec:95). **AGENTS.md:** the last task of every slice that completes a phase (0E, 1B, 2C, 3D, 4B, 5B, 6D, 7C, 8D, 9B) rewrites the "Current phase" section (plan0A:2828, 2901) — `CLAUDE.md`'s through 3D, `AGENTS.md`'s from 4B on, since ADR 0088 retired `CLAUDE.md` (§4.18 Round 6); 0B's last task rewrote it to name 0B, 0D, 0C, 0E.

**Amended 2026-11-17 (ADR 0088's amendment of that date):** `AGENTS.md`'s "Current phase" and "Current State" sections keep their names and now hold a short form. A phase-closing rewrite also rewrites that phase's entry in `docs/status/phase-history.md`, and the records that outlive a phase are in `docs/status/current-state.md`, which is part of "Current State". "Replace only that section" still means the `## Current phase` section and nothing else in the file.

### 3.10 The assumptions block every plan header must carry

Immediately after the writing-plans header (Goal / Architecture / Tech Stack / Spec) and before "Global Constraints", every plan carries this block, filled in:

```markdown
## Assumptions and contracts (from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-dulja-plan-contracts.md)
- **Slice:** <id> — <title>. **Phase:** <n>. **Phase gate:** this plan starts only when <predecessor slices> are merged and <phase n−1 DoD> is green in CI (spec:87).
- **Depends on (merged):** <slice ids and the Plan 0A helpers consumed, by exact name: e.g. `startDb`, `seedTenant`, `withTenant`, `lintSchema`, `app_meta.enable_tenant_rls`>.
- **Migration numbers:** <range> — files <names>. **ADR numbers:** <range>.
- **Interfaces consumed:** <§4 section numbers of the contracts document, e.g. §4.2.2 withTenant, §4.3.1 postDocument>.
- **Interfaces produced:** <§4 section numbers this plan implements verbatim>.
- **Owner decisions:** <OD-nn → Task N (isolated); default assumed>.
- **Part VI tests owned / re-run:** <numbers>. **§3.0.4 rows owned:** <spec lines>. **Regression files created / appended:** <sah-NNN lists — a conditional file names its creator per §3.7.3>.
- **Shared namespaces this slice writes into:** document-type codes (§4.14) <codes, each with its `module`>; account codes (§4.15) <codes seeded, and the codes consumed but seeded elsewhere, with the seeding slice>; report codes (§4.16.1) <codes> and `DatasetId` members (§4.16.2) <ids, or "none">; `fixtures.ts` helpers (§4.17) <helpers added> and shared test helpers (§4.17.1) <helpers added, or "none">. **A slice that writes a literal into any of these four and cannot name its row here has not read the register.**
- **Never re-decide:** D1–D27 (spec:114–142); every name in the contracts document is frozen — a needed change goes to that document first.
- **Contracts version:** 2026-09-07. (The six plans written against 2026-09-05 — 0B, 0D, 0C, 0E, 1A, 1B — keep that value; every plan written from now on carries 2026-09-07 and consumes §4.18's names, **both rounds**. The string is deliberately **not** bumped for round 2: 2A, 2B, 2C and 9A already cite 2026-09-07 in their headers, and a new value would stale all four the moment their amendments landed.)
```

## 4. Interface registry

Every shape below is frozen for all plans. Code blocks are the contract: a plan implements them **verbatim** (parameter names, types, return types, thrown error codes) and may add members only by amending this document. Items marked **convention (not in spec)** were invented here because the spec is silent; they are deliberately minimal.

**A named type with no body in this section is owned outright by the slice that implements the enclosing function, and needs no cross-plan agreement** — it appears only inside that slice's own files, so no second writer can spell it differently. There are exactly five, listed here so a reviewer can see they were left open deliberately: `CsvMapping` (§4.8.3, 4B), `TaxTransactionRow` (§4.9.1, 5A — the row shape of the §4.9.2 `tax_transaction` table), `OutboxRow` (§4.10.5, 6B — the local SQLite `outbox` row of §4.10.6), `LegacyPredicate` (§4.13.1, **9A** — 9B *consumes* it through `LegacyReader.read` and never redefines it), and `JobPayload[N]` (§4.2.6 — a type map each slice grows additively for its own job names). Every other named type in §4 has its body here, and a plan that finds one missing amends this document rather than inventing a shape.

### 4.1 The Plan 0A produced surface (immovable)

Everything below exists after Plan 0A and is cited by the exact names given. Plans **never rename** these.

**Package `@dulja/db` — public exports (plan0A:2802–2803, the final `packages/db/src/index.ts`):**

```ts
export { discover, down, listApplied, up, type Migration } from "./migrate";
export { AUDIT_EXEMPT, IMMUTABLE, lintSchema, type Violation } from "./lint-schema";
```

with `Migration = { version: number; name: string; upPath: string; downPath: string }`, `up(sql: Sql, dir: string): Promise<number[]>`, `down(sql: Sql, dir: string, toVersion = 0): Promise<number[]>`, `listApplied(sql: Sql): Promise<number[]>`, `discover(dir: string): Migration[]`, `lintSchema(sql: Sql): Promise<Violation[]>`, `Violation = { table: string; rule: string; detail: string }`, `AUDIT_EXEMPT: Set<string>`, `IMMUTABLE: Set<string>` (**plan0A:2694–2711** — the six linter sets; plan0A:1606–1632 is `fixtures.ts`/`documents.test.ts` and is not where they live). CLI `packages/db/src/cli.ts up | down [toVersion] | status | lint` on `DATABASE_URL_MIGRATOR`, exit 2 on config error, 1 on lint violations (plan0A:774–798, 2788–2797); package scripts `db:migrate`, `db:rollback`, `db:lint` (a `db:status` script is missing — 0B adds `"db:status": "bun run src/cli.ts status"`).

**Test harness `packages/db/test/harness.ts` (plan0A:443–510):** `MIGRATIONS_DIR: string`, `ROLES_SQL: string`, `type Role = "app_migrator" | "app_rw"`, `interface Db { container: StartedPostgreSqlContainer; admin: Sql; migrator: Sql; rw: Sql; url(role: Role): string; stop(): Promise<void> }`, `interface StartOptions { migrate?: boolean }`, `startDb(opts?: StartOptions): Promise<Db>`, `withTenant<T>(sql: Sql, tenantId: string, actorId: string, fn: (tx: Sql) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` (the **test** helper — keeps this 4-argument name and shape forever; the production helper is §4.2.2), `uuidv7(sql: Sql): Promise<string>`. Passwords `migrator-test` / `rw-test` are test-only.

**Fixtures `packages/db/test/fixtures.ts` (plan0A:1563–1611):** `interface Seed { tenant; system; human; company; period; closedPeriod; lockedPeriod; cash; sales; docType; policy; branchType; hq }` (all `string`), `seedTenant(db: Db, name: string): Promise<Seed>`, `draftDocument(db: Db, s: Seed, opts?: { effectiveDate?: string; periodId?: string; clientRef?: string }): Promise<string>`. Seed constants later tests rely on: company `HQ` / `MYR`; periods 2026-01 open, 2026-02 closed, 2026-03 locked; accounts `1000 Cash` (asset), `4000 Sales` (income); dimension type `BRANCH` with value `HQ`; document type `JOURNAL`; policy v1 effective 2026-01-01 with definition `{"version":1,"documentType":"JOURNAL","direction":"none","lines":[]}`; `draftDocument` uses series `'JV'`, effective date `2026-01-15`, actor `s.human` on `db.rw`. **`seedTenant` grants `s.human` no permission — it inserts no `role`, no `role_permission` and no `role_assignment` at all** (plan0A:1581–1600), so `app.actor_has(<any code>, s.company)` is false for `s.human` in a bare seed and every `requirePermission`-gated route returns 403. A route test therefore grants first: 0B's `grantAdmin()` (§4.17.1) is the one way to do it **from the `tests` tier**, and a slice that needs a narrower grant adds an option to that helper rather than hand-rolling the three inserts. **The one admitted exception, recorded in round 4 (1B amendment 7): a test under `apps/api/test/**` may declare a file-local grant helper** — plan0A:1195–1200's three inserts as `s.system` — because `grantAdmin()` lives in `tests/support/api.ts` and §3.7.5's `ESCAPE_ALLOW` is a door for `postJournal`-shaped helpers, not a reason for every route suite to reach across workspaces for three inserts. 0B's own `apps/api/test` files already do this and 1B's Task 10 `grantReportCodes` is the second; the helper is file-local, is never exported, and never appears in §4.17 or §4.17.1. (Pinned 2026-09-07; several slices were about to depend on the answer either way.) **Plans extend `fixtures.ts` additively** — new exported helpers in new tasks; existing helpers and constants are never changed (a JOURNAL policy v1 upgrade in 1A adds `seedTenantV2`/`JOURNAL_POLICY_V1` rather than editing `seedTenant`). `fixtures.ts` is a merge hotspot for parallel plans exactly as `lint-schema.ts` is, so **every post-0A helper is pre-declared with its owner and return type in §4.17** — a plan adds only the rows §4.17 assigns it, and amends §4.17 before adding any other.

**`schemaFingerprint(sql: Sql): Promise<string>`** exported from `packages/db/test/privileges.test.ts` (plan0A:2445–2456) — extended by 0B (§3.4.6). **`verifyChain(tx, tenantId)`** (plan0A:2153–2165) is the hash-recompute formula the integrity job reuses (§4.2.6). **`post(tx, s, docId, lines, periodId?)`** in `ledger.test.ts` (plan0A:1908–1923) shows the exact `ledger_entry` insert column list and `base_* = round(value::numeric * rate::numeric, 4)` the posting service must reproduce.

**Roles (plan0A:399–431, 529–550):** `app_migrator` (login, owns schema `app`, `timezone = UTC`, member of `app_auth` with `inherit false`), `app_rw` (login, no `BYPASSRLS`, `timezone = UTC`, DELETE only on the §3.5.4 list, no TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER, cannot read `app_meta`, cannot create objects in `app`), `app_auth` (`nologin`, `noinherit`, owns `resolve_principal` and, from migration 0060, `resolve_enrolment`). Connections are session mode / direct (5432), never the transaction-mode pooler (6543).

**Session settings and functions:** `set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true)`, `set_config('app.actor_id', $2, true)`; `app.current_tenant() returns uuid`, `app.current_actor() returns uuid`; `app.resolve_principal(p_auth_subject text) returns table (principal_id uuid, tenant_id uuid, kind app.principal_kind)` (SECURITY DEFINER, owner `app_auth`, EXECUTE for `app_rw` only, callable with no tenant set); `app.resolve_enrolment(p_code_hash bytea) returns table (enrolment_id uuid, tenant_id uuid, company_id uuid, branch_id uuid)` (0060 — SECURITY DEFINER, owner `app_auth`, EXECUTE for `app_rw` only, callable with no tenant set; returns zero rows for an unknown, expired or already-redeemed code). Terminal authentication needs no new function: `app.resolve_principal('terminal:<terminal_id>')` already answers it; `app.actor_has(p_code text, p_company_id uuid, p_branch_id uuid default null) returns boolean` (THE authorisation predicate, plan0A:985–1004 — NULL branch = company-wide, never fails open; system principal passes); `app.forbid_self_grant()`, `app.assert_assignment_kind()`, `app.keep_last_admin_assignment()`, `app.keep_last_admin_permission()`, `app.forbid_change()`, `app.assert_period_open()`, `app.assert_document_balanced()`, `app.audit_chain()`, `app.audit_row()`, `app.stamp_actor()` (semantics plan0A:965–980).

**Migration-only procedures (`app_meta`, plan0A:920–948):** `app_meta.enable_tenant_rls(tbl regclass)`; `app_meta.attach_audit(tbl regclass, mode text default 'tenant_column', key_cols text default '')` with modes `tenant_column | self_id | current_tenant`; `app_meta.attach_stamp(tbl regclass, col text)`. Trigger names the linter checks: `audit_row`, `stamp_<col>`, `*_immutable`.

**The 23 tables of migration 0001** (plan0A:1173–1568): `tenant`, `principal`, `membership`, `company`, `role`, `permission`, `role_permission`, `role_assignment`, `role_assignment_branch`, `fiscal_period`, `account`, `document_type`, `posting_policy`, `document_series`, `document_number_void`, `document`, `dimension_type`, `dimension_value`, `ledger_entry`, `ledger_entry_dimension`, `audit_log`, `pos_terminal`, `idempotency_key` — columns as §3.8 of the spec (spec:1387–1962) and input-plan0a §12; every parent carries `unique (tenant_id, id)`; plain FKs are allowed only to `tenant`, `principal`, `permission`. Enums: `principal_kind ('human','system','terminal')`, `period_status ('open','closed','locked')`, `account_type ('asset','liability','equity','income','expense')`, `document_status ('draft','submitted','approved','issued','void','posted','reversed')`.

**Error tokens raised by 0001** (all `errcode = 'check_violation'`, SQLSTATE 23514, message `TOKEN: text`): `ERR_RBAC_SELF_GRANT`, `ERR_RBAC_SELF_ESCALATION`, `ERR_RBAC_KIND`, `ERR_RBAC_LAST_ADMIN`, `ERR_TABLE_IMMUTABLE`, `ERR_PERIOD_NOT_OPEN`, `ERR_LEDGER_UNBALANCED`, `ERR_ACTOR_IMMUTABLE` (plan0A:1130–1141). Every later DB-raised token follows the same form.

**Fixed literals:** role code `pos_terminal` (plan0A:1416); permission code `admin.user.manage` (plan0A:1433, 1451); dimension type code `BRANCH`; `permission.module in ('admin','accounting','inventory','hr','pos')`; `principal.auth_subject` = Supabase `sub` | `'system:<tenant_id>'` | `'terminal:<terminal_id>'`; advisory lock `hashtextextended('tenant-serial:' || tenant_id::text, 0)` (audit chain; also the catalogue-revision lock — §4.10.2); advisory lock `hashtextextended('sync-batch:' || terminal_id::text, 0)` (6A — `applyBatch` takes it at the top of its transaction, serialising applies for one terminal before dedup on `document_company_id_client_ref_key`; distinct from `tenant-serial:` and `series:`. A transaction may hold `sync-batch:` then `tenant-serial:`, never the reverse); money `numeric(19,4)`, rates `numeric(19,8)`, quantities `numeric(19,6)`; idempotency TTL 24 hours; default company timezone `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`.

**Conventions every caller inherits:** insert a `principal` **without `RETURNING`** and its `membership` in the same transaction (plan0A:837); ids are pre-generated with `uuidv7(db.admin)` in tests; `admin` is for catalog assertions only.

### 4.2 The 0B / 0D surface that Phase 1+ consumes (frozen before 0B exists)

#### 4.2.1 `@dulja/domain` — `Money`, `Quantity`, `Rational`, rounding, exchange rates (0D)

Files: `packages/domain/src/money/money.ts`, `rounding.ts`, `quantity.ts`, `rational.ts`, `exchange-rate.ts`, re-exported from `packages/domain/src/index.ts`. Dependency: `decimal.js` only (D11). **Convention (not in spec)** for the API surface; the semantics are spec:2041–2043.

```ts
import Decimal from "decimal.js";

/** ISO 4217 code, upper case, exactly three letters. */
export type CurrencyCode = string & { readonly __brand: "CurrencyCode" };
/** `const` type parameter: currency("MYR") is `CurrencyCode & "MYR"`, not the wide brand — this is what makes
 *  `Money.of("1", currency("MYR")).add(Money.of("1", currency("USD")))` a **compile** error (spec:2041, 2319). */
export function currency<const S extends string>(code: S): CurrencyCode & S;   // throws ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_INVALID

/** The one rounding function (spec:2228). Symmetric across sign. */
export type RoundingMode = "HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO" | "HALF_EVEN" | "TOWARD_ZERO" | "AWAY_FROM_ZERO";
export function round(value: Decimal, scale: number, mode: RoundingMode): Decimal;

export const MONEY_SCALE = 4;        // numeric(19,4)
export const RATE_SCALE = 8;         // numeric(19,8)
export const QUANTITY_SCALE = 6;     // numeric(19,6)

/** Opaque, immutable, always at MONEY_SCALE. `C` is the currency literal when known at compile time. */
export class Money<C extends CurrencyCode = CurrencyCode> {
  private constructor(readonly currency: C, private readonly value: Decimal);
  static of<C extends CurrencyCode>(amount: string, currency: C): Money<C>;          // "1234.5000"; ERR_MONEY_SCALE if more than 4 dp
  static zero<C extends CurrencyCode>(currency: C): Money<C>;
  static fromDecimal<C extends CurrencyCode>(value: Decimal, currency: C, mode: RoundingMode): Money<C>;
  add(other: Money<C>): Money<C>;                    // same-currency only: a type error across literals, ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH at runtime
  subtract(other: Money<C>): Money<C>;
  negate(): Money<C>;
  multiply(factor: Decimal | Rational | string, mode: RoundingMode): Money<C>;   // explicit rounding, never implicit
  divide(divisor: Decimal | Rational | string, mode: RoundingMode): Money<C>;
  allocate(weights: readonly bigint[], mode: RoundingMode): Money<C>[];         // Σ result = this, largest-remainder residue to the first weight
  abs(): Money<C>;
  compare(other: Money<C>): -1 | 0 | 1;
  equals(other: Money<C>): boolean;
  isZero(): boolean; isNegative(): boolean; isPositive(): boolean;
  toDecimal(): Decimal;
  toString(): string;                                  // fixed 4 dp, e.g. "1234.5000" — the SQL literal
  toJSON(): { amount: string; currency: C };           // wire form (§4.2.8)
  static fromJSON(json: { amount: string; currency: string }): Money;
}
export class MoneyCurrencyMismatchError extends Error { readonly code: "ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH" }

/** Exact rational for unit conversions (spec:2043). */
export interface Rational { readonly numerator: bigint; readonly denominator: bigint }   // denominator > 0
export function rational(numerator: bigint, denominator: bigint): Rational;             // ERR_RATIONAL_ZERO_DENOMINATOR
export function rationalToDecimal(r: Rational, scale: number, mode: RoundingMode): Decimal;

/** Opaque quantity at QUANTITY_SCALE in the item's base unit. */
export class Quantity {
  static of(value: string): Quantity;                          // "12.000000"
  static zero(): Quantity;
  add(other: Quantity): Quantity; subtract(other: Quantity): Quantity; negate(): Quantity;
  multiply(factor: Rational | Decimal | string, mode: RoundingMode): Quantity;
  convert(conversion: Rational): Quantity;                    // exact; rounded HALF_EVEN to 6 dp only at the end
  compare(other: Quantity): -1 | 0 | 1; isZero(): boolean; isNegative(): boolean;
  toDecimal(): Decimal; toString(): string;                   // fixed 6 dp
  toJSON(): string;                                            // wire form: string
}

/** A rate quoted as 1 unit of `from` = `rate` units of `to`; `rate` has RATE_SCALE dp. */
export interface ExchangeRate {
  readonly from: CurrencyCode; readonly to: CurrencyCode;
  readonly rate: string;                  // "4.68000000"
  readonly effectiveFrom: string;         // YYYY-MM-DD
  readonly source: string;                // 'BNM 2026-09-04', 'manual:<actor_id>' (spec:1762)
}
/** base = round(value × rate, 4) — HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO, identical to Postgres numeric round() used by the ledger_entry CHECK (spec:1816). */
export function toBase(value: Money, rate: ExchangeRate): Money;   // ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH if value.currency ≠ rate.from
export const UNIT_RATE: (c: CurrencyCode) => ExchangeRate;         // rate "1.00000000", source 'unit'
```

Rules: no `number` in any signature above; `Money.multiply/divide` require an explicit `RoundingMode`; base conversion is always `HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` at scale 4 so the CHECK `base_debit = round(debit * exchange_rate, 4)` holds by construction; display rounding (currency policy) is a `packages/ui` concern and never persisted (spec:2041). Property tests (fast-check): `a.add(b).subtract(b).equals(a)` over 10⁶ cases; `allocate` sums exactly; `toBase` agrees with Postgres `round()` on a 10⁴-case table executed against Testcontainers.

**"Adding two currencies is a type error" (spec:2041, 2319) is proved at compile time**, not only by `ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH` at runtime. 0D's property-test task carries this exact assertion in `packages/domain/test/money.type.test.ts` as the DoD evidence, and `bun run typecheck` fails if it ever compiles:

```ts
const myr = Money.of("1.0000", currency("MYR"));
const usd = Money.of("1.0000", currency("USD"));
// @ts-expect-error — Money<CurrencyCode & "USD"> is not assignable to Money<CurrencyCode & "MYR"> (spec:2319)
myr.add(usd);
```

**`Quantity` has two documented conversion routes, and the difference is the rounding mode (3A).** `Quantity.convert(conversion)` above is exact and rounds **HALF_EVEN** at 6 dp; 3A's `applyConversion(unitQuantity: Quantity, conversion: Rational): Quantity` (`packages/domain/src/quantity/convert.ts`, re-exported from `@dulja/domain`, with `IDENTITY_CONVERSION` for `1/1`) is the **same arithmetic** — multiply first, divide second, one rounding at the end on a cloned precision-40 `Decimal` — at **`HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO`**. **A conversion whose result must agree with migration 0032's `app.document_line_base_quantity()` trigger goes through `applyConversion`; `convert`'s own HALF_EVEN is for display-side conversion only.** The trigger derives the base quantity as Postgres `round(new.unit_quantity * num::numeric / den::numeric, 6)`, which is half away from zero, and it **raises** rather than overwrites when a supplied `quantity` disagrees — so a caller that used the display route on a line destined for `document_line` gets `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED` on a legitimate line at a tie (`1.000000 × 1/2000000` is `0.000000` under HALF_EVEN and `0.000001` under the trigger). `applyConversion` is **not** `Quantity.multiply(conversion, "HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO")`: `multiply` divides before it multiplies, which is the per-step shape 0D's own `convert` docstring calls the SAH-066 defect, and the trigger multiplies first.

#### 4.2.2 `withTenant`, `TenantContext`, `createDb` (0B, `packages/db/src/`)

**Convention (not in spec)** for the shape; behaviour is spec:1368, 2053, 2315. Two helpers with the same name coexist by import path: the **production** one below is exported from `@dulja/db`; the **test** one keeps its 4-argument form in `packages/db/test/harness.ts` and is used only by `packages/db/test/*`. Root `tests/` and every app use the production one.

```ts
// packages/db/src/client.ts
import postgres, { type Sql } from "postgres";
export interface DbOptions { max?: number; debug?: (connection: number, query: string) => void }   // default max 4 — "one small pool per instance" (spec:1160); `debug` is postgres.js's own hook (0C, ADR 0013) — never a monkey-patch, and it never sees parameter values
/** Refuses a transaction-mode pooler URL: throws `PoolerUrlError` when the URL contains ':6543'. The URL is redacted in the message. */
export function createDb(url: string, opts?: DbOptions): Sql;
export class PoolerUrlError extends Error { readonly code: "ERR_DB_POOLER_URL" }   // named here so a test can `expect(...).toThrow(PoolerUrlError)`

// packages/db/src/with-tenant.ts
export interface TenantContext {
  readonly tenantId: string;      // uuid
  readonly actorId: string;       // uuid — the acting principal (a terminal for POS postings, the system principal for jobs)
  readonly requestId: string;     // uuidv7 minted by the request-id middleware or the job runner
}
export class TenantContextError extends Error { readonly code: "ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING" | "ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_NESTED" }   // one class, both codes — the nested case is the same misuse

/** The one door that runs BEFORE a tenant is known, so it cannot live in `apps/**` (the `no-bare-db` allow-list covers this file). */
export interface ResolvedPrincipal { readonly principalId: string; readonly tenantId: string; readonly kind: "human" | "system" | "terminal" }
export function resolvePrincipal(sql: Sql, authSubject: string): Promise<ResolvedPrincipal[]>;   // `select … from app.resolve_principal($1)`

/**
 * One transaction, explicitly `begin isolation level read committed` (the audit chain depends on it — spec:1368),
 * first statement `select set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true), set_config('app.actor_id', $2, true)`,
 * then `fn(tx)`. On SQLSTATE 40P01 (deadlock) or 40001 (serialisation failure) the whole transaction is retried
 * exactly once with a fresh `fn` invocation; a second failure propagates. Any other error propagates untouched.
 */
export async function withTenant<T>(sql: Sql, ctx: TenantContext, fn: (tx: Sql) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;

/** For jobs: resolves the tenant's system principal via app.resolve_principal('system:<tenantId>') and returns a context. */
export async function systemContext(sql: Sql, tenantId: string, requestId: string): Promise<TenantContext>;
```

The `no-bare-db` lint (§3.7.5) guarantees that every statement outside the allow-list is tagged by a `tx` obtained from `withTenant`. Nested `withTenant` calls are forbidden (a `tx` is passed down instead); `withTenant` detects a `tx` argument (a postgres.js reserved transaction) and throws `ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_NESTED`.

#### 4.2.3 Request context and the Hono environment (0B, `apps/api/src/`)

**6C amendment A3.** `AuthAdmin` adds `createUser(email: string): Promise<InvitedUser>`. The existing invitation method and `{ sub, email }` return stay unchanged. `StubAuthAdmin.createUser` uses the same deterministic subject as invitation. `SupabaseAuthAdmin` adds a `createPath` constructor option for the server-side admin-create endpoint, creating an email-confirmed user without sending an invitation or disclosing a password. Preserve existing production credential selection, request timeout, response validation and error handling; no browser credentials or new environment variable are introduced.

```ts
// packages/contracts/src/logger.ts — the one Logger type (apps/api, apps/worker and every handler signature use it)
export type LogFields = Record<string, unknown>;
export interface Logger {
  debug(fields: LogFields, msg: string): void;
  info(fields: LogFields, msg: string): void;
  warn(fields: LogFields, msg: string): void;
  error(fields: LogFields, msg: string): void;
  /** Returns a logger with these fields merged into every later call (the request logger presets tenant_id, actor_id, request_id, trace_id — spec:2063). */
  child(fields: LogFields): Logger;
}
// The implementation refuses (drops the key and emits one `forbidden_log_field` warn) any field name matching
// /token|password|authorization|card|pin|secret/i — the runtime twin of the `forbidden-log-fields` lint (§3.7.5).
export type LogLevel = "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error";
export const FORBIDDEN_LOG_FIELD: RegExp;     // = /token|password|authorization|card|pin|secret/i — the ONE spelling; no plan re-writes it
export function createLogger(opts?: { level?: LogLevel; sink?: (line: string) => void; base?: LogFields }): Logger;   // `sink` defaults to stdout; `child()` returns createLogger with merged `base`

// apps/api/src/config.ts — the reader of the §3.11 environment (0B). Every entrypoint calls it and exits 2 on ConfigError.
export interface ApiConfig {
  readonly appEnv: "dev" | "staging" | "production";
  readonly logLevel: LogLevel;
  readonly databaseUrl: string;
  readonly supabaseJwksUrl: string;
  readonly supabaseJwtIssuer: string;
  readonly supabaseJwtAudience: string;       // round 5: SUPABASE_JWT_AUDIENCE, default "authenticated" — a
                                              // default and not a required name, because the edge passes the
                                              // container a fixed variable list this is not on
  readonly supabaseUrl: string | null;        // round 5: both null where the identity provider is unreachable,
  readonly supabaseServiceRoleKey: string | null;   // read as null rather than "" so createAuthAdmin has one
                                              // thing to test before it refuses to start outside dev
  readonly terminalJwtSigningKey: string;    // 6A — TERMINAL_JWT_SIGNING_KEY, no default
  readonly port: number;                      // PORT, default 8080
}
export class ConfigError extends Error {}
export function readConfig(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): ApiConfig;   // throws ConfigError naming the variable and citing §3.11

// apps/api/src/ports.ts — the two seams apps/api declares and does not implement (0B), so the app builds in a test without Supabase
export interface VerifiedToken { readonly sub: string; readonly aal: "aal1" | "aal2" }
export type JwtVerifier = (token: string) => Promise<VerifiedToken>;
export interface InvitedUser { readonly sub: string; readonly email: string }
export interface AuthAdmin { inviteUser(email: string): Promise<InvitedUser>; createUser(email: string): Promise<InvitedUser> }
// apps/api/src/verifier.ts (0B)
export function createJwtVerifier(opts: { jwksUrl: string; issuer: string; audience: string }): JwtVerifier;              // production: createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(jwksUrl)) — the URL is never assembled from a project ref
export function createJwtVerifierWithKeys(opts: { keys: JWTVerifyGetKey; issuer: string; audience: string }): JwtVerifier;  // tests and any local key set
// `audience` is round 5's, on both: a token minted for another audience by the same issuer verified here until
// PR #3. The verify call also requires `exp` explicitly rather than trusting its absence to be caught later.
// apps/api/src/auth-admin.ts (0B)
export class SupabaseAuthAdmin implements AuthAdmin { constructor(opts: { url: string; serviceRoleKey: string; invitePath: string }) }
export class StubAuthAdmin implements AuthAdmin { constructor(seed?: string) }        // sub = `stub:${sha256(email)}`
// apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts (0B)
export const AAL1_PATHS: ReadonlySet<string>;   // EXACTLY { "/v1/session" } — the one concrete aal1 exemption (see below)
export function authenticate(deps: { db: Sql; verifier: JwtVerifier }): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
// packages/contracts/src/session.ts (0B)
export const SessionSchema: z.ZodObject<{ principalId; tenantId; principalKind; aal; displayName; email }>;

// apps/api/src/context.ts
import type { Sql } from "postgres";
import type { TenantContext } from "@dulja/db";
import type { Logger } from "@dulja/contracts";
export interface RequestContext extends TenantContext { readonly principalKind: "human" | "system" | "terminal"; readonly aal: "aal1" | "aal2" }
export type AppEnv = {
  Variables: {
    ctx: RequestContext;                                             // set by the identity middleware
    withTenant: <T>(fn: (tx: Sql) => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>;     // = withTenant(db, c.var.ctx, fn) — the spec's `withTenant(tx => …)` form (spec:1368)
    logger: Logger;                                                  // structured JSON, fields tenant_id, actor_id, request_id, trace_id preset (spec:2063)
    requestId: string;                                               // set by requestId, which runs BEFORE auth — a 401 problem still needs an id, and `ctx` does not exist yet
    traceId: string;
    // 2C — the two middlewares of §4.5.8 hand their resolved row to the handler rather than reading it twice.
    attachment: { row: AttachmentRow; module: DocumentTypeModule };  // set by requireAttachmentRead()
    documentModule: DocumentTypeModule;                              // set by requireDocumentModuleRead()
    jobs: JobClient;                                                 // 3B — set from deps.jobs
    db: Sql;                                                         // 5B — the raw pool, set from deps.db
    terminal: TerminalIdentity;                                      // 6A — terminalAuth; undefined elsewhere
  };
};
```

**The registered `Variables` set is ten members** (6A, reconciled with 5B). The five above are 0B's and 0C's; `attachment` and `documentModule` are 2C's, set by the two gate middlewares §4.5.8 and §4.5.9 describe so a handler never re-reads the row it was just authorised against. **The eighth is `jobs: JobClient` (3B amendment A5)** — set by a two-line middleware `createApp` runs in `apps/api/src/app.ts` from `deps.jobs` (`AppDeps.jobs`, §4.2.7), so a handler that must enqueue on the *same* transaction as its own insert reads `c.var.jobs` rather than reaching for a closure it does not have. 1A's post handler and 2B's `…/reverse` handler do not read it today; **3B's Task 7 edits both to pass `jobs: c.var.jobs` into `postDocument` / `reverseDocument`, whose input objects its amendments A5 and A15 give an optional `jobs?: JobClient` — those two signature members land with 3B and are not in §4.3.1 yet.** **7A Task 12's `POST …/reports/{code}/runs` and 7C Task 9's `POST …/exports` both read `c.var.jobs` and do not type-check without the `Variables` member, and neither slice adds a member of its own.** **The ninth, `db: Sql`, already landed with 5B** (round 12 amendment 13) and its existing `createApp` setter remains single. 6A moves that setter before `requestId`, so the pool is available even on a public request, and adds the public enrolment handler as the third registered call site after 5B's cancel and poll handlers (PR 11 review). Handlers with a tenant use `c.var.withTenant` except the two registered `SELF_TRANSACTED` e-invoice handlers; enrolment has no tenant context and uses the raw pool through the SECURITY DEFINER doors. The `no-bare-db` allow-list (§3.7.5) retains 5B's e-invoice allowance and admits `packages/db/src/sync/identity.ts` for those doors. **`jobs` is unchanged: no second declaration or setter. The tenth, `terminal: TerminalIdentity` (6A),** is set by `terminalAuth` on every `/v1/sync/*` terminal-authenticated request, so the handler and `requirePermission`'s `{ company: "terminal" }` branch consume the resolved row; it is undefined on every other route, including public enrolment. A slice adding an eleventh member amends this block first.

**The `aal1` exemption is exactly `{ GET /v1/session }`.** spec:2004 demands `aal2` on "every route except the MFA-enrolment routes", but no slice ships an enrolment route — enrolment happens in Supabase from 0E's shell — so `AAL1_PATHS` above is the concrete, testable exemption list and 0C's DoD clause (spec:2317) calls `GET /v1/session`. A slice that needs a second exempt path amends this document first.

Middleware order (fixed): the `db` pool setter (6A, reusing 5B's member) precedes `requestId`; **`otel`** (0C, ADR 0013 — `startActiveSpan` must wrap every later middleware; without an active span `setPrincipalAttributes` is a silent no-op) → `requestId` (header `X-Request-Id`, minted uuidv7 if absent, echoed on every response) → `logger` → `auth` (JWKS verify → `aal` check → `resolve_principal` → membership; MFA-enrolment routes accept `aal1`, everything else requires `aal2`) → `idempotency` (unsafe methods only, §4.2.9) → `requirePermission` (per route, §4.2.5) → handler. Terminal routes (`/v1/sync/*`) replace `auth` with `terminalAuth` (signed request → terminal JWT, §4.10.5) and set `principalKind = "terminal"`. Jobs build their context with `systemContext()`.

```ts
// apps/api/src/middleware/terminal-auth.ts (6A)
export interface TerminalIdentity {
  readonly terminalId: string; readonly tenantId: string; readonly companyId: string;
  readonly branchId: string; readonly principalId: string; readonly code: string | null;
}
```

`readConfig` throws `ConfigError` when `TERMINAL_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` is shorter than 32 characters; there is no default, because a default would be a shared secret in the repository.

#### 4.2.4 Error envelope and the `ERR_*` registry (0B, `packages/contracts/src/errors.ts`)

**6B amendment A6.** Allocate exactly four till-local rows: `ERR_TILL_PIN_INVALID` (401, failed PIN), `ERR_TILL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (422, local authority/limit refusal), `ERR_TILL_CATALOGUE_STALE` (409, no usable catalogue), `ERR_TILL_STORE_CORRUPT` (500, local integrity failure). The latter two land with the store; the former two with authority. Preserve server `ERR_POS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` separately.

RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with two extension members (**convention, not in spec**): `code` and `remedy`.

```ts
export interface Problem {
  type: `urn:dulja:error:${ErrCode}`;   // stable URN — no domain is invented
  title: string;                         // short, English, from the registry
  status: number;                        // HTTP status from the registry
  detail: string;                        // names the specific entity ("document 0192… is posted")
  instance: string;                      // request path
  code: ErrCode;                         // ERR_<DOMAIN>_<REASON>
  remedy: string;                        // what the caller can do
  requestId: string;
  errors?: { path: string; message: string }[];   // ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED and ERR_POLICY_INVALID — and no other code
}
// ERR_SYNC_TICKET_REJECTED and ERR_SYNC_MESSAGE_UNSUPPORTED status 200 describe wrappers within a batch result.
// If thrown as a standalone error, toProblem maps it to 422; no Problem response is a success.
export interface ErrorDef { status: number; title: string; remedy: string }
export const ERRORS = { /* every code below */ } as const satisfies Record<string, ErrorDef>;
export type ErrCode = keyof typeof ERRORS;
export class AppError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: ErrCode, readonly detail: string, readonly extra?: Partial<Problem> & { sqlstate?: string }) }
// `& { sqlstate?: string }` is 0B's, recorded in round 4: `fromDatabaseError` keeps the SQLSTATE for the log
// line while the wire `Problem` never carries it. It is the ONE widening of `extra`; a slice that wants a
// second member amends this line rather than widening it again at a call site.
/** Maps a postgres.js error to an AppError: SQLSTATE 23514 whose message starts with /^ERR_[A-Z_]+:/ → that code; 42501 → ERR_RLS_DENIED; 23505 → ERR_CONFLICT_UNIQUE; 23503 → ERR_CONFLICT_REFERENCE; the five class-22 states 22P02, 22007, 22008, 22009 and 22003 → ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED (amended round 5: a hand-crafted pagination cursor is base64url and unsigned, so it reaches a `::uuid`, `::timestamptz` or `::bigint` cast and raised an unmapped 500 — a bound value that will not parse is bad input, not a server defect. The detail is fixed text, never the driver's, which quotes the rejected value back — SAH-083. A slice adding a sixth state amends this line; 1A's numeric sums are the named place to revisit 22003); anything else → ERR_INTERNAL (logged with the SQLSTATE, never echoed). */
export function fromDatabaseError(e: unknown): AppError;
```

**The allocated code space — this document is the registry of record; `packages/contracts/src/errors.ts` is not a copy of it.** The table below reserves the name, status, title and raiser of every code the v1 system will ever raise, so two slices never invent two spellings for one condition. `ERRORS` in `errors.ts` contains **only the codes whose raiser has shipped**: each slice adds its rows in the same PR that raises them, and the `error-codes` build check (below) therefore stays green from 0B onward. A slice that needs a code absent from this table amends this table first. **0B's subset** — the rows `errors.ts` holds after 0B — is exactly: `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `ERR_AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID`, `ERR_AUTH_AAL_INSUFFICIENT`, `ERR_AUTH_NO_MEMBERSHIP`, `ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN`, `ERR_RLS_DENIED`, `ERR_RBAC_SELF_GRANT`, `ERR_RBAC_SELF_ESCALATION`, `ERR_RBAC_KIND`, `ERR_RBAC_LAST_ADMIN`, `ERR_ACTOR_IMMUTABLE`, `ERR_TABLE_IMMUTABLE`, `ERR_PERIOD_NOT_OPEN`, `ERR_LEDGER_UNBALANCED` (**these eight** — `ERR_RBAC_SELF_GRANT` through `ERR_LEDGER_UNBALANCED` — are the tokens migration 0001's SQL text raises, plan0A:1130–1141, so they count for the build check from 0B onward), `ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING`, `ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_NESTED`, `ERR_DB_POOLER_URL`, `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING`, `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`, `ERR_ROUTE_GATE_READONLY`, `ERR_CONFLICT_UNIQUE`, `ERR_CONFLICT_REFERENCE`, `ERR_NOT_FOUND`, `ERR_INTERNAL`. 0D adds `ERR_MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH`, `ERR_MONEY_SCALE`, `ERR_RATIONAL_ZERO_DENOMINATOR`, `ERR_RATE_NOT_FOUND`. 0C adds `ERR_RATE_LIMITED`. **Rows added by the round-2 slices:** **2A adds none** (it raises only codes already shipped); **2B adds four** — `ERR_SOD_NO_SUBMISSION`, `ERR_SOD_MAKER_IS_CHECKER`, `ERR_OVERRIDE_NOT_AUTHORISED` (raised as tokens by migrations 0021/0022) and `ERR_DOC_NOT_DRAFT` (0023), **each landing in the same commit as the migration whose SQL text raises it**, because `error-codes` scans `packages/db/migrations/**` too and must stay green at every commit; **2C adds `ERR_PRINT_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED`**; **9A adds `ERR_IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE`** — raised as a plain `Error` carrying the token by `unreadable()` in `packages/importer`, which has no HTTP surface and may not import `AppError` (§3.1), and the CLI maps the token to its own exit code. **Round 4 adds one row for 3A: `ERR_WAREHOUSE_TREE_CYCLE` (409), raised as a DB token by `app.warehouse_no_cycle()`** — the recursive-CTE guard of SAH-071 — **landing in `ERRORS` in the same commit as the migration whose SQL text raises it**, because `error-codes` scans `packages/db/migrations/**` and must stay green at every commit. It is not `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`: the request is well-formed and the refusal is a state conflict, and without the row `fromDatabaseError` has no `ERRORS[token]` to map, so the 409 would surface as an unmapped 500. **3A has no Task 0 and no gate script (§4.18 round 3), so nothing else lands it.** **4A adds two** — `ERR_CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (already allocated) and `ERR_CREDIT_HOLD`, both raised as tokens by migration 0045's trigger, each landing in the same commit as that migration. The two are deliberately distinct because the remedies differ — raise the limit or obtain a second principal's override, versus release the hold — and **`ERR_CREDIT_HOLD` is not overridable** (§4.8.1: "`party.credit_hold` blocks regardless").

Each slice that raises a new code adds it to this table first (one amendment PR) and to `ERRORS` in the PR that raises it. The build check (`scripts/lint/rules/error-codes.ts`, 0B) fails when a code **present in `ERRORS`** has no occurrence in `apps/**`, `packages/**/src/**`, `packages/db/migrations/**` or — from 8B onward (its amendment A16) — **`packages/domain/payroll/**`** (DB-raised tokens count through their SQL text) — spec:2051 "a code no code raises fails the build". **The fourth root is not optional and is not conditional.** `packages/domain/payroll/` sits deliberately *outside* `src/`, which is what makes spec:2366's "core never imports HR" mechanically checkable by `dependency-rule` (8B amendment A8), and it is the only place `ERR_PAYROLL_RATE_TABLE_UNVERIFIED` and `ERR_PAYROLL_INPUT_MISSING` are raised — the one occurrence inside an older root is a *comment*, and a check satisfied by a sentence dies the first time someone tidies it. 8B widens the rule's `ROOTS` in the same commit that adds those two `ERRORS` rows. It never reads this document, so an allocated-but-unshipped name costs nothing. **The scan excises the `ERRORS` object literal in `packages/contracts/src/errors.ts` from its own evidence** — that file is inside `packages/**/src/**`, so without the exclusion every code would trivially satisfy itself and spec:2051 would have no force. Only the literal is excised, not the file: a raise elsewhere in the same file (`fromDatabaseError`, the sole raiser of `ERR_RLS_DENIED`) still counts.

**`PostingError` (1A, `packages/db/src/posting/errors.ts`) is the one declared exception to "the posting service throws `AppError`".** `AppError` lives in `@dulja/contracts`, and 0B's `dependency-rule` lint pins `packages/db` to `['@dulja/domain']`, so `packages/db/src/posting/**` cannot import it:

```ts
export type PostingErrorCode =
  | "ERR_NOT_FOUND" | "ERR_DOC_STATUS_ILLEGAL" | "ERR_DOC_NO_LINES" | "ERR_POLICY_NOT_FOUND"
  | "ERR_POLICY_INVALID" | "ERR_POLICY_REQUIRES_MISSING" | "ERR_PERIOD_NOT_FOUND" | "ERR_PERIOD_NOT_OPEN"
  | "ERR_LEDGER_UNBALANCED" | "ERR_RATE_NOT_FOUND";            // a literal subset of ErrCode — never a new code
export class PostingError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: PostingErrorCode, readonly detail: string) }
```

**`PostingErrorCode`'s `ERR_RATE_NOT_FOUND` member (4B amendment 11, round 8) is a registry correction, not a new decision.** §4.3.8 already lists `ERR_RATE_NOT_FOUND` among the errors the posting service raises, and `ERRORS` has carried the row since **0D**, so the union stays a literal subset of `ErrCode` and 1A's `if (e instanceof PostingError) return new AppError(e.code, e.detail)` branch still type-checks **with no cast**. 1A declared nine members because Phase 1 had no rate-resolving code path inside `packages/db`; **4B is the first slice that does** — `revalueAtPeriodEnd` calls `app.rate_for` in `packages/db/src/ar-ap/fx.ts`, which may not import `@dulja/contracts` (§3.1) and so cannot raise `AppError` the way 0D's and 1A's *handlers* do. 4B's Task 5 makes the one-line edit to `packages/db/src/posting/errors.ts`; no second error class. **The tree's union is already wider than this block, and round 8 records that without re-litigating it:** 3B added `ERR_STOCK_INSUFFICIENT`, `ERR_COST_NEGATIVE` and `ERR_COST_VALUE_MISSING` (step 9's costing hook) and `ERR_INTERNAL` (step 14's fail-closed replay branch) to `packages/db/src/posting/errors.ts` without amending this block, so 4B's member is the **tenth here and the fourteenth in the tree**, and 5A's A4 (`ERR_TAX_REGIME_MISMATCH`) follows it.

**`errors[]` carries two codes, not one (2A amendment A10, a correction).** `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED` fills it from Zod. **`ERR_POLICY_INVALID` fills it too**, each entry a **JSON Pointer into the rejected policy definition** plus the validator's message — which is what §4.4.2's `PolicyValidation.errors` already produces and what the policy API must return, because SAH-078's own fix is "an invalid rule is refused at configuration time, **naming the JSON path**". `AppError`'s `extra?: Partial<Problem>` and `ProblemSchema`'s optional `errors` already permit it structurally; the member is now stated rather than contradicted by the comment. **No third code gains it** — a slice that wants one amends this paragraph. **`errors[]` is optional, not required**, which is what admits 3A's two database raisers of `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`: `app.pick_lots_fefo` (a non-positive quantity) and `app.document_line_base_quantity()` (three raises, on a supplied `quantity` disagreeing with the conversion, and on a missing or zero conversion) each raise the token in the `TOKEN: text` form and reach the wire through `fromDatabaseError` with **no `errors[]` array** — a `check_violation` has no JSON Pointer to report. Neither is a new code; both are new raisers for a shipped one.

`apps/api/src/problem.ts` gains **one** `asAppError` branch translating it, exactly as it already has one for `TenantContextError`; the wire `Problem` is unchanged, and §4.3.8's list is unchanged. `PolicyEvaluationError` (§4.4.2, `packages/domain`) reaches the same branch for the same reason.

#### 4.2.5 Permission catalogue module and `requirePermission` (0B)

```ts
// packages/contracts/permissions.ts  (the spec's path — spec:2135)
export type PermissionModule = "admin" | "accounting" | "inventory" | "hr" | "pos";
export type PermissionAction =
  | "read" | "manage" | "create" | "post" | "approve" | "reverse" | "close" | "reopen" | "override" | "export"
  | "reconcile" | "sell" | "discount" | "return" | "return_blind" | "void" | "prepare" | "pay" | "record" | "request"
  | "check" | "clock" | "manage_pin" | "resolve" | "pull" | "push" | "file" | "generate"
  | "assign" | "read_sensitive" | "verify" | "own" | "close_any";        // used by the spec's own catalogue (C2)
export type SliceId = "0B" | "0D" | "1A" | "1B" | "2A" | "2B" | "3A" | "3B" | "3C" | "3D" | "4A" | "4B" | "5A" | "5B" | "6A" | "6B" | "6C" | "6D" | "7A" | "7C" | "8A" | "8B" | "8C" | "8D";
export interface PermissionDef {
  readonly code: `${PermissionModule}.${string}.${PermissionAction}`;
  readonly module: PermissionModule;
  readonly mutating: boolean;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly phase: SliceId;                 // the slice that introduced the handler
}
export const PERMISSIONS = [ /* §3.6.2, grown additively per slice */ ] as const satisfies readonly PermissionDef[];
export type PermissionCode = (typeof PERMISSIONS)[number]["code"];
export const PERMISSION = Object.fromEntries(PERMISSIONS.map((p) => [p.code, p.code])) as { readonly [K in PermissionCode]: K };  // PERMISSION["accounting.journal.post"]
export function isMutating(code: PermissionCode): boolean;

// packages/db/seed/roles.ts  (spec:2368; R6 pairs live here — §4.2.2 of the spec says "the catalogue file names permission pairs", §5.2 places the list in roles.ts; §5.2 wins)
export interface RoleSeed { readonly code: string; readonly nameEn: string; readonly nameAr: string; readonly description: string; readonly permissions: readonly string[] }
export const ROLES: readonly RoleSeed[];                        // nine entries; `admin.permissions` is computed from PERMISSIONS
export const INCOMPATIBLE_PAIRS: readonly (readonly [string, string])[] = [
  ["accounting.payment.create", "accounting.payment.approve"],
  ["hr.payroll.prepare", "hr.payroll.approve"],
  ["hr.statutory_table.manage", "hr.statutory_table.verify"],
  ["hr.employee.read_sensitive", "pos.ticket.sell"],
];                                                              // spec:2177 — typed as strings so not-yet-present codes are legal (F-21)

// apps/api/src/middleware/require-permission.ts
export type ScopeSource =
  | { company: "path:companyId"; branch?: "body:branchId" | "query:branchId" | "document" }   // "document": the branch of the document named by path :documentId
  | { company: "body:companyId"; branch?: "body:branchId" }
  | { company: "terminal" }                                                                   // /v1/sync/*: from pos_terminal
  | { company: "any" };                                                                       // tenant-scoped routes that carry no company id (0B)
/** Pre-flight only (spec:2173): calls app.actor_has(code, company, branch) inside c.var.withTenant; 403 ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN. The data layer remains the control. */
export function requirePermission(code: PermissionCode, scope: ScopeSource): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
/** 2C (round 10, ⚠️ owner review — ADR 0087 decision 7): marks `handler` as a gate over READ codes on an UNSAFE method.
 *  assertRouteGates admits the mark only when the method is unsafe, `codes` is non-empty and REPLAY_BY_RERUN (§4.2.9)
 *  lists the route; anything else is ERR_ROUTE_GATE_READONLY. Two declarations of write-free, checked against each other at boot. */
export function markWriteFreeGate<H extends MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>>(handler: H, codes: readonly string[]): H;
/** Boot check for R7 (spec:2178): walks the mounted app and throws ERR_ROUTE_GATE_READONLY on either of two
 *  defects — an unsafe method gated by a `mutating: false` code, and (amended round 5) a route group carrying
 *  NO gate at all, which passed silently for the whole of Phase 0 and left seven GET routes bounded by RLS,
 *  which is tenant-wide and not company-wide. Both read the method+path *group*: one `openapi()` call becomes
 *  several `app.routes` entries and only one carries the gate symbol. Exemption is by declaration, never by path
 *  shape — a module opts out by declaring `auth: "public"` or no permissions — and `modules` is what a group is
 *  matched back to. (Round 10) a group marked `markWriteFreeGate` is exempt from the first defect only where
 *  `isReplayByRerunPath` also lists it. Called once from createApp, after ROUTES are mounted. */
export interface GatedModule { readonly path: string; readonly permissions: readonly PermissionCode[]; readonly auth: "human" | "terminal" | "public" }
export function assertRouteGates(app: OpenAPIHono<AppEnv>, modules?: readonly GatedModule[]): void;
```

**The fourth variant, `{ company: "any" }` (0B).** `app.actor_has` is company-keyed, but `/v1/admin/users`, `/v1/admin/roles`, `/v1/admin/audit-log` and `GET|POST /v1/companies` carry no company id. That variant evaluates `exists (select 1 from app.company c where app.actor_has($code, c.id))` — "holds this code in *some* company of the caller's tenant". It is not a bypass: the query runs inside `c.var.withTenant`, so RLS has already reduced `app.company` to the caller's tenant, and the handler's own reads and writes remain under RLS. Role **assignments** mount under a company (`role_assignment` carries `company_id`) and use `{ company: "path:companyId" }`; roles themselves do not, and use `{ company: "any" }`.
