**6C amendment A6.** `cashier_snapshot_drift` is the registered audit `table_name` sentinel for report-only snapshot differences; the comparison job does not repair rows.

**6C amendment A7.** The additive payload-map member is `"pos.cashier.compare": { companyId?: string }`; omission selects the whole tenant. The existing job registry name, owner and nightly schedule stay unchanged.

**6C worker placement reconciliation.** `cashierCompare` is exported from
`apps/worker/src/jobs/cashier-compare.ts`, the plan's location (PR 12 review, 2026-10-22: this row
earlier named `packages/db/src/jobs/cashier-compare.ts`, a file the tree never had). The existing worker
composition root `apps/worker/src/index.ts` registers it, and `apps/worker/test/support/worker.ts`
re-registers it after test registry resets, matching the existing handler pattern.
There is no `apps/worker/src/register.ts`; no second composition root is added.

**6C drift-audit writer reconciliation.** The worker does not receive INSERT on
`app.audit_log`, whose application grant remains SELECT-only. Migration 0067
ships `app.record_cashier_snapshot_drift(p_principal_id uuid, p_before jsonb,
p_after jsonb) returns bigint`: SECURITY DEFINER owned by app_migrator, fixed
`search_path = app, pg_temp`, PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked and app_rw EXECUTE granted.
It validates a system principal with membership in the current tenant and a
cashier keyed by the supplied principal in that same tenant. It inserts only the
fixed `cashier_snapshot_drift` audit `table_name` sentinel, action `update`,
current actor and tenant, supplied before/after images and cashier row ID, returning
the assigned audit sequence. The existing audit-chain trigger owns hashing. No
caller-selected action/table/tenant, protected-table grant, snapshot repair or
permissive policy is added. Handwritten down drops this function before its table.
Tests prove real worker drift reporting and chain integrity plus human, missing
cashier and cross-tenant refusals, exact owner/search_path/EXECUTE and unchanged
audit grants. The later general system-event writer remains unchanged.

**Who creates which of the three `packages/db/src/jobs/` files — settled (round 2), the same way §4.18 settled `payloads.ts`.** `createApp` cannot compile without `JobClient`, so **0B (Task 4) creates all three**, types only, with no pg-boss import and no `createJobClient`:

| File | Created by | Then | Round-2 correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs/names.ts` | **0B** — the complete, closed sixteen-name `JOBS` const below, verbatim, plus `JobName`. **Those two and nothing else** | **0D neither creates nor rewrites it.** 0D's task in this file is "verify `JOBS` is the sixteen names of §4.2.6 and `JobName` is `keyof typeof JOBS`" | **0d:1801 lists it under *Create* and 0d:1970 says "Write" — both must read *Modify (verify only)*.** Writing it a second time is how two spellings of a closed registry appear |
| `jobs/payloads.ts` | **0B** — a types-only stub, `export interface JobPayload { [name: string]: unknown }` | **0D replaces the body** with the registered `extends Record<JobName, unknown>` map. `JobPayload[N]` is `unknown` under both, so no 0B call site changes | none — 0d:1802 already says *Modify (replace)* and names 0B as the creator. This is the row round 1 settled, and the other two now follow it |
| `jobs/enqueue.ts` | **0B** — `JobEnvelope`, `EnqueueOptions`, `JobClient`, interfaces only | **0D modifies it**: adds `createJobClient(boss: PgBoss): JobClient`, the pg-boss import (its one `sql.unsafe` home, §3.3) **and `JOB_NAMES`** | **0d:1801 lists it under *Create* — it must read *Modify*.** A `Create` verb on a file 0B already wrote is how a plan silently drops the interfaces its predecessor shipped |

`packages/db/src/jobs/tenants.ts` is genuinely 0D's to create, and stays under *Create*.

**`JOB_NAMES` is 0D's, and it lives in `enqueue.ts` (settled, round 3).** The code block below groups it with `JOBS` for readability, and that grouping was read as a file assignment: it is not one. 0B's `names.ts` ships `JOBS` and `JobName` only (0b:1547–1568 — the block ends at `export type JobName`), and **0D declares `export const JOB_NAMES: readonly JobName[] = Object.keys(JOBS) as JobName[]` at the foot of `jobs/enqueue.ts`** (0d:2067) and re-exports it from the barrel in the same step (`export { createJobClient, JOB_NAMES, JOBS, … } from "./jobs/enqueue"`, 0d:2099). That is why §4.18 round 1 credits `JOB_NAMES` to 0D and not to 0B, and why the 0D verify-only rule for `names.ts` above is still exactly right — 0D adds no line to that file. `apps/worker/src/install.ts` and the job half of the isolation suite import `JOB_NAMES` from `@dulja/db`. **No plan changes.**

**Convention (not in spec).** pg-boss (D8) installs its own tables in schema `pgboss`; `app_rw` may not create objects, so migration `0004_create_pgboss_schema.sql` creates the schema and grants (`create schema pgboss; grant usage on schema pgboss to app_rw; alter default privileges for role app_migrator in schema pgboss grant select, insert, update, delete on tables to app_rw; alter default privileges for role app_migrator in schema pgboss grant usage, select on sequences to app_rw;`), and pg-boss's table installation runs **once per environment as `app_migrator`** in the deploy step `bun run --cwd apps/worker jobs:install` (the same class of tooling as the migration runner — not application code). At runtime pg-boss is constructed with `migrate: false`, `schema: "pgboss"`, on `DATABASE_URL`. 0D verifies the exact pg-boss option names for "run this insert on my transaction" and "do not migrate" against the installed version's documentation and records them in ADR 0007 — the wrapper below is what every other plan calls.

```ts
// packages/db/src/jobs/names.ts — every job name in the system; a name not listed here fails the build
export const JOBS = {
  "accounting.ledger.integrity_check": { schedule: "0 2 * * *", owner: "1B" },   // scaffolded in 0D
  "accounting.projection.rebuild":     { schedule: "0 3 * * *", owner: "4B" },   // party_ageing, item_profitability
  "inventory.projection.rebuild":      { schedule: "0 3 * * *", owner: "3B" },   // stock_valuation
  "accounting.period.month_end":       { schedule: "0 1 1 * *", owner: "1B" },
  "accounting.tax.submit":             { schedule: null,        owner: "5B" },
  "admin.idempotency_key.purge":       { schedule: "*/30 * * * *", owner: "0D" },
  "admin.export.run":                  { schedule: null,        owner: "7C" },
  "admin.import.run":                  { schedule: null,        owner: "9B" },   // 9B's loaders; async status at /v1/jobs/{jobId} (spec:2206)
  "inventory.cost.replay":             { schedule: null,        owner: "3B" },
  "inventory.lot.expiry_warning":      { schedule: "0 6 * * *", owner: "3A" },
  "pos.sync.apply":                    { schedule: null,        owner: "6A" },
  "pos.cashier.compare":               { schedule: "30 2 * * *", owner: "6C" },
  "reporting.render":                  { schedule: null,        owner: "7A" },
  "hr.employee_ytd.rebuild":           { schedule: "0 4 * * *", owner: "8C" },
  "hr.rate_table.lapse_warning":       { schedule: "0 7 * * *", owner: "8A" },
  "hr.encryption_key.rotate":          { schedule: null,        owner: "8D" },
} as const;
export type JobName = keyof typeof JOBS;
// `names.ts` ends here. JOB_NAMES is 0D's and is declared in enqueue.ts below — see the settlement above the block.

// packages/db/src/jobs/payloads.ts — the type map, grown additively per slice
export interface JobPayload extends Record<JobName, unknown> {
  /** Slice 1B. Omit both fields for the nightly whole-tenant run. */
  "accounting.ledger.integrity_check": { companyId?: string; sinceAuditSeq?: number };
  /** Slice 1B. `asOf` defaults to the run date; a period is due when `ends_on < asOf` and `status = 'open'`. */
  "accounting.period.month_end": { asOf?: string };
  /** Slice 4B (amendment 1, round 8) — 3B's `inventory.projection.rebuild` key verbatim. Omit both fields for the
   *  nightly whole-tenant rebuild of `party_ageing` and `item_profitability`; `asOf` defaults to the run date. */
  "accounting.projection.rebuild": { companyId?: string; asOf?: string };
  "pos.sync.apply": { terminalId: string; batch: unknown /* the TicketBatch, structurally */ };
  /** Slice 7C (A10, round 15). The `export_job` row carries the format, the recorded gates and the company. */
  "admin.export.run": { exportJobId: string };
  /** Slice 8C (B4, round 18; spelled `year` by B18 — `no-number-money` reads `tax`). Omit both fields for the
   *  nightly whole-tenant compare — 1B's integrity-check shape. */
  "hr.employee_ytd.rebuild": { companyId?: string; year?: number };
  /** Slice 9B (C3, round 20). Enqueued by `POST …/imports`, never scheduled; `only` restricts a resume to the named
   *  target tables (C14). */
  "admin.import.run": { companyId: string; runId: string; cutOverDate: string; dryRun: boolean; only?: string[] };
}
// Extending `Record<JobName, unknown>` (rather than an index signature) keeps `JobPayload[N]` well-typed for the
// names whose owning slice has not landed, so a slice adds ONLY its own key and touches no other line.

// packages/db/src/jobs/tenants.ts — scheduled handlers fan out through this, never through app.tenant (FORCE RLS)
/** Invokes `fn` once per tenant with BOUNDED CONCURRENCY (amended round 5; it was sequential until PR #3,
 *  so the nightly fan-out's wall clock grew linearly with the tenant count); one tenant's failure does not stop
 *  the rest, and the caller receives an aggregated failure after every tenant has been attempted (§4.9 — one
 *  broken tenant must not silence the nightly alarm for all the others). `concurrency` defaults to
 *  `sql.options.max - 1`, below the pool size so a task needing a second connection cannot deadlock, and clamps
 *  to at least 1 and at most the tenant count. The registry is still read `order by created_at, tenant_id`, but
 *  processing in that order was a side effect of the sequential loop and is not one now. */
export async function eachTenant(sql: Sql, fn: (tenantId: string) => Promise<void>, opts?: { concurrency?: number }): Promise<void>;

// packages/db/src/jobs/enqueue.ts
export interface JobEnvelope<T = unknown> { readonly tenantId: string; readonly requestId: string; readonly payload: T }
export interface EnqueueOptions { singletonKey?: string; startAfterSeconds?: number; retryLimit?: number /* default 3 */; retryDelaySeconds?: number /* default 60, exponential */ }
export interface JobClient {
  /** Inserts the job through pg-boss USING `tx` (tx.unsafe with pg-boss's own parameterised text and bound values), so it is visible only after the enclosing withTenant commits and never on rollback (spec:2321). Returns the pg-boss job id — for a `STATELY_JOBS` request that collapsed, the id of the queued job it collapsed into (round 8, below). */
  enqueue<N extends JobName>(tx: Sql, name: N, job: JobEnvelope<JobPayload[N]>, opts?: EnqueueOptions): Promise<string>;
}
export function createJobClient(boss: PgBoss): JobClient;
export const STATELY_JOBS: readonly JobName[];   // round 8: ["inventory.cost.replay", "accounting.projection.rebuild"]
export function queuePolicy(name: string): "standard" | "stately";   // what the install step creates `name` with
export const JOB_NAMES: readonly JobName[];      // 0D: Object.keys(JOBS), registry order — the install step and the isolation suite iterate this

// apps/worker/src/handler.ts
export type JobHandler<N extends JobName> = (sql: Sql, job: JobEnvelope<JobPayload[N]>, ctx: TenantContext /* systemContext(sql, tenantId, requestId) */) => Promise<void>;
export function registerHandler<N extends JobName>(name: N, handler: JobHandler<N>): void;   // throws if the name is already registered
export function registeredJobNames(): JobName[];                                             // sorted; fewer than JOBS until every owning slice has landed
/** Resolves the tenant's system principal and runs the registered handler. The one entry point the worker
 *  entrypoint, `startWorker()` (§4.17) and the job-isolation probes all go through. */
export async function runJob<N extends JobName>(sql: Sql, name: N, job: JobEnvelope<JobPayload[N]>): Promise<void>;

// apps/worker/src/log.ts (0D)
export function log(): Logger;
export function setLogger(l: Logger): void;

// tests/invariants/probes.ts — the job half of the isolation registry (0D), beside PROBES (§4.2.7)
export interface JobIsolationProbe {
  seed(db: Db, attacker: Seed, victim: Seed): Promise<void>;
  /** Optional adversarial payload; the shared harness defaults to {} for existing probes. */
  payload?(db: Db, attacker: Seed, victim: Seed): Promise<unknown>;
  /** If present, require this exact refusal code before verifying survivors; never swallow arbitrary errors. */
  expectedErrorCode?: string;
  /** Rows of `victim` that must still be there after the job ran for `attacker`. */
  survivors(db: Db, victim: Seed): Promise<number>;
}
export const JOB_PROBES: Readonly<Partial<Record<JobName, JobIsolationProbe>>>;
```

**6A job-probe correction (2026-10-08).** Optional `payload` and `expectedErrorCode` let the existing shared isolation harness invoke a validly shaped POS apply job with a victim terminal ID inside the attacker envelope. Existing probes keep `{}` and require success. A refusal probe asserts the exact declared error and still checks unchanged victim rows/audit state; handler validation is never weakened to accommodate an empty test payload.

Rules: every handler runs as the tenant's **system principal** (`systemContext`, spec:2179) and does its work as many short `withTenant` transactions (spec:1368), never one long one; scheduled jobs are registered with `boss.schedule(name, JOBS[name].schedule)` once per environment; **the scheduled *dispatcher* iterates `pgboss.tenant_registry (tenant_id uuid primary key, created_at timestamptz not null default now())` — created by migration 0004 and populated by the seed CLI, because a job runner cannot list `app.tenant` without a tenant set (FORCE RLS) — and invokes each registered handler once per tenant under that tenant's `systemContext`** (corrected in round 4, 1B amendment 1: the Rules sentence used to put the iteration inside the handler, which contradicts `JobHandler`'s own signature — it takes one `TenantContext`, not a list — and contradicts the code 0D ships, `apps/worker/src/index.ts` scheduling `${name}.fanout` and calling `eachTenant`. The signature wins); `JobPayload` is a type map grown additively per slice in `packages/db/src/jobs/payloads.ts`; the tenant-isolation harness (§3.7.2) enqueues each job for tenant A with tenant B's ids in the payload and asserts zero rows touched — narrowed by 0D to the job names with a **registered** handler (`registeredJobNames()`), since a name whose slice has not landed has nothing to probe.

**Two queues are `stately`, and a keyed request collapses only into a job that has not started (0D, corrected in round 8 by a 4B remediation; ADR 0007's amendment).** `STATELY_JOBS` — `inventory.cost.replay` and `accounting.projection.rebuild`, the two jobs `postDocument`'s step 14 enqueues with `singletonKey = companyId` — and `queuePolicy(name)` live in `jobs/enqueue.ts` and the barrel. The install step (`apps/worker/src/install.ts`) and its test twin `installBoss` create every queue with `createQueue(name, { policy: queuePolicy(name) })` — those two `stately`, every other one and every `<name>.fanout` `standard` — and the install step **exits non-zero if an existing queue's policy differs**, because pg-boss's `create_queue` is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and `updateQueue` refuses a policy change. pg-boss 12's `stately` index (`job_i3`, unique `(name, state, coalesce(singleton_key, ''))` where `state <= 'active'`) admits one job per key in each of `created`, `retry` and `active`, and its claim cannot make a second job of a key `active`. So for these two jobs `createJobClient` sends `singletonKey` **without** `singletonSeconds`, **requires** the key (keyless, every tenant's job would share the `''` slot), and: a request while the key's job is **queued** is refused by the index and **collapses** into it — `enqueue` locks that `created` row `FOR SHARE` on the caller's `tx`, so pg-boss's `FOR UPDATE … SKIP LOCKED` claim skips the job until the caller commits and the job can never start without the caller's writes, and resolves with its id; a request while the job is **active** inserts the next queued job, because the running job may already have read what the request changed; a request after it **completed** inserts a new one. `JobNotInsertedError` (not in the barrel) remains for every other non-insert — a keyed `standard` job still carries 0D's 24-hour `singletonSeconds` slot and still throws on it (SAH-005's pinned `accounting.period.month_end` case), and a stately collapse that finds no queued row to lock after three retried inserts throws it too. **Why:** 0D paired *every* key with `singletonSeconds = 86400`, a throttle slot whose unique index (`job_i4`) counts every state but `cancelled`, so a completed job refused its key for the rest of the UTC day — a company's second back-dated post failed, and its step-14 rebuild ran at most once a day. No environment has pg-boss installed yet (staging was never seeded), so no deployed queue needs recreating.

**`accounting.projection.rebuild`'s payload and probe (4B amendment 1, round 8).** 4B adds exactly one `JobPayload` key, `"accounting.projection.rebuild": { companyId?: string; asOf?: string }`, and **`JOB_PROBES` gains an entry for it** in `tests/invariants/probes.ts` in the PR that registers the handler (hazard 31). The shape is 3B's `inventory.projection.rebuild` key verbatim, deliberately: both are "rebuild this company's async projections as of this date", the two handlers are twins, and a reader who has seen one has seen both. **`JOBS` itself is not edited** — the name and its `"0 3 * * *"` schedule are already in 0B's closed sixteen-name const with `owner: "4B"`. (The block above records the keys this document names by contract; the tree's `packages/db/src/jobs/payloads.ts` also carries the 0D, 3A and 3B keys, including the `inventory.projection.rebuild` key this one copies.)

**Audit `table_name` sentinels (a shared literal namespace, like §4.14 and §4.15).** A job that has no row of its own to audit writes an `app.audit_log` row whose `table_name` is a sentinel rather than a table. The two allocated so far are **`integrity_incident`** and **`month_end_ready`**, both 1B's; 7B's `accounting.audit_log` report reads them. A slice that needs a third registers it here first. **8C registers `employee_ytd_drift`** (B2, round 18): the nightly `hr.employee_ytd.rebuild` reports drift rather than repairing it, on 6C's `cashier_snapshot_drift` precedent.

**One registered exception: `pos.sync.apply` (6A).** Its handler resolves the **terminal's** principal through `app.resolve_principal('terminal:<terminalId>')` and runs `applyBatch` under that context, because hazard 19 requires `document.posted_by` to be the terminal and a system-posted ticket would misattribute every POS posting in the ledger. The terminal id comes from the **payload the route wrote after authenticating the signed call**, never from a client body, and the handler re-checks `pos_terminal.revoked_at` before applying. Every write it makes is audited under the terminal's id, which is what §4.2.6's rule actually protects.

`batch` is `unknown` because `packages/db` may not import `@dulja/sync` (§3.1); the worker validates it through the shared wire contract.

#### 4.2.7 Hono route module shape and the `ROUTES` registry (0B)

**6C amendment A4.** Register four company-scoped route modules and exactly four probe keys: `/v1/companies/:companyId/employees` → `employeeRoutes` (`hr.employee.read`, `hr.employee.manage`); `/v1/companies/:companyId/cashiers` → `createCashierRoutes(authAdmin)` (`admin.user.manage`, `pos.cashier.manage_pin`); `/v1/companies/:companyId/branch-pos-policies` → `branchPosPolicyRoutes` (`admin.company.manage`); `/v1/companies/:companyId/attendance-events` → `attendanceEventRoutes` (`hr.employee.read`, `hr.attendance.record`). The cashier router is a factory consuming the existing auth-admin port.

**Convention (not in spec).** Routes are organised by module directory, mounted under the URL scheme: tenant-scoped resources at `/v1/admin/<resource>` and `/v1/companies`; company-scoped resources at `/v1/companies/{companyId}/<resource>` (no module segment — resource names are unique); terminal routes at `/v1/sync/<resource>` (spec:1296); async status at `/v1/jobs/{jobId}`; health at `/healthz` (spec:2314). Every `documents` route is generic over document types (`/v1/companies/{companyId}/documents`, `…/documents/{documentId}/lines`, `…/documents/{documentId}/transitions`); a type-specific route is a convention violation.

Sub-paths the scheme above does not spell out, fixed by 1A: `GET …/accounts/tree`, `POST …/accounts/{accountId}/archive`, `PUT …/documents/{documentId}/lines`, `POST …/fiscal-periods/{periodId}/close`, `POST …/fiscal-periods/{periodId}/reopen`. **Added in round 2** — by 2A: `POST …/document-types/{documentTypeId}/policies`, `POST …/document-types/{documentTypeId}/archive`, `POST …/parties/{partyId}/archive`; by 2B, on 1A's `documents` module: `POST …/documents/{documentId}/reverse`, `POST …/documents/{documentId}/overrides`, `DELETE …/documents/{documentId}`, `GET …/documents/{documentId}/events`; by 2C: `GET …/attachments/{attachmentId}/content` and `POST …/documents/{documentId}/print`. **Added in round 3** — by 3C, on 1A's `documents` module: `POST` and `GET …/documents/{documentId}/links`, `GET …/documents/{documentId}/open-quantity`, `POST` and `GET …/documents/{documentId}/landed-cost` — five sub-paths, no new module, no new `PROBES` key. **Added by 4A**, all on modules that already exist: on 1A's `documents` module `POST …/documents/{documentId}/convert-to-invoice`, `POST …/documents/{documentId}/credit-note`, `POST …/documents/{documentId}/allocations`, `GET …/documents/{documentId}/allocations`, `POST …/documents/{documentId}/allocations/{allocationId}/unallocate`, `GET …/documents/{documentId}/open-balance` and `POST …/documents/settlements`; on 2A's `parties` module `GET …/parties/{partyId}/balance`. **None of the eight takes a `PROBES` entry** — `PROBES` is keyed by `RouteModule.path`, so they inherit `documents`' and `parties`' existing keys, and 4A adds exactly one new key, for `payment-terms`. Every `POST` sub-path of an existing document is gated `requireDocumentPermission("submit")`, never `"create"` — §4.5.4's `"create"` branch resolves the type from the request body and 404s when the body does not carry one (see §4.5.4's note below). **Two riders from 4A's execution (round 7).** `POST …/documents/settlements` is **not** a sub-path of an existing document — it creates one, as 3D's `POST …/documents/transfers` does — so it is gated `requireDocumentPermission("create")`, and **its body names `documentTypeCode`, not a type id**, because that is what the `"create"` branch resolves the gate from; the handler resolves the id on the path company and the service still takes `documentTypeId`. And **`…/convert-to-invoice` and `…/credit-note` carry two gates** — `"submit"` on the source document's policy, then the target type's `approval.create` in the handler (§4.5.4's two-gate note). **A sub-path needs no `PROBES` entry of its own** — `PROBES` is keyed by `RouteModule.path` (hazard 31), so 2B's four routes and 2C's print route inherit `documents`' existing key, and the two genuinely new modules each slice mounts get one entry each: 2A two (`document-types`, `parties`), 2C two (`attachments`, `print-templates`). **Reads on `accounts`, `fiscal-periods` and `documents/{id}` are gated by membership only**, following §4.2.11's dimension precedent — spec:2158 gives the clerk "reads accounts" and §3.6.1 closes the vocabulary with no accounts-read code; a slice that wants one adds it to §3.6.2 first.

**The company-resolution guard on a membership-only company-scoped read — settled once in round 4 (0D), so no later slice re-decides it.** Nothing in the middleware chain refuses a `{companyId}` belonging to another tenant on a read gated by membership alone: RLS simply matches no row and the handler would answer **`200 { items: [], next_cursor: null }`**. That form is not expressible in the isolation harness — `IsolationProbe.expect` is typed `403 | 404` (above) and §3.7.2 says the harness asserts "a 404/403" — so **the guard is required, not optional**. Every company-scoped route module resolves the company first: one `select 1 from app.company where id = $1` inside the handler's existing `c.var.withTenant`, and `c.notFound()` on no row, which is `ERR_NOT_FOUND`, whose registry note is "never reveals cross-tenant existence". **It is a file-local `companyExists` function in each route module and is exported from none of them**, so it needs no §4.2.12 or §4.17.1 row and no two slices share one import. 0D's three modules ship it first; **1A's `accounts` / `fiscal-periods` / `documents`, 2A's `parties` / `document-types`, 2C's `attachments` and 7A's report routes all face the identical question and take the identical answer.**

```ts
// apps/api/src/routes/<module>/<resource>.ts
import { OpenAPIHono, createRoute, z } from "@hono/zod-openapi";
export const <resource>Routes = new OpenAPIHono<AppEnv>();
<resource>Routes.openapi(createRoute({ method, path, request, responses, middleware: [requirePermission(PERMISSION["<code>"], scope)], tags: ["<module>"] }), handler);

// apps/api/src/routes/index.ts — production only; no test type is reachable from here (§3.1 dependency rule)
export interface RouteModule {
  readonly path: string;                              // mount prefix, e.g. "/v1/companies/:companyId/accounts"
  readonly router: OpenAPIHono<AppEnv>;
  readonly permissions: readonly PermissionCode[];    // every code this module evaluates (the catalogue check reads it)
  readonly auth: "human" | "terminal" | "public";     // /healthz is public; /v1/sync/* is terminal
}
/** **`buildRoutes` is the authoritative form; `ROUTES` is derived from it.** A route module that needs an
 *  injected dependency (the invite endpoint needs `AuthAdmin`) cannot be built by a module-level const, so
 *  every slice that registers a module adds it **inside `buildRoutes`**, never by pushing onto `ROUTES`. */
export function buildRoutes(deps: { authAdmin: AuthAdmin }): readonly RouteModule[];
export const ROUTES: readonly RouteModule[] = buildRoutes({ authAdmin: new StubAuthAdmin() });
// — the stub-built list is what the catalogue lint, the OpenAPI generator and the isolation harness enumerate;
//   `createApp` mounts `buildRoutes({ authAdmin: deps.authAdmin })`, i.e. the real one.
/** The `Idempotency-Key` header, declared once so every unsafe route documents it identically (spec:2055).
 *  Every `post`/`put`/`patch`/`delete` `createRoute` in every slice sets `request.headers: IdempotencyHeader`. */
export const IdempotencyHeader: z.ZodObject<{ "Idempotency-Key": z.ZodString }>;

// apps/api/src/app.ts
export interface AppDeps { db: Sql; jobs: JobClient; logger: Logger; authAdmin: AuthAdmin; verifier: JwtVerifier; objectStore: ObjectStore; terminalJwtSigningKey: Uint8Array }
export function createApp(deps: AppDeps): OpenAPIHono<AppEnv>;   // mounts buildRoutes(deps), middleware chain §4.2.3, then assertRouteGates; used by tests

// tests/invariants/probes.ts — the probe registry lives in the test tier, keyed by RouteModule.path
import type { Db, Seed } from "@dulja/db/test";
export interface IsolationProbe { seed(db: Db, owner: Seed): Promise<{ path: string; method: string; body?: unknown }>; expect: 400 | 401 | 403 | 404 }
export const PROBES: Readonly<Record<string, IsolationProbe>>;   // key = the exact RouteModule.path string
/** The routes that answer *about the caller* rather than about a row, and so have no cross-tenant probe to
 *  perform. Exactly `{ "/healthz", "/v1/session" }` after 0B; a slice adding a member amends this document. */
export const TENANT_FREE: ReadonlySet<string>;
```

**`AppDeps` is seven members.** spec:2132 requires the invite endpoint to obtain its `sub` from Supabase and route tests to verify real signatures, so `apps/api` depends on the two ports of §4.2.3 (`AuthAdmin`, `JwtVerifier`) and never on Supabase itself — that is what makes five of them. Which `AuthAdmin` the deployed container receives is 0C's wiring decision (ADR 0011), not 0B's. The sixth, **`objectStore: ObjectStore`** (2C, `packages/db/src/attachment/object-store.ts`), is there because `POST …/attachments` writes an object *before* its row and the store must be swappable — `MemoryObjectStore` in tests and under `bun run dev`, `R2ObjectStore` in the container; which one the deployed container receives is 0C's ADR 0011 applied to ADR 0031. **The count is stated because it is load-bearing:** a later slice reading "five members, not three" would build a five-member object and would not compile against the app 2C ships.

**After Phase 6 and Phase 8 the count is EIGHT, and both of the last two are named here because neither slice can settle it from its own file (round 4; 8A raised it).** Two slices independently declare a seventh: **6A's `terminalJwtSigningKey: Uint8Array`** — the HS256 key `terminalAuth` signs and verifies the short-lived terminal JWT with (§4.10.3, spec:2273); bytes and not a string because `jose` takes bytes, derived once by the entrypoint from `ApiConfig` — and **8A's `hrKeys: HrKeyRing`** — the field-encryption ring (§4.12.5), on 2C's `objectStore` precedent, so a route never reads a key out of `process.env` and `startApi()` can mint a deterministic test key. **§6.3 runs 8A in parallel with the 6A → 6C → 6B → 6D chain**, so whichever merges second makes the true count eight, and a plan that reads only the other's amendment builds a seven-member object that does not compile. **The settlement: the final count is eight; each of the two slices adds its own member and its own descriptive paragraph in its own Task 0 PR, and — whichever merges second — writes the count as *eight* rather than *seven*.** `startApi()` (§4.2.12) and the production composition root build the same object and move with it in the same PR; a ninth member amends this paragraph first.

**`apps/api` has exactly two entry points**: `package.json` `exports` is `{ ".": "./src/app.ts", "./routes": "./src/routes/index.ts" }`, and `src/app.ts` re-exports `{ ROUTES, buildRoutes, type RouteModule }`. The `tests` tier imports `@dulja/api` only through these; never a route file (§3.1).

**Why the probe is not on `RouteModule`:** `IsolationProbe` uses `Db` and `Seed` from `@dulja/db/test`, where `Db` wraps `StartedPostgreSqlContainer` (§4.1). Putting it on a production interface would give every route module in `apps/api` a compile- and bundle-time dependency on Testcontainers, which §3.1's dependency rule and the `tests` tier row forbid. The guarantee is preserved in the test tier instead: `tests/invariants/tenant-isolation.test.ts` fails the build when a `ROUTES` entry has no `PROBES[path]` entry (and when a `PROBES` key matches no route).

OpenAPI: `bun run --cwd packages/contracts openapi:generate` writes `packages/contracts/openapi.json` from `createApp().getOpenAPIDocument()`; CI runs the generator and fails on a diff (spec:2055); the client `packages/contracts/src/client/` is generated from that file.

An `IsolationProbe.expect` of `401` is the recorded value for a module whose `auth` is `"terminal"`; `400` is recorded for a public module whose only key is a bearer secret. Neither is a widened acceptance set — the harness still asserts equality. `TENANT_FREE` is unchanged and gains no member.

| `RouteModule.path` | Router export | Slice | Gate codes | `auth` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/admin/terminals` | `terminalRoutes` | 6A | `admin.terminal.manage` | `human` |
| `/v1/sync/enrol` | `enrolmentRoutes` | 6A | — | `public` |
| `/v1/sync/catalogue` | `catalogueRoutes` | 6A | `pos.sync.pull` | `terminal` |
| `/v1/sync/tickets` | `ticketRoutes` | 6A | `pos.sync.push` | `terminal` |
| `/v1/companies/:companyId/needs-attention` | `needsAttentionRoutes` | 6A | `pos.needs_attention.resolve` | `human` |

**6C staff-screen context reconciliation.** `GET /v1/staff-context` is mounted by
`staffContextRouteModule` / `staffContextRoutes` with human authentication and the
four existing 6C gate codes (`hr.employee.read`, `hr.employee.manage`,
`hr.attendance.record`, `pos.cashier.manage_pin`). Its read-only `listStaffContext(tx)`
repository returns only companies and active dimension values whose dimension type
is BRANCH in that company and where `app.actor_has` admits at least one of those
codes at the actual company/branch. No accessible configured branch yields 403.
`StaffContextSchema` is `{ companies: [{ id, code, name, baseCurrency, branches:
[{ id, code, nameEn, nameAr }] }] }`, with UUID IDs and nullable Arabic names.
This supplies staff-screen selectors without widening admin company/dimension
routes, adding a permission, or treating a returned ID as authorization. Every
staff operation still applies its own gate and branch RLS. Register the exact
module path in PROBES with expected 403; test branch-only grants, company/tenant
separation and the unchanged admin route refusal. The back-office context query
is scoped to the authenticated session and clears selected-company form state
when the session/company changes.
Acceptance 23's existing local browser operator fixture gains the four 6C codes
in its explicit ADMIN_CODES list, alongside its existing administration and tax
codes. `grantAdminRole` retains its signature and tenant/system writer; this is
test-only authority for actual employee, PIN and policy browser workflows, not
a production role or change to the frozen seed helpers.

**PR 12 review amendment (2026-10-22, owner direction: best practice).** The projection's code set grows from four to six: `pos.report.read` (6D's shift register and Z-report screens) and `admin.company.manage` (the branch-limit screen) join the four 6C codes, because those screens use the same selector and a principal holding only their own gate — the seeded `auditor`, a cloned policy role — was refused the screen. The projection still grants nothing: every operation applies its own gate and branch RLS, and `apps/api/test/routes/staff-context.test.ts` pins a report-only and a policy-only principal to their own branches.

**`/v1/companies/:companyId/needs-attention` is 6A's module and 7C mounts nothing on it.** 7C owns the `needs_attention` `DatasetId` (§4.16.2) and reads the table through `…/reports/{code}/runs`. `/v1/sync/enrol` is §4.10.3's frozen path, used verbatim.

The seventh, **`terminalJwtSigningKey: Uint8Array`** (6A), is the HS256 key `terminalAuth` signs and verifies the short-lived terminal JWT with (§4.10.3, spec:2273). `jose` takes bytes; the entrypoint derives it as `new TextEncoder().encode(config.terminalJwtSigningKey)` from §4.2.3's `ApiConfig`, so one place reads the environment. `startApi()` uses a fixed test literal so terminal tokens verify without an environment variable. Round 4's final-eight settlement still applies when 8A adds `hrKeys: HrKeyRing`.

#### 4.2.8 Zod contract naming, common schemas, list envelope, cursor, filter grammar, JSON forms (0B)

**6C amendment A4 (contract modules).** `hr/employee.ts`, `hr/attendance.ts`, `pos/cashier.ts` and `pos/branch-pos-policy.ts` are the registered modules for the schemas specified in 6C Tasks 3, 4 and 8. Amounts and percentage/increment decimals remain strings on the wire; PIN hashes and stored authentication secrets are not directory response fields.

**Cashier-screen linked identity reconciliation.** `CashierSchema` additionally
carries `employeeNumber: string | null`. For a live credential, T8's repository
projects the linked number through the existing narrow
`app.resolve_cashier_employee(company_id, branch_id, principal_id)` resolver,
under the actual human caller's tenant and permitted credential branch. A revoked
credential yields null; no employee-directory visibility is widened. This lets a
manager identify an authorized credential when its employee home branch differs,
using the same bounded identity projection already registered for catalogue and
attendance. The UI labels rows with the projected number or an independently
visible directory number, and never requires raw principal/employee IDs. No new
query filter, payroll field, authority or resolver grant is added. Test an actual
branch-only human manager's list/reset with home B/credential A, retaining ordinary
directory refusal and other-branch/company/tenant refusal.

**Convention (not in spec).** `packages/contracts/src/<module>/<resource>.ts` exports `<Resource>Schema` (the entity as returned), `Create<Resource>Body`, `Update<Resource>Body`, `<Resource>Query`, `<Resource>List = ListEnvelope(<Resource>Schema)`; `packages/contracts/src/common.ts` exports:

```ts
export const UuidSchema = z.string().uuid();
export const DateSchema = z.string().regex(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/);                 // effective_date and every `date` column
export const TimestampSchema = z.string().datetime({ offset: true });               // timestamptz, RFC 3339 UTC
export const CurrencySchema = z.string().regex(/^[A-Z]{3}$/);
export const MoneySchema = z.object({ amount: z.string().regex(/^-?\d+\.\d{4}$/), currency: CurrencySchema });   // Money.toJSON
export const QuantitySchema = z.string().regex(/^-?\d+\.\d{6}$/);                   // Quantity.toJSON
export const RateSchema = z.string().regex(/^\d+\.\d{8}$/);
export const CursorSchema = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/);                    // opaque base64url of JSON { k: unknown[]; id: string }
export const ListEnvelope = <T extends z.ZodTypeAny>(item: T) => z.object({ items: z.array(item), next_cursor: z.string().nullable() });
export const ListQuery = z.object({ cursor: CursorSchema.optional(), limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(1000).default(100), sort: z.string().optional(), fields: z.string().optional() });
export const ProblemSchema = z.object({ type: z.string(), title: z.string(), status: z.number(), detail: z.string(), instance: z.string(), code: z.string(), remedy: z.string(), requestId: z.string(), errors: z.array(z.object({ path: z.string(), message: z.string() })).optional() });

/** The cursor CODEC — one implementation, in `common.ts`, imported by every list handler in every slice.
 *  A slice that writes its own base64url round-trip has two spellings of one thing (hazard 9). */
export interface Cursor { k: unknown[]; id: string }
export function encodeCursor(c: Cursor): string;      // base64url of JSON.stringify(c)
export function decodeCursor(raw: string): Cursor;    // throws AppError("ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED") on anything that is not this shape

/** The filter grammar below, parsed once. */
export const FILTER_OPS = ["eq", "ne", "lt", "lte", "gt", "gte", "in", "like"] as const;
export type FilterOp = (typeof FILTER_OPS)[number];
export interface FilterClause { field: string; op: FilterOp; value: string }
export function parseFilters(query: Record<string, string | string[]>): FilterClause[];   // ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED on an unknown operator
```

Filter grammar: query parameters `filter[<field>][<op>]=<value>` with `op ∈ eq | ne | lt | lte | gt | gte | in | like` (`in` comma-separated; `like` is a prefix match, never a regex); `sort=<field>,-<field>`; `fields=<a>,<b>` (sparse fieldsets). Each resource declares its filterable and sortable fields in its `<Resource>Query` schema — an undeclared field is `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`; **no field name ever reaches SQL as text** — the handler maps declared fields to Drizzle columns (test 27).

##### The one list-filter convention (settled in round 2; 2A asked, and three forms had already shipped)

The written plans produced three spellings, so the rule is stated in two layers and both bind every slice from 2C onward.

**Layer 1 — the wire shape is the `filter[<field>][<op>]` grammar above, and nothing else.** The only flat query parameters a list route may declare are `ListQuery`'s own four (`cursor`, `limit`, `sort`, `fields`) plus the **closed, grandfathered set** the frozen plans already ship: 0B's `AuditLogQuery`, 1A's `LedgerEntryQuery` (`accountId`, `fiscalPeriodId`, `documentId`, `from`, `to`) and 1B's `TrialBalanceQuery` / `LedgerQuery`. **No slice introduces a new flat filter parameter.** Those four schemas are not to be "fixed" either — 2A's Task 13 consumes `?documentId=` exactly as 1A shipped it, and churning a frozen route to match a convention it predates buys nothing.

**Layer 2 — inside the grammar, the default is literal `filter[<field>][<op>]` keys in the `<Resource>Query` schema** (2A's form, and the form every remaining slice uses). A literal key *is* the declaration Layer 1's sentence asks for: typed, with the enum values checked by Zod rather than by a hand-written switch on a `FilterClause.field` string, and visible in the generated OpenAPI document. **`parseFilters` / `FILTER_OPS` / `FilterClause` stay registered and stay the mechanism for a wide or open filter surface** — more than about four field × operator pairs, or any operator beyond `eq` — where enumerating keys would be worse than parsing them: 0B's `audit-log` as shipped, and the routes 4B (ageing), 7A (report runs) and 9B (import batches) will need. **A route uses one mechanism or the other, never both**, and there is exactly one `parseFilters` and one cursor codec in the repository (hazard 9).

**No plan is corrected by this settlement** — every written plan is compliant, 2A's two configuration routes included. Pagination is keyset on `(sort key, id)`; the cursor encodes the last row's values. Money is always `{ amount, currency }`; quantities and rates are strings; dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps RFC 3339 in UTC; ids uuid strings; enums lower snake case; every list response is `{ items, next_cursor }` — **with one registered exception: 1B's `LedgerList` carries a third member `opening_base_balance`**, because a ledger that does not state the balance brought forward would force the client to derive it by money arithmetic, which spec:2041 exists to prevent. The addition is purely additive; a reader of `items`/`next_cursor` is unaffected. A slice wanting a second exception amends this paragraph first.

**The one exception: a money field on a sub-resource of a single document is a bare 4-dp decimal string (3C).** `z.string().regex(/^-?\d+\.\d{4}$/)`, with **no `currency` member**, in `accounting/document-link.ts` (`DocumentLinkSchema.amount`) and `inventory/landed-cost.ts` (`LandedCostAllocationSchema.allocatedAmount`, `LandedCostSummarySchema.lineAmount` / `allocated` / `landedAmount`). Two reasons, and both are about where the currency lives. (1) `app.document_link` **has no currency column** (§4.6.1) — the currency is the *document's*, and emitting `{ amount, currency }` would mean joining `app.document` on every link read to restate a value the caller already has from the document it just fetched. (2) Every one of these figures is returned under a path that already names the document (`…/documents/{documentId}/links`, `…/landed-cost`), so the currency is fixed for the whole response and repeating it per row is noise a client cannot use to disambiguate anything. The rule this exception does **not** touch: the `Money` *type* is still what computes every one of these numbers (`landedCostSummary` does the addition in `Money`, Global Constraint 4), the scale is still 4, and `no-number-money` still forbids a `number`. A **top-level** resource carrying money — anything whose currency is not implied by its own path — keeps `MoneySchema`, so this is an exception for document sub-resources and not a second general spelling.

**The second registered form: a row's money column may be a bare signed 4-dp decimal string when the row carries its own `currency` exactly once (4B amendment 12, round 8)**, and 4B's `packages/contracts/src/accounting/bank.ts` and the ageing DTOs in `accounting/reports.ts` do that. "Money is always `{ amount, currency }`" is written for a *field*, and repeating the currency on seven bucket columns of one ageing row — five buckets, `total` and `totalBase` — would put the same three characters in the payload seven times and force the ageing handler to read `company.base_currency` for `totalBase` alone, a query the report does not otherwise make. It registers shipped practice rather than inventing an exception: 1A's `DocumentLineSchema` already declares `debit: Amount, credit: Amount` over `const Amount = z.string().regex(/^\d+\.\d{4}$/)` with the currency on the document header. The registered form is `const Amount = z.string().regex(/^-?\d+\.\d{4}$/)` — **file-local, never a `common.ts` export**, because a shared name would invite a slice to reach for it where `MoneySchema` is right. **It differs from 3C's form above in where the currency lives** — 3C's rows carry none because their path names the document, this form's row names its own — and it is no wider: `MoneySchema` remains the rule for a standalone amount, and `CreateBankMatchBody.amount`, `ReconciledBalanceSchema.statement`/`.ledger` and `ReconcilableSchema.amount` all use it. **Two bare forms are now registered, 3C's and this one; a slice wanting a third amends this paragraph first.**

| `admin/export.ts` | `ExportFormatSchema`, `ExportStatusSchema`, `CreateExportBody`, `ExportAcceptedSchema`, `ExportJobSchema`, `ExportJobQuery`, `ExportJobList`, `ExportManifestSchema`, `ExportJobDto` | 7C (A14, round 15) |
| `accounting/payment-term.ts` | `PaymentTermSchema`, `CreatePaymentTermBody`, `UpdatePaymentTermBody`, `PaymentTermQuery`, `PaymentTermList`, `PaymentTermDto` | 4A |
| `accounting/invoice.ts` | `ConvertLineSchema`, `ConvertToInvoiceBody`, `ConvertToInvoiceResultSchema`, `CreditNoteLineSchema`, `CreditNoteBody`, `CreditNoteResultSchema` | 4A |
| `accounting/allocation.ts` | `AllocationSchema`, `AllocateSettlementBody`, `AllocateSettlementResultSchema`, `UnallocateBody`, `AllocationQuery`, `AllocationList`, `OpenBalanceSchema`, `PartyBalanceSchema` | 4A |

**The four 4A modules are registered because they are shared nouns** (round 7): 4B ships an ageing surface over the same nouns, 7C ships the AR/AP reports, and both would otherwise be free to invent a second `AllocationSchema`.

**Two notes on the round-2 rows, both cross-slice.**

**`TransitionResultSchema` grows to nine members as a superset, and 1A's six all survive (2B; a shape change, recorded as such).** §4.3.1's `TransitionResult` names `documentId`, `from`, `to`, `eventId`, `number`; 1A's wire schema names `documentId`, `status`, `number`, `series`, `fiscalPeriodId`, `ledgerEntryIds`. 2B adds `from`, `to` and `eventId` and **keeps all six of 1A's**, because 1A's own route test asserts three of them and `docs/ui/phase-1-api-surface.md` publishes all six; the `TransitionResult` OpenAPI component name is unchanged. Replacing rather than widening would have broken a slice 2B does not edit.

**`DocumentLineInput` is the line as *accepted*, and it is grown by the slice that adds the key it names.** It replaces 1A's inline body object and keeps every constraint 1A chose deliberately: the non-negative `Amount` regex, the debit-or-credit `.refine`, `.min(1)` on the list, and the two `.openapi(…)` component names; `accountId` is required **conditionally on `kind === "account"`**, so a legitimate item line may carry none while 1A's tombstone shape stays filtered. The **returned** `DocumentLineSchema` uses a separate `SignedAmount`, because a reversal's magnitudes genuinely are negative and a non-negative response schema would fail wire validation on every `GET` of a reversal. **3A adds `warehouseId`/`lotId`/`unitId`/`unitQuantity` and 5A adds `taxCodeId` to `DocumentLineInput` in the same PR as the foreign key each adds (§4.3.4), never before** — the column exists from 2A, the wire field arrives with its FK.

**`DocumentLineKindSchema` is rewritten to the full six-label union `["account","item","tax","text","tender","payroll"]` by whichever of 6A's 0061 and 8B's 0087 lands first**, for exactly the reason §4.3.4 gives for the SQL CHECK: Phase 8 may execute before or after Phase 6 (spec:2301), and a schema listing only the labels admitted so far would reject the other phase's label when it ran second. 3C's `DraftLine.kind` takes the same union in the same PR, without which the back-office half of acceptance test 22 cannot carry a tender line.

**`GET …/documents/{documentId}/events` declares no query parameters** (2B). `listDocumentEvents` takes no `limit`/`cursor`, and advertising `ListQuery` while ignoring it would let a caller mistake a truncated page for a complete list; `next_cursor` is a constant `null` with a comment saying why, and **7B adds paging in the PR that needs it** (`accounting.document_event_log`). There is therefore no `DocumentEventQuery`. *(Retired from 7B by 7B amendment A16, round 14: `accounting.document_event_log` reads 7A's `document_event` dataset, never this route.)*

#### 4.2.9 Idempotency middleware semantics (0B)

Header `Idempotency-Key` (any string ≤ 200 chars) required on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (spec:2055); missing → `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING`. Key is `(tenant_id, principal_id, key)` (plan0A:2558); `request_hash = sha256(method || "\n" || path || "\n" || canonical JSON body)`, where `path` is the path Hono routed on (`c.req.path`: unreserved escapes decoded by `decodeURI`, reserved `%2F`/`%3F`/`%25` kept as sent — amended by the PR 11 review, so a path with no `%` hashes exactly as before and two spellings that reach one handler with one set of parameters are one request for a key). First arrival inserts the row with `response_code null`; a concurrent duplicate (row exists, `response_code null`) → 409 `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After: 2`; same key with a different hash → 409 `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; same key and hash after completion → replay of the stored `response_code` and `response_body` with header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. **Two transactions — amended round 5; this sentence read "three transactions, deliberately" until 2026-09-18** (this is the shape §4.3.1 refers to): the middleware opens its own `withTenant` for the reservation and **commits it**, then the handler *and* the `update … set response_code` run inside a single second `withTenant`, each downstream `c.var.withTenant` call joining it as a **savepoint** rather than opening a transaction of its own. The reservation must still be a separate, earlier transaction — a concurrent duplicate has to be able to *see* the in-flight row to answer `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`, which it could not if the row were invisible until the handler committed. **The third transaction was the defect PR #3 removed:** the handler's own committed, and a crash before the separate response write left a committed mutation under `response_code null` for the 120-second reclaim to run a second time — the double write this middleware exists to prevent. ADR 0020 §3 carries the argument and supersedes ADR 0004 in part; it is **a proposal**, so if the owner reverses it this paragraph returns to three. Consequences the plan must implement: a handler that throws is still recorded — the same transaction writes the error `response_code` and problem body, so a retry replays the failure rather than re-running the write; and a reservation whose process died (`response_code` null and `created_at` older than **120 seconds**) is reclaimable — the middleware takes it over with `update … set created_at = now() where key = $1 and response_code is null and created_at < now() - interval '120 seconds'` **and, round 5, `and request_hash = excluded.request_hash`**, so a crash cannot poison a key for the full 24 h. That last conjunct is also round 5's: the reclaim used to overwrite `request_hash`, so a slow first request could record its own answer into a row a second body had claimed, and a replay of that second body was served the first's response. A different body against a reclaimable key is `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` like any other mismatch, which is what the clause above already promised. `expires_at` 24 h (plan0A:2557); purge by `admin.idempotency_key.purge`. `POST /v1/sync/tickets` carries the header like every unsafe route **and** dedups per ticket on `client_ref` — two layers, both required (spec:1304, 2201).

**Liveness, fence and the first-write transaction (full review 2026-11-15, CON-01/CON-02; proposed amendment to ADR 0020).** Age alone no longer reclaims a key. The request-spanning transaction holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('idempotency:<tenant>/<principal>/<key>', 0))` for its life, and the reclaim above gains a last conjunct, `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(<same key>)`, so a running request is never reclaimed and its retry gets `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`. The reservation's `created_at` is a fencing token. The request checks it before the handler runs, and the response update is conditioned on it and on `response_code is null`. A request superseded before it took the lock answers `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` and rolls back. **`TRANSACTION_AT_FIRST_WRITE` and `isTransactionAtFirstWritePath(method, path)` join the frozen names**: for a member (only `POST …/payroll-runs/{documentId}/payslips`), each `c.var.withTenant` call is its own short transaction until the first one that writes. That one stays open as the request transaction, and the response record commits in it, so the one-transaction guarantee holds and no connection idles through the renders. `REPLAY_BY_RERUN` and `SELF_TRANSACTED` keep the age-only reclaim with a fenced record, and hold no connection across the handler.

**One-time secret response exception (6A, 2026-10-07; proposed amendments to ADRs 0055 and 0020).** `ONE_SHOT_SECRET_RESPONSES` registers exactly `POST /v1/admin/terminals/enrolments`, matched on the concrete routed path (`c.req.path`), including equivalent unreserved percent-encoding. Its successful first response is 201 and contains the plaintext enrolment code once. In the ordinary request-spanning transaction, enrolment writes commit together with a safe replay record: status 409 and an `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` problem telling the operator that the one-time code was already issued and a fresh enrolment is required. Neither the plaintext code nor a recoverable version enters `idempotency_key.response_body`; only `terminal_enrolment.code_hash` stores its hash. Failed issuance responses keep ordinary replay semantics. Same-key retries, including retries after management authority is removed, return the safe 409 without re-running issuance. In-flight, request-hash and reclaim checks remain unchanged. The route remains inside the existing atomic mutation/response-record transaction and joins neither `REPLAY_BY_RERUN` nor `SELF_TRANSACTED`. This correction implements the authorized one-time-display/hash-only enrolment design; it does not weaken mutation idempotency. A lost first response reserves its terminal code until that enrolment expires (§4.10.3, PR 12 review); a new issuance before then uses a fresh terminal code.

**Frozen names (0B):**

```ts
// apps/api/src/middleware/idempotency.ts
export function idempotency(db: Sql): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
export const RECLAIM_AFTER_SECONDS = 120;   // the reclaim window above, as a name — no plan re-types the literal
// 6A — exactly POST /v1/admin/terminals/enrolments; successful 201 is never cached with its secret.
export const ONE_SHOT_SECRET_RESPONSES: readonly { method: string; path: RegExp }[];
// 2C — the write-free routes whose response is not JSON. See the paragraph below.
export const REPLAY_BY_RERUN: readonly { method: string; path: RegExp }[];
export function isReplayByRerun(c: Context<AppEnv>): boolean;
export function isReplayByRerunPath(method: string, path: string): boolean;   // 2C — also read by assertRouteGates (§4.2.5; round 10)
// apps/api/src/routes/index.ts — the OpenAPI declaration of the header (§4.2.7)
export const IdempotencyHeader: z.ZodObject<{ "Idempotency-Key": z.ZodString }>;
```

**`REPLAY_BY_RERUN` and the two binary-body problems it closes (2C).** The middleware `JSON.parse`s the response body to store it, and a PDF parses as nothing — a replay would have returned `null`. `REPLAY_BY_RERUN` is a `readonly { method: string; path: RegExp }[]` of **write-free** routes whose response is not JSON; at 2C it holds exactly `POST …/documents/{documentId}/print`. For a matching route a replayed key **re-runs the handler** instead of returning the stored body, and the recorded `response_body` is a descriptor `{ contentType, byteSize, sha256 }` rather than the bytes. The reservation, the request-hash comparison and `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` are all unchanged. **A route that writes may never join this list.** `isReplayByRerun(c)` matches the **concrete routed path** (`c.req.path`, percent-decoded exactly as the router decodes it — PR 11 review: matching the URL's encoded spelling let `…/%70rint` reach the handler unmatched), never `c.req.routePath`: the middleware is registered with `app.use`, so `routePath` there is the middleware's own pattern and a pattern comparison would match nothing. **`assertRouteGates` reads this list too (round 10):** it is the only evidence on which a read code may gate an unsafe method (`markWriteFreeGate`, §4.2.5). A matching route runs **outside** the request-spanning transaction above (Phase 2 review, ADR 0087 decision 7, a proposal): each `c.var.withTenant` the handler makes is its own short transaction and the response descriptor is recorded in one more, which costs nothing on a crash because a replay re-runs the handler anyway. POST …/payroll-runs/{documentId}/payslips returns JSON and writes, so it is not a member (8D, A5).

**The request hash of a `multipart/form-data` body is taken over its parsed parts, never its wire bytes.** `await c.req.text()` re-encodes a binary part as UTF-8 and corrupts every byte above 0x7f; hashing the wire bytes instead is equally wrong and less obvious, because `new Request(…, { body: formData })` mints a fresh random boundary every time, so two honest retries differ byte for byte and the second is refused as `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. The digest is therefore over `[name, fileName, contentType, sha256(bytes)]` per part, sorted — **a boundary never enters it**. Hono caches the parsed form, so the handler's own `c.req.formData()` re-uses that parse and the bytes reach the store intact.

The `aal` gate's own constant, `AAL1_PATHS`, is in §4.2.3 with the middleware chain it belongs to.

**Public routes carry no idempotency, and declare no `Idempotency-Key`.** The middleware needs a tenant and a principal to key on, and a `auth: "public"` module has neither. `createApp` therefore attaches `idempotency` from the same `route.auth` switch that attaches `authenticate` / `terminalAuth`: `"human"` and `"terminal"` get it, `"public"` gets neither. An unsafe public route must be **idempotent in its own right** and say how in one sentence: `POST /v1/sync/enrol` is, because redemption is `update … set redeemed_at = now() where redeemed_at is null returning …` and a second redemption of one code answers `ERR_TERMINAL_ENROLMENT_INVALID` whatever the header says. A future public unsafe route that cannot make that claim does not become public.

#### 4.2.10 Currency and exchange-rate tables (0D, migration 0005) — convention (not in spec) beyond spec:1177, 1762

```sql
create table app.currency (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id),
  code char(3) not null, name_en text not null, name_ar text, minor_units smallint not null default 2,
  pos_rounding_increment numeric(19,4) not null default 0.01,           -- spec:1349 POS rounding per currency
  rounding_mode text not null default 'HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO' check (rounding_mode in ('HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO','HALF_EVEN','TOWARD_ZERO','AWAY_FROM_ZERO')),
  archived_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (tenant_id, code), unique (tenant_id, id));
create table app.exchange_rate (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  from_currency char(3) not null, to_currency char(3) not null, rate numeric(19,8) not null check (rate > 0),
  effective_from date not null, source text not null,                     -- 'BNM 2026-09-04', 'manual:<actor_id>'
  entered_by uuid not null default app.current_actor() references app.principal(id),   -- stamped
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (company_id, from_currency, to_currency, effective_from), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id));
-- rate lookup: the row with the greatest effective_from <= the document's effective_date for (company, from, to); no row → the caller raises ERR_RATE_NOT_FOUND (422).
-- The identity pair (p_from = p_to) is never looked up: the application uses UNIT_RATE (rate 1, source 'unit').
create function app.rate_for(p_company uuid, p_from char(3), p_to char(3), p_on date) returns app.exchange_rate language sql stable as $$
  select r.* from app.exchange_rate r
   where r.company_id = p_company and r.from_currency = p_from and r.to_currency = p_to and r.effective_from <= p_on
   order by r.effective_from desc
   limit 1
$$;
```

#### 4.2.11 Dimension API and custom fields (0D) — convention (not in spec) beyond spec:1235, 2320

Dimensions use the 0001 tables; API `POST /v1/companies/{companyId}/dimension-types`, `…/dimension-types/{id}/values` under `admin.company.manage`; reads need membership only. Custom fields (migration 0006):

```sql
create table app.custom_field_definition (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  entity text not null check (entity in ('document','party','item','employee')),   -- 'document' in 0D; others enabled by their slices
  document_type_id uuid,                                                          -- null = every type of that entity
  code text not null, name_en text not null, name_ar text,
  kind text not null check (kind in ('text','integer','decimal','money','date','boolean','dimension_value','enum')),
  required boolean not null default false, options jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,   -- enum labels, decimal scale, dimension_type_id
  indexed boolean not null default false, archived_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (company_id, entity, code), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, document_type_id) references app.document_type(tenant_id, id));
create table app.custom_field_value (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id),
  definition_id uuid not null, entity_id uuid not null,                          -- the document/party/item/employee id
  value jsonb not null,                                                            -- money as {"amount","currency"}; decimal as string
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (definition_id, entity_id), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, definition_id) references app.custom_field_definition(tenant_id, id));
create index custom_field_value_lookup_idx on app.custom_field_value (definition_id, (value));
```

Validation is `packages/domain/src/custom-fields/validate.ts`: `validateCustomFieldValue(def: CustomFieldDefinition, value: unknown): ValidationResult`.

#### 4.2.12 Test-harness export and the shared test utilities (0B)

`packages/db/package.json` `exports` gains `"./test": "./test/index.ts"`; `packages/db/test/index.ts` is `export * from "./harness"; export * from "./fixtures";`. **0C adds two more subpaths — `"./provision/verify-supabase"` (so the staging suite can import the posture probe) and `"./seed"` (`./src/seed/index.ts`, §4.2.13).** The seed is deliberately **not** re-exported from `packages/db/src/index.ts`: `packages/db/src/seed/auth-admin.ts` imports `@supabase/supabase-js`, and a barrel re-export would put the service-role admin client on the import graph of every `apps/api` and `apps/worker` module that imports `withTenant`. Root `tests/` and `apps/*/test` import `startDb`, `seedTenant`, `draftDocument`, `uuidv7`, `Seed`, `Db` from `@dulja/db/test`, and `withTenant` (production) from `@dulja/db`. `apps/api/test/support/app.ts` exports `startApi()` with a local JWKS issuer (0B generates a test key pair; production verifies Supabase's) so every route test and the isolation harness run on Testcontainers alone.

**The full signature — every route test in every slice calls `request`, so it is written out here rather than elided** (convention, not in spec):

```ts
// apps/api/test/support/app.ts (0B)
export interface ApiRequest {
  method: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  path: string;                       // '/v1/…', no origin; query string included in the path
  body?: unknown;                     // JSON.stringify'd with Content-Type: application/json unless `form` is set
  form?: FormData;                    // multipart (2C attachment upload); mutually exclusive with `body`
  as?: string;                        // principal id → Authorization: Bearer tokenFor(as, aal); omit for an unauthenticated call
  aal?: "aal1" | "aal2";              // default "aal2"
  idempotencyKey?: string | null;     // default: a fresh uuidv7 is minted for every unsafe method (so ordinary tests need not think about it)
                                      // pass an explicit string to test replay; pass null to send NO header (the ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISSING case)
  headers?: Record<string, string>;   // merged last — wins over every header above (terminal signature headers, forged X-Tenant-Id, …)
}
export interface StartedApi {
  db: Db;
  objectStore: MemoryObjectStore;    // 2C — the in-memory store this instance's AppDeps was built with
  app: OpenAPIHono<AppEnv>;
  /** Always writes `iss: TEST_ISSUER`, `exp: now + 600`, and the principal's `auth_subject` as `sub`. */
  tokenFor(principalId: string, aal?: "aal1" | "aal2"): string;
  /** Signs an ARBITRARY claim set with the same key and `kid` — the only way to mint the expired and
   *  wrong-issuer tokens §3.7.2 requires the bypass suite to attempt. */
  signToken(claims: Record<string, unknown>): string;
  /** Refreshes the principal → `auth_subject` map. `request({ as })` calls it on a miss; a test that hands a
   *  raw token to `headers` calls it itself before `tokenFor`. A principal the map has never seen is signed
   *  with its own id as the subject, which resolves to no membership — the orphan-token case. */
  loadPrincipals(): Promise<void>;
  request(input: ApiRequest): Promise<Response>;   // the Fetch API Response; `await res.json() as Problem` on a failure (§4.2.4)
  stop(): Promise<void>;                            // stops the container; `db.stop()` is not called separately
}
export function startApi(opts?: { authAdmin?: AuthAdmin }): Promise<StartedApi>;
export const TEST_ISSUER = "https://test.dulja.invalid/auth/v1";
```

`startApi()` builds the **seven-member** `AppDeps` of §4.2.7 itself: a real RS256 key pair and a local JWKS through `createJwtVerifierWithKeys`, `new StubAuthAdmin()`, a `logger` with a no-op sink, a `jobs` client that throws until 0D wires pg-boss, and **a fresh `MemoryObjectStore()` (2C), exposed on `StartedApi` as `objectStore` so a route test can assert what was stored and can tamper with an object to exercise ADR 0031's integrity refusal**. **0C additionally passes `debug: pgDebugTracer()` to that `createDb` call** (§4.2.2), so route-test Postgres spans join the request trace; nothing else about the harness changes.

**6C provider-call test seam.** `startApi` accepts the optional injected `AuthAdmin`; omission retains `new StubAuthAdmin()`. The returned fixture shape is unchanged. This proves invalid employee, actual-company branch and PIN requests make zero provider calls, while replay/concurrency creates one user. No production authentication bypass is introduced.

Every slice that adds routes uses this shape unchanged; a slice needing a new field amends this document first.

#### 4.2.13 The seed CLI's loader seam (0C, `packages/db/src/seed/`) — convention (not in spec); the sequence is §3.4.8

§3.4.8 assigns a sub-pack loader to **five later slices** (1A `document-types`, 2C `templates`, 5A `tax`, 7A `reports`, 8A `statutory`), so the shape those loaders plug into is frozen here rather than left to whichever slice reads 0C's source first. Everything else about the seed CLI — its `SeedResult`, its owner-bootstrap step, its `SeedAuthAdmin` port — is 0C's alone and is not registered.

```ts
// packages/db/src/seed/index.ts, config.ts, packs.ts — reachable as `@dulja/db/seed` (§4.2.12)
export type SubPack = "roles" | "dimensions" | "fiscal-periods" | "chart-of-accounts" | "document-types" | "templates" | "tax";
export const SUB_PACKS: readonly SubPack[];        // APPLICATION order, never alphabetical

export interface SeedConfig {
  readonly tenantId: string;                 // `--tenant <uuid>`; the CLI never invents one
  readonly only: readonly SubPack[] | null;  // `--only <sub-pack>`, repeatable; null = the whole bootstrap
  readonly packRoot: string;                 // `--pack <dir>`; default packages/db/seed/my
  readonly tenantName: string; readonly ownerEmail: string;                       // OD-21
  readonly companyCode: string; readonly companyName: string;                     // OD-21
  readonly baseCurrency: string; readonly timezone: string;
  readonly fiscalYearStartMonth: number; readonly fiscalYear: number;             // OD-21; carried here, NOT a column on app.company
}

/** What `--only <sub-pack>` dispatches to. One module per sub-pack, shipped by the slice that introduces it,
 *  and exported from `packages/db/src/seed/index.ts` — reachable as `@dulja/db/seed`, NEVER from the main
 *  `packages/db/src/index.ts` barrel at any depth (§3.1, sah-039). */
export interface PackLoader { readonly name: SubPack; load(tx: Sql, ctx: LoaderContext): Promise<number> }
export interface LoaderContext {
  readonly config: SeedConfig; readonly tenantId: string; readonly companyId: string;
  readonly systemPrincipalId: string; readonly packRoot: string;
}
/** Reads and JSON-parses `<packRoot>/<sub-pack>/<file>`; throws naming the file on a parse failure. */
export function readPackFile<T>(packRoot: string, subPack: SubPack, file: string): T;
/** Fails loudly, naming the owning slice, if a pack directory a later slice owns appears early (F-21/F-23).
 *  **From 2C onward it derives its ALLOWED set from `SUB_PACKS`**, not from a second literal list — see below. */
export function assertPackShape(packRoot: string): void;
/** The directories the pack must CONTAIN. Grows with `SUB_PACKS`, minus `roles`, which is TypeScript data
 *  (`packages/db/seed/roles.ts`) and has no directory. 0C ["chart-of-accounts", "dimensions", "fiscal-periods"];
 *  + "document-types" (1A); + "templates" (2C). The name records where the list started, not what it holds. */
export const PHASE_0_SUB_PACK_DIRECTORIES: readonly string[];
```

**`SubPack` gains `"document-types"` (1A) and `"templates"` (2C) — this closes §4.18's round-1 open item 1.** 1A ships the `document-types` loader as a `PackLoader` (`documentTypesLoader`), registers it in `LOADERS`, adds the member to `SubPack` and `SUB_PACKS` (last, after `chart-of-accounts`: application order, and a policy is validated against accounts that must already exist — hazard 33), and adds `"document-types"` to `PHASE_0_SUB_PACK_DIRECTORIES`. 2C does the same five edits for `templates` **and** makes `assertPackShape` derive its allowed-directory set from `SUB_PACKS` rather than from a second literal list, so a *shipped* loader's directory can never again make `bun run seed` exit 3. `OWNED_ELSEWHERE` keeps its remaining entries and still names the owning slice for `reports` (7A) and `statutory` (8A); 5A removes `tax` as its loader lands.

**`PHASE_0_SUB_PACK_DIRECTORIES` keeps its name — settled (round 2), because 2A routed the question here.** 0C's ADR 0012 foresaw "renaming it as the pack grows" and 1A deliberately declined to rename it; **the decision is to keep the spelling and amend its meaning instead**, as the doc comment above now states: it is the *required-presence* list, widened additively by each loader-owning slice exactly as `SUB_PACKS` is, while the *allowed* set comes from `SUB_PACKS` from 2C onward. **No plan changes** — 0C's tests, 1A's five edits, 2C's five, and 2A's and 2C's consumed-interfaces lists all name the spelling that stands. The only superseded text is 0C's own ADR 0012 sentence foreseeing the rename (0c:2809), which is a doc line in a slice-owned artefact and needs no code change. A rename would have touched three frozen plans and one written one to change nothing a reader gets wrong once the comment says what the list is.

**Exit codes of `bun run seed` (frozen — the deploy workflow and the release runbook read them):** **0** success · **1** a seed failure (a loader threw, the database refused) · **2** a configuration error (a missing flag or environment variable; `DATABASE_URL` supplied where `DATABASE_URL_MIGRATOR` is required) — the CLI raises **`SeedConfigError`**, a named 0C export, and nothing else maps to exit 2 (recorded in round 4; the rest of the seed CLI is 0C's alone and stays unregistered) · **3** a pack-shape violation.

**The fiscal-year start month has no column.** It is needed once, to generate the first year's periods, and `app.company` has no field for it, so 0C carries it on `SeedConfig` and adds no column. 1A owns period close and the next year's periods and may want one; that is a migration in 1A's range and an amendment here, not a silent addition.

### 4.3 The posting service (Phase 1, generalised in Phase 2)

**Location (convention, not in spec — forced by the dependency rule):** the I/O half lives in `packages/db/src/posting/` and is exported from `@dulja/db`; the pure half (policy evaluation, balancing, base conversion) lives in `packages/domain/src/posting/`. Neither `apps/api` nor `apps/worker` contains posting logic: the API's document routes and the worker's sync-apply / payroll / recost jobs all call the same functions (spec:1360, 2081 — "exactly the same posting service").

#### 4.3.1 TypeScript signatures (`packages/db/src/posting/index.ts`)

**File layout inside `packages/db/src/posting/` (1A; 2A, 3B and later slices extend these files rather than adding siblings):** `errors.ts` (`PostingError`, §4.2.4), `load.ts` (`loadSnapshot`), `issue.ts` (`issueDocument`), `post.ts` (`postDocument`), `reverse.ts` (`reverseDocument`, `voidDocument`), `index.ts` (the barrel below) — and, added by 2B, **`lifecycle.ts`**.

**`setEventContext`'s module path is `packages/db/src/posting/lifecycle.ts` (settled, round 3).** 2B creates that sixth file and puts `setEventContext`, `transitionDocument`, `recordOverride` and `listDocumentEvents` in it (2b:71, 2b:1347); `reverse.ts` imports the helper from `./lifecycle` (2b:1491) and the barrel re-exports all four (2b:1187). The five-file list above was 1A's and was never widened when 2B landed, which is the whole of the ambiguity 6A's Task 0 gate reported — that gate deliberately greps the **barrel**, `packages/db/src/posting/index.ts`, and is unaffected by the settlement either way. Every consumer (6A's up-sync apply, 3B, 6D) imports from `@dulja/db` or from `../posting`, never from the file, so **no plan changes**; a plan that names a file for this helper names `lifecycle.ts`.

```ts
import type { Sql } from "postgres";
import type { TenantContext } from "../with-tenant";
import type { DocumentSnapshot, PostingPlan, PostingPolicy } from "@dulja/domain";

export type DocumentStatus = "draft" | "submitted" | "approved" | "issued" | "void" | "posted" | "reversed";

/** Reads the header, lines, company, party and every referenced account/item/tax code/component the policy may address. Rows are read under RLS as the caller. */
export async function loadSnapshot(tx: Sql, documentId: string): Promise<DocumentSnapshot>;               // ERR_NOT_FOUND

/** The policy effective for a document: the row of its document type with the greatest effective_from <= effectiveDate; ties broken by the highest version (spec:2172 "the policy effective for the document's effective_date"). */
export async function resolvePolicy(tx: Sql, documentTypeId: string, effectiveDate: string): Promise<{ policyId: string; definition: PostingPolicy }>;   // ERR_POLICY_NOT_FOUND

/** Assigns series/period/number under the advisory lock (spec:1741–1745). Legal only when the status trigger admits `→ issued` (§4.5.1). */
export async function issueDocument(tx: Sql, ctx: TenantContext, input: { documentId: string }): Promise<IssueResult>;
export interface IssueResult { documentId: string; series: string; fiscalPeriodId: string; number: bigint }

/**
 * Posts a document. If the document is not yet `issued` and the transition to `issued` is legal, issues it first in the
 * same transaction (two document_event rows). Steps are fixed in §4.3.2. Throws AppError codes listed in §4.3.7.
 */
export async function postDocument(tx: Sql, ctx: TenantContext, input: { documentId: string }): Promise<PostResult>;
export interface PostResult {
  documentId: string; number: bigint; series: string; fiscalPeriodId: string;
  postingPolicyId: string; postingSeq: bigint;
  ledgerEntryIds: string[]; movementIds: string[]; taxTransactionIds: string[];
  enqueuedJobIds: string[]; warnings: string[];
}

/**
 * D13: creates the reversing document of `policy.reversal.producesType` with sides swapped, posts it, and marks
 * the original `reversed`.
 *
 * **The `reversal` block is read from the policy PINNED ON THE ORIGINAL DOCUMENT** — `app.document.posting_policy_id`,
 * the column spec:1753 exists for — and **never** from `resolvePolicy(documentTypeId, original.effective_date)`
 * (2A amendment A8; the signature, the return and the error codes are unchanged). 1A shipped the second form,
 * which was safe while a policy version could arrive only through a reviewed seed PR. 2A's
 * `POST …/document-types/{documentTypeId}/policies` makes a **back-dated** `effective_from` an ordinary API call,
 * and a version whose `effective_from` falls on or before an already-posted document's `effective_date` would
 * then change what that document's reversal produces — or refuse it outright — with no write to the document.
 * That is SAH-013 verbatim: "reversal reads *current* flags, not those originally applied." `resolvePolicy` still
 * governs the reversal document's OWN posting at its OWN effective date, which is why the two documents
 * legitimately pin different policies (and why hazard 18 projects `posting_policy_id` out of test 22's multiset).
 * Every posted or reversed document has a non-null pin — §4.3.2 step 13 writes it — so there is no fallback path.
 *
 * **Refused while part of the original has already been taken back, or while an allocation still leans on it
 * (4A, round 7).** A full reversal mirrors EVERY line, so it raises `ERR_DOC_STATUS_ILLEGAL` while any non-void
 * document points `reverses_document_id` at the original (4A's partial credit note, `creditNoteFrom`), while
```
