Consumers check `exists (select 1 from app.document_event e where e.document_id = $1 and e.event_kind = 'override' and e.override_code = $2)`: `app.assert_stock_available` (3A) for negative stock, the credit-control check (4A), and the sync-apply limit check (6C) for discount/void/blind-return beyond `branch_pos_policy`.

#### 4.5.4 API

`POST /v1/companies/{companyId}/documents/{documentId}/transitions` body `{ to: "submitted" | "approved" | "issued" | "posted" | "void" | "draft", reason?: string, attributedTo?: string }` — `to = "posted"` calls `postDocument`, `to = "void"` calls `voidDocument`, the rest `transitionDocument`; the route's permission is the policy's `approval.post` for `posted`/`void`/`issued`, `approval.approve ?? approval.post` for `approved`, and `approval.create ?? approval.post` for `submitted`/`draft` and for creating or editing the draft itself — resolved per request by `requireDocumentPermission(stage)` (**2A** — see the authorship note below) which reads the effective policy; the trigger remains the control (spec:2173). `POST …/documents/{documentId}/reverse { effectiveDate, reason }` under `accounting.document.reverse` (**2B** — the route and the code land together, §2.3's 2A card and amendment A7). `POST …/documents/{documentId}/overrides { code, reason }` (§4.5.3). `DELETE …/documents/{documentId}` (drafts only). `GET …/documents/{documentId}/events` (membership + the type's module read code).

**Authorship: `DocumentStage`, `requireDocumentPermission` and `DOCUMENT_STAGE_CODES` are created by 2A, not 2B (2A amendment A4, a settlement).** This section previously read as though the middleware were 2B's, while 1A's Task 12 states **twice** that "2A replaces both static gates with `policy.approval.create` / `policy.approval.post` resolved from the effective policy". 1A's statement wins, because it is the frozen plan another writer already built against. **2A ships the file with all six `DocumentStage` members mapped**; **2B then *uses* it** for its `submitted`/`approved` transitions, adds its own `RouteModule` permissions and the `stageCode` export, and **edits the stage map never**. Wherever 2A's merged file and a later description of it disagree, 2A's file is the authority.

**`"create"` is for `POST …/documents` only; a `POST` sub-path of an existing document uses `"submit"` (3C).** The two stages resolve the **same** code — `approval.create ?? approval.post` — but `"create"` finds the policy through `body.documentTypeCode` + `body.effectiveDate` and raises `ERR_NOT_FOUND` when either is missing (2a:2897–2906), while every other stage loads the document named by `:documentId` (2a:2909–2915). So a sub-path route whose body carries no type would 404 on the gate under `"create"` and never reach its handler. 3C's `…/links` and `…/landed-cost` use `"submit"`; 3D's `…/count-sheet` and `…/links` and 4A's allocation sub-paths inherit the rule.

**A sub-path that drafts a document of ANOTHER type carries a second gate (4A, round 7).** `POST …/documents/{documentId}/convert-to-invoice` and `POST …/documents/{documentId}/credit-note` resolve `"submit"` on the **source** document's pinned policy — `DELIVERY_ORDER`'s or `GOODS_RECEIPT`'s create code for a conversion, the invoice's for a credit note — and the handler then asks the **target** type's `approval.create` through `app.actor_has` at the source's branch before anything is drafted, refusing `ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN` naming the target. Without it a principal who may ship stock could raise a sales invoice draft, and one who may raise a sale could raise its credit note; R2 still refuses the *post*, but the draft would exist. 3D's `…/convert` beside them is the precedent, and 4A's plan named this narrowing as its first self-review item. `POST …/documents/settlements` is the other way round: it drafts a document of the type its body names, so it uses `"create"` and its body carries `documentTypeCode`.

```ts
// apps/api/src/middleware/require-document-permission.ts (2A)
export type DocumentStage = "create" | "submit" | "approve" | "issue" | "post" | "void";
/**
 * Loads the document named by `:documentId` (or, for "create", the type named in the body), resolves the policy effective for its
 * `effective_date` (§4.3.1 `resolvePolicy` semantics), maps the stage to a code — create/submit → `approval.create ?? approval.post`,
 * approve → `approval.approve ?? approval.post`, issue/post/void → `approval.post` — and then calls `app.actor_has(code, company_id,
 * branch_id)` inside `c.var.withTenant`. 403 `ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN`; 404 `ERR_NOT_FOUND` when the document is invisible. Pre-flight
 * only (spec:2173): the BEFORE UPDATE OF status trigger remains the control.
 */
export function requireDocumentPermission(stage: DocumentStage): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;

/** The pure half of the stage map, exported (2B) in place of 2A's private `codeFor`, so a test can assert the
 *  map with no request and so 6C's sync apply and 8B's payroll routes resolve a stage identically.
 *  **Returns `string`, not `PermissionCode`** — a policy may legitimately name a code whose slice has not
 *  seeded it yet, and narrowing the return would make that a compile error instead of a 403. */
export function stageCode(stage: DocumentStage, approval: PostingPolicy["approval"]): string;

/** **2A.** The `PERMISSION[...]` references that keep the bidirectional `permission-catalogue` lint (§3.6.3)
 *  satisfied for gates resolved from *data*, which no source scan can see. `DOCUMENT_STAGE_CODES` is
 *  initialised from it, and every type-seeding slice appends its own `approval.*` codes to it. Without this
 *  constant a policy-resolved code has no reference and the lint fails on the slice that seeded it. */
export const POLICY_RESOLVED_CODES: readonly PermissionCode[];

// apps/api/src/routes/accounting/documents.ts
/** `RouteModule.permissions` for the documents module: the union of every code any seeded type's policy may name at any stage.
 *  It cannot be derived from source (the code is resolved from data), so it is an explicit constant **initialised from
 *  `POLICY_RESOLVED_CODES`** — a literal array over that line would leave the middleware's `PERMISSION[…]`
 *  references unreferenced, which is exactly the finding the constant exists to prevent. Every slice that seeds a
 *  document type adds its `approval.*` codes here in the same PR as its policy file — that is what keeps the
 *  `permission-catalogue` lint (§3.6.3) satisfied for policy-resolved codes. */
export const DOCUMENT_STAGE_CODES: readonly PermissionCode[];
```

**2C appends nothing to `DOCUMENT_STAGE_CODES`** — `CONSIGNMENT_RETURN`'s `approval.post` is already `accounting.journal.post`. 2B appends nothing either, for the same reason. The first slice that genuinely extends it is 3C.

**A document *read* is gated by membership plus the type's module read code** (§4.5.8's `MODULE_READ_CODE`), not by this middleware: `requireDocumentPermission` maps write stages only. Printing therefore reuses the attachment download map and lives in the same file, which keeps that map at one home for 3A to widen. Listing `accounting.ledger.read` statically on the print `POST` would trip `ERR_ROUTE_GATE_READONLY` at boot (§3.6.3), and so would the middleware gate on its own — `assertRouteGates` judges every gate mark alike. The print route boots because `requireDocumentModuleRead({ writeFree: true })` marks its gate with `markWriteFreeGate` and `REPLAY_BY_RERUN` lists it (§4.2.5, §4.2.9; round 10, ⚠️ owner review).

#### 4.5.5 Gapless proof (2B; spec:2222, 2288)

```sql
create function app.series_gaps(p_company uuid, p_series text, p_period uuid)
returns table (number bigint) language sql stable as $$
  select g.n from app.document_series s
  cross join lateral generate_series(1, s.next_number - 1) as g(n)
  where s.company_id = p_company and s.series = p_series and s.fiscal_period_id = p_period
    and not exists (select 1 from app.document d where d.company_id = p_company and d.series = p_series and d.fiscal_period_id = p_period and d.number = g.n)
    and not exists (select 1 from app.document_number_void v where v.company_id = p_company and v.series = p_series and v.fiscal_period_id = p_period and v.number = g.n)
$$;
```

Zero rows for every `(company, series, period)` is the DoD proof; the 1B integrity job reports any non-empty result **through `SERIES_GAP_CHECK`, a registered `ProjectionCheck` (§4.16.3)**. A gapless assertion is only non-vacuous against a document type whose **policy** names the series, because `issueDocument` writes `policy.numbering.series` back onto the header (§4.3.6) — which is why 2B's numbering tests configure types (`GAP_TEST`, `NG_NG`/`NG_RC`/`NG_HT`) rather than setting a series on a header.

#### 4.5.6 `app.actor_in_branch` and `branch_isolation` (6C, migration 0068; spec:1566–1569, 2166)

```sql
create function app.actor_in_branch(p_company_id uuid, p_branch_id uuid) returns boolean language sql stable as $$
  select exists (select 1 from app.principal p join app.membership m on m.principal_id = p.id
                  where p.id = app.current_actor() and p.kind = 'system' and m.tenant_id = app.current_tenant())
      or exists (select 1 from app.role_assignment ra
                  where ra.principal_id = app.current_actor() and ra.company_id = p_company_id and (ra.expires_at is null or ra.expires_at > now())
                    and (not exists (select 1 from app.role_assignment_branch b where b.principal_id = ra.principal_id and b.role_id = ra.role_id and b.company_id = ra.company_id)
                         or exists (select 1 from app.role_assignment_branch b where b.principal_id = ra.principal_id and b.role_id = ra.role_id and b.company_id = ra.company_id and b.branch_id = p_branch_id)))
$$;
-- Stock lives in warehouses, not branches: the stock tables carry warehouse_id and no branch column. This helper resolves
-- the warehouse's branch and binds the supplied company. Both this predicate and app.warehouse's OWN policy
-- (Form A″ below) admit in-transit rows; admitting only one still blocks legitimate transfer receipts.
create function app.actor_in_warehouse(p_company_id uuid, p_warehouse_id uuid) returns boolean language sql stable as $$
  select exists (select 1 from app.warehouse w
                  where w.id = p_warehouse_id and w.company_id = p_company_id
                    and (w.kind = 'in_transit' or app.actor_in_branch(w.company_id, w.branch_id)))
$$;
```

**Migration 0068 attaches exactly five branch/stock policy forms — A, A″, A′, B, C — in one file.** Every branch/stock policy is named `branch_isolation` and is `AS RESTRICTIVE`. The parent-visibility guard on `document_line`, registered below, is a separate aggregate-child policy, not a sixth branch form. Form A on `terminal_enrolment` is restricted to the two application data roles to preserve its hash-bound pre-tenant resolver.

```sql
-- FORM A — a NOT NULL branch key. Tables: document, pos_terminal, pos_cashier, branch_pos_policy, attendance_event, terminal_enrolment, needs_attention;
-- 6D adds shift and till_event in 0070; every later table with a NOT NULL branch_id takes it in its own migration (§3.5.1 step 7).
create policy branch_isolation on app.<table> as restrictive using (app.actor_in_branch(company_id, branch_id));
-- terminal_enrolment is the sole role-scoped Form A instance: app_auth's pre-tenant resolver must retain
-- its existing app_auth-only SELECT grant and enrolment_resolver policy. No BYPASSRLS or table exemption.
create policy branch_isolation on app.terminal_enrolment as restrictive to app_rw, app_migrator
  using (app.actor_in_branch(company_id, branch_id));

-- FORM A″ — app.warehouse, which is Form A PLUS the in-transit exception, and must be written this way or nothing else works.
-- An in-transit warehouse has a NOT NULL branch_id like any other (§4.6.1), so under plain Form A it is visible only to its own
-- branch. But a two-step transfer is precisely a dispatch from branch A into in-transit and a receipt by branch B (spec:2160
-- gives branch_manager "receiving transfers"), and app.actor_in_warehouse below reads app.warehouse — so if the in-transit row
-- is hidden from B, B's `exists` returns false and every movement, layer and stock_on_hand row against it is refused. The
-- exception belongs on the warehouse row itself AND inside actor_in_warehouse, where the company is bound.
create policy branch_isolation on app.warehouse as restrictive
  using (kind = 'in_transit' or app.actor_in_branch(company_id, branch_id));

-- FORM A′ — employee, whose branch key is named home_branch_id (only if migration 0064 already ran; otherwise 0064's own
-- conditional block attaches it, §4.6.2).
create policy branch_isolation on app.employee as restrictive to app_rw, app_migrator
  using (app.actor_in_branch(company_id, home_branch_id));

-- FORM B — a NULLABLE branch key, where NULL means "every branch". Tables: price_list, promotion, catalogue_tombstone; 8D's public_holiday takes
-- it in 0096. NULL must be VISIBLE, not denied: app.actor_in_branch(company_id, null) is false for every branch-restricted
-- principal, so Form A would hide the head-office price list and every company-wide promotion from exactly the principals
-- that need them — the branch_manager, the cashier and the terminal, all of which have role_assignment_branch rows by
-- construction (R8) — and the catalogue down-sync (§4.10.2) would silently omit them.
create policy branch_isolation on app.<table> as restrictive using (branch_id is null or app.actor_in_branch(company_id, branch_id));

-- FORM C — stock, keyed by warehouse. Tables: inventory_movement, stock_on_hand, cost_layer, stock_valuation.
create policy branch_isolation on app.<table> as restrictive using (app.actor_in_warehouse(company_id, warehouse_id));
-- cost_consumption has no warehouse_id; it reaches one through its movement:
create policy branch_isolation on app.cost_consumption as restrictive
  using (exists (select 1 from app.inventory_movement m where m.id = movement_id and app.actor_in_warehouse(m.company_id, m.warehouse_id)));
```

**`document_line` has no branch column and receives a separate parent-visibility policy.** A composite FK guarantees referential integrity; PostgreSQL's FK checks bypass RLS and do not guarantee parent visibility. Migration 0068 therefore adds the following restrictive guard for reads and writes (Phase 6 integration correction, 2026-10-08, proposed ADR 0062 amendment). It binds tenant, company and document ID to a parent visible under its existing policies; UPDATE/reparenting must satisfy both the old-row `using` and new-row `with check`. The schema linter requires the guard separately from the five branch/stock forms; the down migration drops it. The resulting register has seventeen branch/stock policies plus this one child policy, eighteen in all. Direct app_rw tests cover cross-branch SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and reparenting, including a hidden draft parent whose status the frozen-line trigger cannot read.

```sql
create policy document_parent_visibility on app.document_line as restrictive
  using (exists (select 1 from app.document d
                  where d.tenant_id = document_line.tenant_id and d.company_id = document_line.company_id
                    and d.id = document_line.document_id))
  with check (exists (select 1 from app.document d
                       where d.tenant_id = document_line.tenant_id and d.company_id = document_line.company_id
                         and d.id = document_line.document_id));
```

**Why Form C exists at all.** 6C owns test 36's assertion that a `branch_manager` at A cannot reach B's **stock** (spec:2454 forbids the leak "through any endpoint, filter or export"), and none of `inventory_movement`, `stock_on_hand`, `cost_layer`, `cost_consumption` or `stock_valuation` carries a branch column — `warehouse.branch_id` is the only branch key in the inventory model. Without Form C, `select * from app.stock_on_hand` under `withTenant` as a branch_manager at A returns branch B's stock. 3A and 3B create these tables branch-ready (that is, with `warehouse_id NOT NULL`) and attach nothing; 0068 attaches all of it in one file, so 6C needs no extra migration number. **6A's three tables are attached in 0068 like every other pre-0068 table; 6A creates them branch-ready and attaches nothing (§3.5.1 step 7).** `terminal_enrolment` and `needs_attention` carry `branch_id uuid not null` (Form A); `catalogue_tombstone` carries nullable `branch_id uuid` (Form B), so company-wide deletions reach every terminal.

**Read Form A″ and Form C together — they are one mechanism.** `actor_in_warehouse` performs an ordinary RLS-bound lookup, so Form A″ must expose an in-transit warehouse and the function must also admit it while binding `p_company_id`. Either missing exception blocks a legitimate cross-branch transfer receipt. This preserves 3D's DoD clause "goods in transit are in neither warehouse's on-hand and **in the company's total**". No SECURITY DEFINER or BYPASSRLS is introduced; ordinary tenant isolation still constrains the lookup. Prove both cross-branch receipt and cross-company/tenant refusal, alongside ordinary branch-stock hiding.

**Note — the cross-branch receipt proof, Phase 6 plan audit, 2026-10-23 (ADR 0062's amendment of that date).** The proof asked for above is met at the predicate level and for the dispatch's post, and not for a receipt by the receiving branch. ADR 0043 puts the corridor at the receiving branch, so the in-transit exception is what admits the SENDING branch: a principal restricted to A posts a dispatch into B's corridor. No principal restricted to one branch can complete an inter-branch transfer. The dispatch is stamped with the sending branch, so Form A on `document` hides its header from the receiving branch, `document_parent_visibility` hides its lines, and Form A's WITH CHECK refuses a receipt stamped with that branch. Form A″ hides the destination stock warehouse from the sending branch. 3D's create gate on `POST …/documents/transfers` asks for authority at no branch. The "after 0068" cases in `packages/db/test/inventory/transfer-receipt.test.ts` and `apps/api/test/routes/accounting/document-transfer.test.ts` pin this, beside the controls: a company-wide principal, or one granted both branches, completes the receipt. Which branch gates and stamps a receipt, and how the receiving branch reads the dispatch without a `SECURITY DEFINER` or a permissive policy, are the owner's questions in ADR 0043's proposed amendment of the same date. No policy here changes until the owner decides. **2026-11-04: the owner approved that amendment with every recommended default, and migration 0119 implements it** (§3.4.1's tail):
- The receiving branch stamps and gates the receipt.
- Form A on `document` gains one read-only case: `using (app.actor_in_branch(company_id, branch_id) or (status = 'posted' and exists (… w.id = document.to_warehouse_id and w.kind = 'in_transit' and app.actor_in_branch(w.company_id, w.branch_id))))`. Its `with check` is the original predicate.
- `document_parent_visibility` keeps its `using`, and its `with check` asks that the parent pass `app.actor_in_branch(d.company_id, d.branch_id)`, so that a line is written only under a parent the actor may write.
- Form A″ keeps its `using` and is scoped `to app_rw, app_migrator`, as Form A′ and `terminal_enrolment`'s Form A are. This lets the bounded, `app_auth`-owned `app.transfer_destination_branch(company, warehouse)` give the sending branch the branch of a destination it cannot see.
- The dispatch's create gate asks at the source warehouse's branch.

The register still counts nineteen `branch_isolation` policies plus the one child guard. The "after 0068 and 0119" cases in the two files above now prove the receipt by the receiving branch, and that every write path from it onto the dispatch is refused. ADR 0043's *Implementation* section and ADR 0062's note of the same date record the detail.

Phases 1–5 rely on `actor_has(code, company_id, branch_id)` in handlers and triggers only (F-18); 6C attaches the row-level policies and re-runs test 36's branch-scoping assertions over documents, stock, shifts, attendance and tickets.

#### 4.5.7 `app.party` (2A, migration 0017; spec:1169, 1759; convention for columns)

```sql
create table app.party (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  kind text not null check (kind in ('customer', 'vendor', 'employee', 'student', 'dealer')),      -- student/dealer reserved (F-16)
  code text not null, name_en text not null, name_ar text,
  receivable_account_id uuid, payable_account_id uuid,                                            -- policy paths party.receivable_account / party.payable_account
  currency char(3),                                                                               -- statement currency; null = base
  tax_registration text, email text, phone text, address jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  archived_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (company_id, code), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, receivable_account_id) references app.account(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, payable_account_id) references app.account(tenant_id, id));
call app_meta.enable_tenant_rls('app.party'); call app_meta.attach_audit('app.party');
alter table app.document add constraint document_party_fk foreign key (tenant_id, party_id) references app.party(tenant_id, id);   -- migration 0018_alter_document_party_fk_and_document_type_module.sql (spec:1759); the same file carries the document_type additions of §4.3.4
```

4A adds `credit_limit numeric(19,4)`, `payment_term_id uuid`, `credit_hold boolean not null default false` (migration 0045); 9B adds `legacy_ref text`. **4A's file is `0045_alter_party_and_document_add_credit_terms.sql`** (§3.4.2's rename rule — it also adds `document.payment_term_id` and creates `app.assert_credit_available()`), and `payment_term_id` carries the composite FK `(tenant_id, payment_term_id) → app.payment_term(tenant_id, id)` (4A amendment 6, round 7).

**The fourth 4A column is 6B's request, not 4A's own idea:** **`price_list_id uuid`, nullable, with the composite FK `(tenant_id, price_list_id) → app.price_list(tenant_id, id)`, added by the same migration 0045**. It is registered here because 4A owns the customer's commercial terms and a price list is one of them, and because the column has to exist before the slice that reads it: 6B's Task 0 amendment **A10(b)** names `app.party.price_list_id` as the key §3.7.6's *customer-specific pricing* has nothing to resolve on — `app.price_list.customer_kind` is the trade *level* (3A) and no column ties a party to a list — and names **4A's 0045** as the file that adds it. 6A down-syncs `party` (customers) as a catalogue stream and 6B mirrors this column into `catalogue_customer`; until it exists, 6B's price resolution falls back to branch-then-company-wide and the row cannot close. **This amendment lands in 4A's Task 0 rather than 6B's** because 4A executes in Phase 4 and 6B in Phase 6, and 4A's Global Constraint 13 forbids a task writing a literal into a register that does not yet hold it — 0045 is written in 4A's Task 3, two phases before 6B's own Task 0 could amend the register. 6B's A10(b) is unchanged and stays true; when 6B runs, the sentence it asks for is already here.

#### 4.5.8 `app.attachment` (2C, migration 0025; spec:1067, 1138; convention for columns)

**6C amendment A11.** 6C adds **no** row to `MODULE_READ_CODE`: the HR attachment read mapping remains `hr.payroll.read` owned by 8B, and the POS mapping is `pos.report.read` owned by 6D. Employee-directory read authority must not be substituted for either.

```sql
create table app.attachment (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  document_id uuid,                                              -- lot_id uuid added by 3A (0031)
  object_key text not null unique,                               -- '<tenant_id>/<id>' — server-generated (SAH-038); never a client path
  file_name text not null, mime_type text not null, byte_size bigint not null check (byte_size >= 0), sha256 bytea not null,
  uploaded_by uuid not null default app.current_actor() references app.principal(id),   -- stamped
  archived_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, document_id) references app.document(tenant_id, id));
call app_meta.enable_tenant_rls('app.attachment'); call app_meta.attach_audit('app.attachment'); call app_meta.attach_stamp('app.attachment', 'uploaded_by');
```

Download gate = the read code of the owning module: `document_type.module` → `accounting → accounting.ledger.read`, `inventory → inventory.stock.read`, `hr → hr.payroll.read`, `pos → pos.report.read`; a lot attachment → `inventory.item.read`. Upload `POST /v1/companies/{companyId}/attachments` (multipart; the server computes `sha256` and the R2 key); download `GET …/attachments/{attachmentId}/content`. Export (7C) includes attachments by `object_key`.

**The frozen names behind that sentence (2C).** The map itself is **`MODULE_READ_CODE`**, a `Readonly<Record<DocumentTypeModule, PermissionCode>>` in **`apps/api/src/middleware/require-attachment-read.ts`** — the file 2C shipped (2c:1786, 2c:4903), and where 3A added its `inventory` row; this paragraph used to name `apps/api/src/routes/accounting/attachments.ts`, which **imports** the map and declares none (corrected in round 7, 4A for 2C; round 3's 3C row and 6D's amendment A18 record the same correction). It is **the one home of the map**, and 3A, 6D and 8B each add one row to it rather than declaring a second. (2B's `MODULE_READ_CODE` inside `documents.ts` is a *local* precedent with the same name and a different scope; **2C owns the shared map and must not import 2B's, and no slice may merge the two without amending this paragraph** — two spellings of one map is hazard 32.) Beside it: **`requireAttachmentRead()`**, which resolves the row, applies the map and sets `AppEnv["Variables"].attachment` (§4.2.3); **`readableModules()`**, which returns the modules the caller may see; and, for the print route, **`requireDocumentModuleRead()`**, which sets `documentModule`. **What the merged tree holds, checked in round 7:** `requireAttachmentRead` and `requireDocumentModuleRead` are in the same middleware file as the map, beside 3A's `LOT_READ_CODE`; **`readableModules()` was not shipped as an export anywhere** — the list's row-level gate is `listAttachments`' required `readCodes` parameter (the next paragraph's `modules`), to which the route passes `MODULE_READ_CODE` itself. Round 7 records the difference and renames nothing; a slice that wants the name back adds it to that file.

**The attachment LIST needs two gates, not one.** §4.5.8 gates the download because attachment *identity* is a side channel, and the list returns `fileName`, `byteSize`, `sha256`, `uploadedBy` and `objectKey` for a caller-supplied `companyId` while RLS is only tenant-scoped. So the list carries `requirePermission(PERMISSION["accounting.ledger.read"], { company: "path:companyId" })` — legal on a `GET` under R7 — **and** filters its rows through `readableModules()`. `listAttachments`' `modules` parameter is **required, never defaulted**, for exactly that reason: forgetting it is a type error, not a silent unfiltered list. This is what keeps §4.14's test-32 claim true when 8B adds `hr → hr.payroll.read`. **Amended by the Phase 8 review (2026-11-08, item R2 below Round 19):** when `?documentId=` names a document of the path company, the list's company gate asks **that document's module read code** from `MODULE_READ_CODE` at its branch — the code the download gate asks — instead of `accounting.ledger.read`; with no document named it still asks `accounting.ledger.read`.

**The store is a port (2C, ADR 0031 — a proposal).** `ObjectStore` in `packages/db/src/attachment/object-store.ts`, with `MemoryObjectStore` (tests, `bun run dev`) and `R2ObjectStore` (the container) as its two implementations and `objectStoreFromConfig` choosing between them from the four §3.11 R2 names. It is `AppDeps`' sixth member (§4.2.7) because `POST …/attachments` writes the **object before its row** and the store must be swappable; `objectKeyFor` derives the key from the ids alone, so a client path can never reach it (SAH-038).

**The map is built one module at a time, in the slice that introduces the code.** `PermissionCode` is derived from `PERMISSIONS` (§4.2.5), so `PERMISSION["hr.payroll.read"]` is a compile error before 8B seeds it and the `permission-catalogue` lint fails on a reference naming no catalogue code (§3.6.3). At 2C only `accounting.ledger.read` exists, so **2C ships the `accounting` row and a default deny** (`ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN` for any other module value — a document type of another module cannot exist yet either, since `document_type.module` defaults to `'accounting'`, §4.3.4). The one-line edit adding a module's row is then owned by the slice that seeds that module's read code: **3A** adds `inventory → inventory.stock.read` and the lot rule with `inventory.item.read`; **6D** adds `pos → pos.report.read`; **8B** adds `hr → hr.payroll.read`. Each is listed in that slice's Delivers.

#### 4.5.9 `app.print_template` (2C, migration 0026; spec:1240 "text-defined, diffable, version-controlled")

```sql
create table app.print_template (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  document_type_id uuid not null, code text not null, name_en text not null, name_ar text,
  version int not null check (version > 0),
  engine text not null,                          -- the value set is fixed by ADR 0016 (PDF engine)
  source text not null,                          -- the template text
  paper text not null default 'A4' check (paper in ('A4','A5','receipt')),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (document_type_id, code, version), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, document_type_id) references app.document_type(tenant_id, id));
```

**`paper`'s value set is `A4 | A5 | receipt`** (2C, as `PaperSchema` in `packages/contracts/src/accounting/print-template.ts`). It is a closed vocabulary in the sense of §4.14 and §4.16, and is registered here so **7A's `layout.paper` (§4.11.1) uses the same three tokens** and no slice invents a fourth without amending this line. `version > 0` is the second CHECK 2C's migration ships; **a template is never deleted and never archived — a new `version` supersedes** (§3.5.4 is unchanged by this slice).

**One consequence of the uniqueness key, stated once.** `unique (document_type_id, code, version)` and `document_type` is tenant-scoped, not company-scoped — so within a tenant a given type + code + version exists exactly once, and `company_id` records which company owns it. The resolver therefore matches on `company_id` as well, and a second company that wants a different body for the same type uses **its own `code`** (`standard-hq`, say). Changing that shape is an amendment here, not a plan decision.

**The engine CHECK admits three ADR-0016 codes and 2C ships two adapters, deliberately.** `react-pdf` renders a component, not template text, so `engineFor` raises `ERR_PRINT_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED` (422) for it — ADR 0032 records the reasoning. **If ADR 0016's Decision row names `react-pdf`, templates cannot ship at all** (spec:1240 wants text-defined and diffable) — that is ADR 0016's own "no candidate passes" branch and an owner decision, not a plan change. Determinism is pinned at the **rendered-template-text** layer, never at the byte layer: Chromium embeds a `CreationDate`, so no test asserts byte-identical PDFs.

Seeded from `packages/db/seed/my/templates/<TYPE>.<code>.v<N>.<ext>` through the `templates` sub-pack loader §3.4.8 assigns 2C (§4.2.13); render `POST /v1/companies/{companyId}/documents/{documentId}/print { templateCode?, lang: "en" | "ar" }` → **synchronous** `200 application/pdf` for a single document (no job name, so `JOBS` stays closed and 2C needs no worker) — its idempotency behaviour is `REPLAY_BY_RERUN`'s one member (§4.2.9). Batch and catalogue rendering is 7A's `reporting.render` job. Both directions verified (test 23), asserted at the PDF text layer through §4.17.1's `pdfText`.

**`PAYSLIP_ENGINE: PrintEngineCode` in `apps/api/src/print/payslip.ts` (8D A11, round 19)** — the ADR-0016 code a payslip renders through. 2C's print route reads its engine off `print_template.engine` and a payslip has no template row; 2C exports no engine-choice function; hazard 30 forbids an environment read. So the choice is a named constant in one place, `"chromium"` (the only member of `PrintEngineCode` in the tree), changed in one line if ADR 0016's Decision names another.
### 4.6 Table register — every table beyond migration 0001, its slice and compact columns

Column form: `name type [constraints]`. Every table below also carries `id uuid primary key default uuidv7()` (unless in `NO_ID_TABLES`, §3.5.3), `tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id)`, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()` (unless exempt), `unique (tenant_id, id)`, composite FKs to every tenant-scoped parent, `call app_meta.enable_tenant_rls(...)`, `attach_audit` unless exempt, `attach_stamp` for every `*_by`, and — for a table with a branch key, or one of the five stock tables of §4.5.6 Form C, from 6C — the matching `branch_isolation` form of §4.5.6. (A `warehouse_id` alone does **not** attract the policy: `document_line` has one and must not carry it.) Tables already given in full above are referenced, not repeated.

**`item_profitability`'s home and its sale-type membership (4B amendment 6, round 8).** **`packages/db/src/projections/item-profitability.ts` is the home of `item_profitability`'s rebuild and read**, and **`app.item_profitability_rows(p_company uuid, p_sale_types text[])`** (migration 0048) is the one definition of its arithmetic — the rebuild `MERGE`s from it and the nightly compare full-outer-joins the stored table against it. The **sale-type membership** is **`SALE_MOVEMENT_TYPES`**, a `readonly string[]` in that module — `["DELIVERY_ORDER", "SALES_INVOICE", "SALES_CREDIT_NOTE"]` at 4B, **`"POS_TICKET"` appended by 6A** — with a companion **`NON_SALE_MOVEMENT_TYPES`** and an exhaustiveness test that fails when a *seeded* document type with a stock effect appears in neither list, so the slice that adds a type must classify it. **Membership means "a sale document", not "a document with a movement":** under 4A's ADR 0044 (§4.14, round 7) `SALES_INVOICE` and `SALES_CREDIT_NOTE` are financial-only in every case, linked or not, so two of the three members carry no movement and are members for their revenue alone. **It is membership only and carries no sign**: the direction of revenue is read from the ledger per document (amendment 7) and the direction of quantity and cost from the movement's own sign. At 4B the ledger read and 4A's convention agree on every seeded path — 4A writes a credit note's magnitudes negated whether `reverseDocument` or `creditNoteFrom` produced it (§4.8.1, §4.16.3, round 7) — and the ledger read is kept because a type → sign map would be right for 4A's credit notes and wrong for a document whose magnitudes are not negated: a tenant's own zero-code return type (test 15), or 6A's `POS_TICKET` return.

**`item_profitability`'s attribution, in three sentences (4B amendment 7, round 8).** `quantity_sold` = `Σ −inventory_movement.quantity` over the sale documents' movements, so an issue adds and a return subtracts. `cogs_base` = per movement, `Σ cost_consumption.value` for an issue and `−(cost_layer.qty_in × unit_cost)` for a receipt, both `where invalidated_at is null` — **the same `cost_consumption` source 3D's `salesByItem` chose over `document_line.cost`, for 3D's reason: only consumptions and layers are rewritten by `inventory.cost.replay`, so a projection reading `document_line.cost` would show the pre-recost figure for ever.** `revenue_base` = `m × Σ round(document_line.amount × document.exchange_rate, 4)` over the document's item lines, **each line keeping its own sign**, where `m = doc_sign × sign(Σ document_line.amount)` over those lines and `doc_sign` is `+1` unless the document's ledger rows on the **item's own `revenue_account_id`** net to a debit, in which case `−1` (**corrected in round 8 by 4B Task 4**: this sentence first read `doc_sign × Σ round(abs(document_line.amount) × …)`, which adds a negative-quantity line's revenue to an invoice instead of subtracting it — 325be17 made that line legal — and so broke consequence (1) below on a mixed-sign document; migration 0048 was written with the sign-keeping form, which equals the `abs()` form on every single-sign document); a document with no such ledger row (a `DELIVERY_ORDER`, which posts to `1250`) contributes quantity and cost and **no revenue**, and a `SALES_INVOICE` — which under ADR 0044 never carries a movement — contributes revenue and no quantity, which is exactly how the two-document path lands both halves on one `(item, period)` row. **Two consequences of 4A's landed text, stated so no later slice re-derives them.** (1) On 4A's documents `revenue_base` equals 4A's `sales_by_item` `revenue` (§4.16.3: `Σ round(document_line.amount × document.exchange_rate, 4)`, the negated magnitudes doing the subtraction), because `round` is symmetric at scale 4 — which is what lets 7B re-express that report over this projection unchanged. (2) 4A's `SALES_INVOICE` posts the **ledger** COGS leg (`item.cogs_account` debit, `1250` credit at `line.cost`), while `cogs_base` is cut on the **delivery's** consumption; the two are the same figure when the invoice posts (4A's conversion copies the delivery's `document_line.cost` onto the invoice line, §4.7.2) and fall in one `(item, fiscal_period)` row only when delivery and invoice share a period — absent a later recost, the difference in any period is that period's movement on `1250`, exactly the "cut on different documents" statement §4.16.3 makes for `sales_by_item`; a later recost moves `cogs_base` and posts its own difference through 3B's `COST_ADJUSTMENT`, never through the invoice. The invoice's COGS debit never moves `doc_sign`, which reads the item's revenue account alone.

#### 4.6.2 The minimal `employee` table — fixed DDL (`0064_create_employee_minimal.sql`; spec:2075; F-7/C14 resolved)

Whichever of 6C and 8A executes first commits **exactly this file** under version 0064; the other plan's task is "assert `listApplied()` includes 64 and the fingerprint of `app.employee` matches" and creates nothing.

```sql
-- 0064_create_employee_minimal.sql — §3.10.1 "Employee master", the minimal master (spec:2075); cashiers are employees (spec:2097).
create table app.employee (
  id               uuid primary key default uuidv7(),
  tenant_id        uuid not null references app.tenant(id),
  company_id       uuid not null,
  party_id         uuid not null,                                  -- 1:1 with a party of kind 'employee'
  employee_number  text not null,
  home_branch_id   uuid not null,                                  -- BRANCH dimension value (spec:2075)
  principal_id     uuid unique references app.principal(id),       -- nullable 1:1: only staff who log in or sell (spec:2097)
  hired_on         date not null,
  terminated_on    date,                                           -- AFTER UPDATE OF terminated_on trigger arrives with 8C (migration 0093)
  created_at       timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (company_id, employee_number),
  unique (party_id),
  unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id)     references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, party_id)       references app.party(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, home_branch_id) references app.dimension_value(tenant_id, id)
);
call app_meta.enable_tenant_rls('app.employee');
call app_meta.attach_audit('app.employee');
-- branch_isolation is attached by 0068 (6C) if this file ran before it, or here if 0068 already exists:
do $$ begin
  if exists (select 1 from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'app' and p.proname = 'actor_in_branch') then
    execute 'create policy branch_isolation on app.employee as restrictive to app_rw, app_migrator using (app.actor_in_branch(company_id, home_branch_id))';
  end if;
end $$;
```

**Alternate-order role reconciliation.** The conditional 0064 employee policy
uses the same `TO app_rw, app_migrator` clause as 0068's Form A′. This preserves
the registered app_auth linked-cashier resolver regardless of whether 0064 or
0068 runs first, while retaining existing tenant isolation and restrictive
home-branch checks for application/migration actors. No other 0064 DDL changes;
the runtime remains byte-identical to this owning block, with both orders tested.

`0064.down.sql`: `drop table if exists app.employee;`. Reads are gated by `hr.employee.read` (6C code); writes by `hr.employee.manage`. The `party` row is created first (kind `employee`), then the employee row — one transaction (§5.1 #12: one party + one employee per person).

#### 4.6.3 `app.pos_cashier` (6C, migration 0065; spec:1324, 2097)

**6C company-bound staff writers and branch gates.** The registered signatures are
`linkEmployeePrincipal(tx: Sql, companyId: string, employeeId: string, principalId: string): Promise<void>`,
`getCashier(tx: Sql, companyId: string, principalId: string)`,
`setCashierPin(tx: Sql, companyId: string, principalId: string, pinHash: string)` and
`revokeCashier(tx: Sql, companyId: string, principalId: string)`.
Each query binds the gated company as well as the resource ID and current tenant.
Employee linking locks and validates an active, unlinked employee and an active
actual BRANCH in the same company before `AuthAdmin.createUser`; invalid requests
must never create provider users. Staff route gates mark their existing code and
require it on at least one actual company BRANCH, admitting branch-only managers;
per-resource branch permission checks and restrictive RLS remain mandatory.
`listEmployees` additionally filters each row through `app.actor_has('hr.employee.read', company_id, home_branch_id)` and `listCashiers` through `app.actor_has('pos.cashier.manage_pin', company_id, branch_id)` before LIMIT/cursor. A blank unrelated role at another branch must not expand a code-gated directory. By-ID and mutation paths retain their actual resource-branch code check. No signature or permission is added.
This does not widen administration routes or add a permission.
Attendance and branch-policy modules use the same marked scoped-any-actual-company-BRANCH gate for their existing codes, so a branch-only grant reaches its own branch. Attendance reads retain `hr.employee.read`, writes `hr.attendance.record`; branch-policy reads/upserts retain `admin.company.manage`. Writes/upserts additionally check that existing code on the actual target branch. `listAttendance` and `listBranchPosPolicies` apply their matching read-code predicate per row before LIMIT/cursor, so unrelated empty-code scope at B cannot widen a code held only at A. No code, role grant or administration-directory endpoint is changed.

The existing `lockTenantAuditSerial` is additively exported by the DB main barrel, with its signature and lock namespace unchanged. Onboarding acquires that tenant lock before employee FOR UPDATE and the bounded provider call, preserving audit/row lock order and serializing duplicate hires. No duplicate SQL lock helper is introduced.

**6C linked-cashier identity reconciliation (2026-10-09).** Migration 0068 adds `app.resolve_cashier_employee(p_company_id uuid, p_branch_id uuid, p_principal_id uuid) returns table(employee_id uuid, employee_number text)`: STABLE SECURITY DEFINER owned by `app_auth`, fixed `search_path = app, pg_temp`, PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked, `app_rw` EXECUTE granted. It joins the live cashier to its employee by tenant, company and ID, binds `app.current_tenant()` plus the supplied company, credential branch and principal, requires `app.actor_in_branch(company, branch)`, and returns only the linked ID and employee number. It has no directory or payroll projection. `app_auth` gains only SELECT columns required for that projection and its scope predicate: employee `(id, tenant_id, company_id, employee_number)`; pos_cashier `(principal_id, tenant_id, company_id, employee_id, branch_id, revoked_at)`; role_assignment `(tenant_id, principal_id, role_id, company_id, expires_at)`; role_assignment_branch `(tenant_id, principal_id, role_id, company_id, branch_id)`. Existing tenant isolation remains effective on every relation; no additional permissive policy, BYPASSRLS, application flag or role is introduced. Employee Form A′ applies to `app_rw, app_migrator`, preserving their home-branch directory boundary; the internal resolver is current-tenant bound and explicitly credential-branch bound.

Before 0068, the cashier stream derives `employee_number` through an ordinary tenant/company-bound employee join. In 0068 it uses the resolver so an allowed credential branch different from the employee’s home branch still receives its cashier’s number. Down restores the earlier stream and removes only the new resolver and its column grants before dropping branch predicates. `recordAttendance` retains its single writer and adds optional server-only `cashierPrincipalId` to `RecordAttendanceInput`; the signed seam passes the verified cashier. Its terminal path binds the live terminal to the current actor, company and branch, resolves only that cashier’s linked employee and checks the requested employee ID. The back-office path keeps its visible-employee insert-select. No wire actor, employee-directory access, second attendance writer or new stream is added. Positive tests pin column privileges, tenant/company/branch scope, revoked cashiers, and catalogue/clock success when home and credential branches differ.

**6C amendment A5.** `CASHIER_SNAPSHOT_CODES` in `packages/contracts/permissions.ts` derives every permission whose module is `pos` except codes starting with `pos.sync.`. Its SQL twin selects `app.permission` with `module = 'pos' and code not like 'pos.sync.%'`. The projection uses the existing permission evaluator, has one refresh writer, and gains later POS codes automatically; a test asserts the two derived code sets match.

```sql
create table app.pos_cashier (
  principal_id     uuid primary key references app.principal(id),   -- keyed on the human principal (spec:2097); no separate id (joins NO_ID_TABLES)
  tenant_id        uuid not null references app.tenant(id),
  company_id       uuid not null,
  employee_id      uuid not null,
  branch_id        uuid not null,
  pin_hash         text not null,                                    -- Argon2id PHC string, per-cashier salt (spec:1324); written only by the PIN endpoints
  pin_updated_at   timestamptz not null default now(),
  snapshot         jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,               -- projection: { "codes": [permission codes at this branch], "limits": { branch_pos_policy row }, "revision": bigint }
  snapshot_at      timestamptz,
  revision         bigint not null default 0,                        -- catalogue revision (§4.10.2)
  revoked_at       timestamptz,
  created_at       timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (tenant_id, principal_id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id)  references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, employee_id) references app.employee(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, branch_id)   references app.dimension_value(tenant_id, id)
);
```

Audit-exempt projection (§3.5.3). `snapshot` is regenerated by `app.refresh_pos_cashier(principal_id)` called from the catalogue-revision trigger on `role_assignment`, `role_assignment_branch`, `role_permission`, `branch_pos_policy` and from the termination trigger; `pos.cashier.compare` (nightly) recomputes every snapshot through `app.principal_has` and reports differences. The PIN is verified only at the till from the down-synced `catalogue_cashier` row; the server never accepts a PIN as a login (spec:1324).

⚠️ **PR 12 review (2026-10-22; proposed ADR 0061 amendment).** `app.refresh_pos_cashier` reads and writes as the tenant's **system principal**, whichever actor fired it: it sets `app.actor_id` transaction-locally for its own select and update and restores the caller's value before it returns (a tenant with no system principal is refused `ERR_TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING`). Roles and `role_permission` belong to the whole tenant and are edited through §4.2.5's `{ company: "any" }` gate, while `pos_cashier` and `branch_pos_policy` carry Form A of `branch_isolation`, so under the writer's RLS an edit by an administrator of company X alone, or by one restricted to branch B1, silently left company Y's or branch B2's cashier snapshots stale. The snapshot is derived only from `app.principal_has` and the branch's policy row, so the switch grants nothing; RLS stays forced, nothing is `SECURITY DEFINER`, and the frozen gate, the function's signature and the trigger names are unchanged. `packages/db/test/staff/cashier-snapshot.test.ts` carries both regressions.

#### 4.6.4 `app.branch_pos_policy` (6C, migration 0066; spec:1324 — the spec's list ends with "…"; completed here)

```sql
create table app.branch_pos_policy (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null, branch_id uuid not null,
  max_line_discount_pct numeric(9,6) not null default 0, max_ticket_discount_pct numeric(9,6) not null default 0, max_void_amount numeric(19,4) not null default 0,
  max_price_override_pct numeric(9,6) not null default 0, blind_return_allowed boolean not null default false, max_blind_return_amount numeric(19,4) not null default 0,
  max_cash_in_drawer numeric(19,4), require_customer_over numeric(19,4), rounding_increment numeric(19,4) not null default 0.05,
  paid_out_allowed boolean not null default false, max_paid_out_amount numeric(19,4) not null default 0,     -- ⚠️ OD-10
  revision bigint not null default 0, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (company_id, branch_id), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, branch_id) references app.dimension_value(tenant_id, id));
```

Maintained under `admin.company.manage`; down-synced only to that branch's terminals (stream `branch_pos_policy`); sync apply re-verifies against this row, never the snapshot (spec:1324).

**Phase 6 implementation authorization (2026-10-07).** The branch policy is the sole applied cash-rounding source, with a positive increment and the configurable `0.05` default above. `currency.pos_rounding_increment` remains display-only under ADR 0009 decision 7; no currency seed increment changes. Zero is not a disable mode. This resolves the copied zero-mode consequence in proposed ADR 0059 and the currency/branch ambiguity recorded in ADR 0020 for this implementation; the decision bundle records authorization separately from formal ADR acceptance.

#### 4.6.5 `app.shift` (6D, migration 0070; spec:1331)

```sql
create table app.shift (
  id uuid primary key,                                  -- uuidv7 minted at the till (client id), like tickets
  tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null, branch_id uuid not null, terminal_id uuid not null,
  opened_principal_id uuid not null references app.principal(id),   -- the cashier: ATTRIBUTION data, never stamped (see the naming rule below)
  opened_at timestamptz not null, opening_float numeric(19,4) not null, currency char(3) not null,
  closed_at timestamptz, closed_principal_id uuid references app.principal(id),
  counted_cash numeric(19,4),                           -- from ShiftOpenClose.countedCash (kind = 'close', §4.10.1) — the ONLY cash figure the till sends
  expected_cash numeric(19,4),                          -- derived server-side: opening_float + Σ cash tenders − Σ paid-outs/safe-drops of this shift's posted tickets
  over_short numeric(19,4),                             -- counted_cash − expected_cash: POSITIVE IS OVER, negative is short (the TILL_OVER_SHORT posting reads this sign)
  over_short_document_id uuid,                          -- the TILL_OVER_SHORT document (spec:1352)
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, terminal_id) references app.pos_terminal(tenant_id, id));
```

**Why `opened_principal_id`, not `opened_by`** (the §3.3 naming rule applied): the `stamp_actor` linter rule fires on *every* column whose name ends `_by` and has no `stamp_<col>` trigger (plan0A:2755–2758) — it has no exemption set — and §3.5.2 requires zero violations after every migration, so a column named `opened_by` without the trigger cannot ship. Attaching the trigger would be worse: `stamp_actor` overwrites the column with `app.current_actor()` on insert (plan0A:2373–2376), and on a shift synced up by a terminal that is the **terminal** principal, not the cashier — the exact confusion of acting and attributed principal that SAH-044 names. `till_event` already uses the correct convention (`cashier_principal_id`, `supervisor_principal_id`, §4.6.1). `shift` follows it.

Tenders are `document_line` rows of `kind = 'tender'` (6A's migration 0061 rewrites the `document_line.kind` CHECK to the full union that includes `'tender'` — §4.3.4); a tender line carries `amount`, `custom_fields.method ∈ cash | card | transfer | store_credit` (lifted into the typed `LineSnapshot.tenderMethod` by `loadSnapshot`, §4.4.2) and `custom_fields.reference`; the `POS_TICKET` policy has one `each_line` debit rule per method with `when: { "line.kind": "tender", "line.tender_method": "<method>" }` resolved to accounts by code — **`1110` cash in till, `1120` card clearing, `1100` bank, `2200` store-credit liability, all four registered and seeded in §4.15**. The Z-report's tenders-by-type equal the ledger sums of those accounts over the shift's tickets to the cent; opening float and over/short come from `shift` and the `TILL_OVER_SHORT` document (test 21).

### 4.7 Costing engine interface (Phase 3)

#### 4.7.1 `packages/domain/src/costing/engine.ts` (3B)

```ts
export type CostingMethod = "avco" | "fifo";
export interface Layer { id: string; itemId: string; warehouseId: string; lotId: string; movementId: string; qtyIn: Quantity; value: Money; unitCost: Money; qtyRemaining: Quantity; effectiveDate: string; postingSeq: bigint; lineNo: number; movementNo: number }   // ordering key (effectiveDate, postingSeq, lineNo, movementNo) — §4.3.5
export interface Consumption { layerId: string; quantity: Quantity; unitCost: Money; value: Money }
export interface CostingInput { method: CostingMethod; openLayers: Layer[] /* for the item+warehouse, chronological */; movement: PlannedMovement & { effectiveDate: string; postingSeq: bigint } }
export interface CostingOutput { value: Money; unitCost: Money; consumptions: Consumption[] /* issues */; newLayer: Omit<Layer, "id"> | null /* receipts */; updatedRemaining: { layerId: string; qtyRemaining: Quantity }[] }
export interface CostingEngine {
  /** Pure. Receipts create a layer at the movement's value; issues consume per `method` (FIFO: oldest layers; AVCO: a proportional slice of all open layers at the running average — spec:1222). Throws ERR_COST_NEGATIVE if a computed unit cost is negative; the divisor is clamped to MIN_MEANINGFUL_QTY = Quantity.of("0.000001") (spec:1227); a value-less issue with no open layers costs at zero only when `costing = "zero"` (free-of-charge lines, spec:1055), otherwise ERR_STOCK_INSUFFICIENT. */
  cost(input: CostingInput): CostingOutput;
  /** Running average for display/valuation: Σ(qtyRemaining × unitCost) / Σ qtyRemaining over open layers. */
  average(openLayers: Layer[]): Money;
}
export const costingEngine: CostingEngine;     // the ONE implementation (spec:1228) — reports and valuation import this, never re-implement
```

**Two `cost()` pins added by 3D (amendment 8), because 3D is the first slice whose documents reach both.** A
**receipt** whose `PlannedMovement.value` is null is valued at `average(openLayers)`; with no open layer the
unit cost is `Money.zero` and one warning is recorded — this is the count-surplus and over-receipt case, where
no purchase price exists. And when the policy's `inventory.allowNegative` is true and the movement was admitted
by the data layer (an `inventory.negative_stock.override` event exists, §4.5.3),
`cost()` **does not raise** for the quantity no open layer covers; the covered quantity is consumed and recorded in `cost_consumption` as usual
(`layer_id` is NOT NULL, so the uncovered quantity has no consumption row) and the uncovered quantity's
treatment is 3B's golden fixture, not 3D's to define.

**Owner-approved costing amendment (2026-10-01; ADRs 0038/0039).** `Layer.value` is the exact original receipt value. Export `remainingLayerValue(layer, quantity = layer.qtyRemaining): Money`, rounded once as `value × quantity / qtyIn`. Covered issues cost the sum of the reductions in that remaining value; AVCO keeps its proportional quantity split and allocates this budget across nonzero shares, FIFO uses each layer's reduction. A running average is the sum of remaining exact values divided by remaining quantity. Receipts, replay, as-of valuation, layer reads and receipt-side reports share this rule.

`CostingInput` additionally accepts optional `cancellation: { movementId: string; value: Money }`, resolved internally from a reversing document's pure purchase receipt. It cancels only that wholly untouched layer at its original booked value. A missing, consumed, mismatched or recost-pending source raises `ERR_DOC_STATUS_ILLEGAL`, atomically, regardless of a stock override. Replay resolves the same source. New back-dated issues that would consume a later-cancelled purchase are refused rather than making its historical cancellation un-replayable. No immutable movement or ledger entry is rewritten.

Migration 0118 adds `cost_layer.value numeric(19,4) not null check (value >= 0)`, backfills it from receipt movements under tenant contexts and marks existing issues for replay. Existing receipt unit costs remain display metadata; receipt-side report totals read `cost_layer.value`. The ordinary return, transfer and count rules remain unchanged. A transfer receipt delegates to its same-line computed issue value even when a reversal carries a copied `line.cost`; branch 1’s copied cost applies only to a one-leg receipt, so equal quantities always conserve the exact value across warehouses. The `posting-only-tables` gate allows only this exact migration path to backfill `cost_layer`, invalidate `cost_consumption`, and mark `cost_booking`; immutable ledger and movement writes and every other migration remain protected.

#### 4.7.2 `packages/db/src/costing/` (**`applyMovements` 3A provisional, 3B completes; the rest 3B**)

`applyMovements` is the single hook `postDocument` step 9 calls, and it is the **only** writer of `app.inventory_movement`. Its signature is frozen from 3A onward and never changes; only its body grows:

- **3A** ships it in provisional form in `packages/db/src/costing/apply-movements.ts`: **take the stock advisory locks first through `lockStockKeys(tx, companyId, keys)`** (3A, `packages/db/src/costing/stock-on-hand.ts` — the sorted, de-duplicated `stock:<company>/<item>/<warehouse>/<lot>` transaction-scoped advisory locks), assign `movement_no` from `plan.movements[i].movementNo`, resolve each line's `lot_id` to the item's `NONE` sentinel lot when the line carries none, insert the `inventory_movement` rows (the BEFORE INSERT `assert_stock_available` trigger fires here — that is how 3A owns test 18 "by API, job and `app_rw` SQL"), set `value = round(unit_price × quantity, 4)` in base currency for a receipt and the same for an issue, write `document_line.cost`, and return the plan with `value` filled. It writes **no** `cost_layer`/`cost_consumption` — they do not exist yet.
- **3B** replaces the body: compute through `costingEngine.cost()` (pure), insert the `inventory_movement` rows, then insert `cost_layer` / `cost_consumption` — that internal order is mandatory, because `cost_layer.movement_id` has FK `(tenant_id, movement_id) → inventory_movement(tenant_id, id)` and the rows must exist first — and write `document_line.cost` from the consumption values. 3A's provisional value rule is deleted, not extended.

`inventory_movement` is immutable, so a value written by the provisional body can never be corrected in place. **Rows posted between 3A and 3B are test data only**: no tenant transacts before the Phase 3 DoD is green, and 3B's task list ends with a re-seed of staging (§3.4.8 already makes re-applying the seed a release-runbook step), so no provisional value survives into Phase 4. A plan that proposes back-filling them instead has misread this.

**The advisory locks are part of the frozen behaviour of step 9, not of 3A's provisional value rule — 3B keeps the `lockStockKeys` call.** `assert_stock_available` is a BEFORE INSERT trigger that reads `sum(quantity)` and then admits the row; under READ COMMITTED (§4.2.2's fixed isolation level) two `postDocument` transactions issuing the same `(company, item, warehouse, lot)` both read the same committed sum, both satisfy the trigger and both commit — the one clause of acceptance test 18 that a correct-looking implementation fails. `lockStockKeys` **before** the insert is what makes the trigger's read-and-insert atomic per stock key; `mergeStockOnHand` takes the same keys again at step 12 (re-locking a held key is a no-op, so the second call is free), which is 1A amendment A4's reasoning applied to the projection. **3B replaces the body around this call and must not drop it**: a 3B implementation that computes through `costingEngine.cost()` and inserts without locking reintroduces the double-issue, and no test in 3B's own suite would catch it because the case is 3A's — acceptance test 18's two-concurrent-jobs clause, in 3A Task 9. If §4.2.2's isolation level ever changes, both lock sites and A4 need re-deriving — a contracts amendment, never a plan edit.

```ts
/** Called by postDocument step 9 inside the posting transaction. Inserts app.inventory_movement (always), then cost_layer /
 *  cost_consumption (3B onward), fills `value` on the plan's movements and `cost` on document_line, and returns the plan. */
export async function applyMovements(tx: Sql, ctx: TenantContext, plan: PostingPlan, snapshot: DocumentSnapshot): Promise<PostingPlan>;
/** Marks every layer/consumption of the affected items at or after (effectiveDate, postingSeq) invalid and enqueues inventory.cost.replay (one job per company, singletonKey = companyId). */
export async function invalidateFrom(tx: Sql, ctx: TenantContext, input: { companyId: string; itemIds: string[]; effectiveDate: string; postingSeq: bigint }): Promise<void>;
/** Job handler: replays movements forward from the earliest invalidation in bounded batches (default 500 movements per withTenant transaction — spec:1368), rewrites layers/consumptions, and posts one COST_ADJUSTMENT document per fiscal period whose COGS/inventory totals changed (spec:1224). Idempotent and restartable (SAH-054). */
export async function replay(sql: Sql, job: JobEnvelope<{ companyId: string }>, ctx: TenantContext): Promise<{ movementsReplayed: number; adjustmentsPosted: string[] }>;
```

**A receipt movement's value — the four-branch rule, and the null it closes (3C, superseding 3A's provisional rule).** `planMovements` (3A) returns every movement with `value: null` (3a:4930), and 3B's `costReceipt` raises `ERR_COST_VALUE_MISSING` on a null value (3b:994) while 3B's `applyMovements` passes a receipt's `movement.value` through untouched (3b:2990) — so **between 3B and 3C no receipt can post at all**, and 3B's own Task 7 case expecting `value: "1000.0000"` is red until this rule lands. 3C closes it, in the one place a receipt's value is decided, `packages/db/src/costing/landed-cost.ts`:

    export function receiptValue(line: LineSnapshot, landedCost: Money, rate: ExchangeRate): Money;
    export async function landedCostByLine(tx: Sql, documentId: string): Promise<Map<string, string>>;

`receiptValue` is `toBase(line.amount.add(landedCost), rate)`. `line.amount` and not `round(unit_price × quantity, 4)`: §4.3.4 defines `amount` as "excl. tax, document currency", which is the discount-correct figure, and 3A's provisional rule ignored `document_line.discount`. `landedCostByLine` is keyed by `document_line.id` with a **document-currency** decimal string as its value; a document with no allocation yields an empty map, and `receiptValue` is then `toBase(line.amount, rate)`.

**`applyMovements` calls it at exactly one site, and the rule there has four branches in this order — a receipt whose value comes from somewhere else must not be overwritten:**

1. **`snapshot.lines[i].cost !== null` → that cost.** A4 makes it base currency and a magnitude already, so it is used as it stands. **This branch is reachable only because 3C adds one column to `reverseDocument`'s line copy — `l.cost`, unnegated.** 2A widened that copy to `kind, item_id, quantity, unit_price, discount, amount` and 3A to `warehouse_id, lot_id, unit_id, unit_quantity` (3a:4270); `cost` was left out, so a reversal of a stock **issue** — which emits a *receipt* of the returned goods — would reach branch 3 and value that receipt at the negated **sale** price instead of the carrying cost. `cost` is a magnitude, so it is copied and not negated, and step 5 of `applyMovements` overwrites it with the same number, which makes the copy idempotent. 3D's `DELIVERY_ORDER` and 4A's `SALES_INVOICE` reversals depend on this column.
2. **else, a same-`lineNo` `issue` movement exists → that leg's computed value.** A `transfer` line emits an issue at `warehouse_id` and a receipt at `to_warehouse_id` (§4.7.3); the receipt leg's value is what left the first warehouse, never a re-priced `line.amount`. 3D's `TRANSFER`/`TRANSFER_RECEIPT` depend on this branch.
3. **else → `receiptValue(line, landedCost, rate)`.** The genuine purchase-side receipt: `GOODS_RECEIPT`, `SHIPMENT`, 9B's `OPENING_STOCK`.
4. **else — no line at all for the movement's `lineNo` → `null`, explicitly**, and `costingEngine` raises `ERR_COST_VALUE_MISSING` naming the movement (SAH-007). The fall-through is written out rather than defaulted to zero: a movement with no source line is an internal inconsistency, and a zero would silently create a free receipt and a zero-cost layer that every later margin reads.

**The `fill` rules (3D amendment 6).** `applyMovements` fills every planned ledger line carrying a `fill` tag
(§4.4.2) with a **non-negative magnitude** and never alters `side` — direction is the policy's, through a fixed
`side` or `when: { "line.quantity_sign": … }`. **Which rule applies is decided by the tags the policy put on the
source line, not by how many movements survived the evaluator's zero-drop.** A source line carrying **only one**
tag kind is a single-value line: that tag receives `|movement.value|` of its sole movement. A source line
carrying **both** tags is a two-quantity variance line, and then `fill: "cost"` receives `|receipt.value|` and
`fill: "variance_value"` receives `| |issue.value| − |receipt.value| |`, **with an absent leg contributing
`Money.zero`** — which is the total-loss case (`counted_quantity = 0`, the receipt movement dropped by the
zero-quantity rule): `cost` is zero, so the destination's inventory account is debited nothing, and the whole
dispatched value lands on the variance legs. Reading the survivor's value into both tags there would debit the
destination for goods that never arrived and relieve the corridor twice. `document_line.cost` is written as the
same non-negative magnitude as the line's `fill: "cost"` value (4A and 7B read it).

**The unfilled-cost refusal (4A amendment 4) — 2A's step-9b guard restored where step 9 now lives.** **A `fill`-tagged planned ledger line whose source `document_line` has no surviving `PlannedMovement` is left exactly as the evaluator emitted it** — `applyMovements` fills nothing and alters nothing on it. When that line's amount is `Money.zero` **and** the source line's `LineSnapshot.cost` is null, `applyMovements` **refuses the post** with `ERR_POLICY_REQUIRES_MISSING` naming the document line: the cost was never computed by a movement and never supplied by a conversion, and inserting the zero would understate cost of goods sold silently. When the source line carries a non-null `cost` — a figure another document computed and this one copied forward — the line stands at that figure and no movement is required. This is the branch 4A is the first slice to need, because it is the first with a `line.cost` ledger leg on a policy whose `inventory.effect` is `none`; 2A's step-9b guard said the same thing at step 9b and 3B removed it when it replaced the guard with this call (§4.3.2 step 9b).

**Who may write `document_line.cost` (4A amendment 5; Phase 6 return integration correction).** **`document_line.cost` is written by `applyMovements`, 4A's two conversion services in `packages/db/src/ar-ap/invoice.ts` and `credit-note.ts`, the existing reversal copy, and 6A's server-valued POS return conversion in `packages/db/src/sync/apply.ts`.** 3D's Global Constraint 3 ("a drafting service never sets it") binds ordinary drafting services; these conversion paths are the stated exceptions. The `SALES_INVOICE` must relieve `1250` by **the same figure the `DELIVERY_ORDER` debited**, or the corridor never nets to zero. Recomputing it from current layers would be a second costing answer for one physical movement (SAH-009, spec:1228) and would leave a residue in `1250` after every recost. The copy is a magnitude, exactly as 3C's `reverseDocument` line copy is (3c:219).

The POS exception (2026-10-08, proposed ADR 0056 amendment) supplies a **nonnegative base-currency cost** before the existing receipt-value branch consumes it. Referenced returns use the verified source sale's carrying cost, bounded by source-line identity and remaining return quantity; full return cost conserves the source magnitude. Partial returns use quantity-bounded `returns` links rather than full-reversal semantics. Blind returns use server-owned valid cost-layer facts under the existing stock locks, and refuse when carrying cost cannot be established. No cost is accepted from the wire, no new inventory or ledger writer is added, and missing, stale or ambiguous source facts are recoverable refusals.

**The transfer costing order (3D amendment 7).** For a `transfer` line, `applyMovements` costs the **issue** leg first,
and sets the receipt leg's `value` from the consumed value — `unitCost = |issue.value| ÷ issueQuantity`,
`receipt.value = unitCost × receiptQuantity` — before the destination layer is created. 3D is the first slice to
use `effect: "transfer"`.

**The allocation reaches the layer once, through the movement's value, and every later replay preserves it.** `inventory_movement` is immutable and 3B's `replay` recomputes a receipt's layer as `unit_cost = value / quantity` from that immutable value (3b:4073–4079), which is why 3B's own comment calls landed cost "the one thing that legitimately changes a receipt's value". Landed cost is therefore a **draft-only** operation: after post there is nothing to re-allocate, and a correction is `reverseDocument` plus a re-post.

#### 4.7.3 Tables (3A/3B; spec:1212, 1216–1226; C4 resolved — `tenant_id`, `company_id`, `created_at` present)

```sql
create table app.inventory_movement (                       -- IMMUTABLE, audit-exempt (plan0A:1624–1629)
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  document_id uuid not null,
  line_no int not null,                                       -- the source document_line.line_no
  movement_no int not null check (movement_no > 0),           -- 1-based per document; the unique key. A `transfer` line emits TWO
                                                              -- movements (issue at warehouse, receipt at to_warehouse), so line_no
                                                              -- alone is not unique — TRANSFER/TRANSFER_RECEIPT would collide.
  item_id uuid not null, warehouse_id uuid not null,
  lot_id uuid not null,                                       -- NOT NULL: stock_on_hand's primary key contains lot_id, so a NULL here
                                                              -- would fail the step-12 MERGE at runtime. Every item has one sentinel
                                                              -- lot with code 'NONE' created with the item (3A); applyMovements
                                                              -- resolves a line's null lot_id to it before insert (SAH-050).
  unit_id uuid not null,
  quantity numeric(19,6) not null check (quantity <> 0),      -- base unit; + receipt, − issue
  value numeric(19,4) not null,                               -- mandatory (SAH-007); base currency; sign follows quantity
  effective_date date not null, posting_seq bigint not null, posted_at timestamptz not null default now(),   -- the posting instant (spec:1370's ledger_entry pattern)
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),              -- spec:1370 exempts ONLY ledger_entry from created_at; this table is neither a join nor a counter table
  posted_by uuid not null default app.current_actor() references app.principal(id),                          -- stamped
  unique (document_id, movement_no), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, document_id) references app.document(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, item_id) references app.item(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, warehouse_id) references app.warehouse(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, lot_id) references app.lot(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, unit_id) references app.unit_of_measure(tenant_id, id));
create index inventory_movement_chrono_idx on app.inventory_movement (company_id, item_id, warehouse_id, effective_date, posting_seq, line_no, movement_no);   -- the total chronological key (spec:1225; §4.3.5)
create trigger inventory_movement_immutable before update or delete on app.inventory_movement for each row execute function app.forbid_change();
create trigger inventory_movement_stock_available before insert on app.inventory_movement for each row execute function app.assert_stock_available();
-- assert_stock_available: for an issue (new.quantity < 0) it computes the available quantity as sum(quantity) over app.inventory_movement for the same
-- (company_id, item_id, warehouse_id, lot_id) — which already includes this transaction's earlier rows — NEVER from stock_on_hand (MERGEd only at step 12);
-- if available + new.quantity < 0 it raises ERR_STOCK_INSUFFICIENT unless an 'inventory.negative_stock.override' event exists for new.document_id (§4.5.3).
revoke update, delete on app.inventory_movement from app_rw;

create table app.stock_on_hand (                             -- synchronous projection (D14), MERGE in the posting transaction
  tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null, item_id uuid not null, warehouse_id uuid not null, lot_id uuid not null,
  quantity numeric(19,6) not null default 0, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (company_id, item_id, warehouse_id, lot_id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, item_id) references app.item(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, warehouse_id) references app.warehouse(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, lot_id) references app.lot(tenant_id, id));
-- `lot_id` is NOT NULL on both sides: every item has one sentinel lot with code 'NONE' created with the item (3A) and
-- applyMovements resolves a line's null lot to it, so the primary key never contains NULL (SAH-050). `document_line.lot_id`
-- stays nullable — the user need not enter a lot; the posting service is what resolves the sentinel.

create table app.cost_layer (                                -- derived, audit-exempt, updatable by app_rw (qty_remaining)
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  item_id uuid not null, warehouse_id uuid not null, lot_id uuid not null, movement_id uuid not null,
  qty_in numeric(19,6) not null, value numeric(19,4) not null check (value >= 0),        -- exact receipt value (0118, ADR 0039 amendment)
  unit_cost numeric(19,4) not null check (unit_cost >= 0), qty_remaining numeric(19,6) not null check (qty_remaining >= 0),
  effective_at date not null, sequence bigint not null,       -- = movement.posting_seq (spec:1220 "sequence")
  invalidated_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (movement_id), unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id)   references app.company(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, item_id)      references app.item(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, warehouse_id) references app.warehouse(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, lot_id)       references app.lot(tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, movement_id)  references app.inventory_movement(tenant_id, id));
create table app.cost_consumption (
  id uuid primary key default uuidv7(), tenant_id uuid not null references app.tenant(id), company_id uuid not null,
  movement_id uuid not null, layer_id uuid not null, quantity numeric(19,6) not null, unit_cost numeric(19,4) not null, value numeric(19,4) not null,
  invalidated_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (tenant_id, id),
  foreign key (tenant_id, company_id) references app.company(tenant_id, id),   -- round 4 (3B amendment A23): §3.3's Always list requires a composite FK to every tenant-scoped parent; `cost_layer` above and `stock_valuation` (§4.6.1) both carry it, and Plan 0A's `composite_fk` rule only inspects the FKs a table HAS, so `lintSchema` stayed green on the omission
  foreign key (tenant_id, movement_id) references app.inventory_movement(tenant_id, id), foreign key (tenant_id, layer_id) references app.cost_layer(tenant_id, id));
-- 3B's amendment A23 also gives this table `check (quantity > 0)`, `check (unit_cost >= 0)` and `check (value >= 0)`;
-- those three land in 3B's own Task 0 PR with migration 0034. The composite company FK is recorded here because
-- it is a §3.3 Always-list obligation this block was silently missing.
alter table app.company add column costing_method text not null default 'avco' check (costing_method in ('avco', 'fifo'));   -- 0035 (OD-06)
```
