| **A10** | 3.7.4 | For the **tax** area only, `expected.json` is a `TaxGoldenExpectation`: `{ boxes: GoldenBox[]; payload: string; payloadSha256: string; tieOut: TaxReturnTieOutRow[] }`. §3.7.4's sentence — "`expected.json` is … the rendered return (tax)" — still holds; the wrapper adds the sha and the tie-out beside it, because the DoD's three verbs are three assertions and a bare payload proves only one. **`GoldenBox` is `ReturnBox` with `amount` as a 4-dp STRING** — `ReturnBox.amount` is a `Money`, `Money` is not JSON, and the harness re-wraps with `Money.of` on read. **And `input.json` for this area is a `GoldenCase`** — the return's regime, version and period, plus a `GoldenDocument[]` naming its tax codes, accounts and parties **symbolically** (`"SYN-OUT-STD"`, `"4000"`, `"customer"`), not a `DocumentSnapshot[]`: every id in this fixture is a per-run uuid, and the return is proved end-to-end through the database because the tie-out reads `account_balance`. **A tax case therefore carries no `policies.json`** — 3B's A17 file exists because 3B's harness is a pure `evaluatePolicy` driver with no database; this harness posts through `taxFixture`, which reads the four 4A envelopes off disk through `seedTypeFromPack`, and a second copy of those policies would be exactly the two-spellings hazard 9 forbids. **3B took the same shape of amendment for costing** (its A7 and A17). | **T9** |

| **A11** | 4.4.2, 4.3.2 step 6 | **Recorded, not changed — and load-bearing for this slice.** §4.4.2 must state what 2A's evaluator already does: **the `each_tax` path pushes the group's `PlannedTaxLine` unconditionally and then drops a zero-amount group before resolving that rule's `accountRef`.** 2A's shipped body is exactly that order — `taxLines.push({ … })`, then `if (g.amount.isZero()) continue;`, then `normalise` and `resolveAccount` (phase-2a:1843–1855). **5A is the first slice that depends on it**, and depends on it totally: `tax_code_account_for_kind_check` (T1's DDL) and the T6 loader put an account id on `kind = 'output'` and `kind = 'input'` **only**, so a `zero`, `exempt` or `out_of_scope` code has both account columns null — correctly, because a zero-rated supply has no tax account. Resolve-then-drop would refuse an ordinary zero-rated sale with `ERR_POLICY_REQUIRES_MISSING` naming an account that is *right* to be absent, and the pack would ship a box (`S3`, `kinds ["zero","exempt"], measure "base"`) that nothing could fill. Writing the ordering into §4.4.2 is what stops a later refactor of `evaluate.ts` reordering two lines and silently breaking every zero-rated document. **No code changes in any slice.** | **T7, T8, T9** |

| **A12** | 4.17.1, 4.3.4 | **3C's `DraftLine` gains `taxCodeId?: string` and `draftTypedDocument`'s `insert into app.document_line` column list gains `tax_code_id` with `${l.taxCodeId ?? null}`** — the test-tier twin of A7, in the same PR as the foreign key (0055). 3C's frozen shape (phase-3c:384-402, 444-453) carries **no** `taxCodeId` and its insert omits the column, so every taxed line in this slice — five direct `draftTypedDocument` calls and every line that reaches it through 4B's `postFromPack`, whose `lines` is `readonly DraftLine[]` — would be an excess property at compile time and a dropped value at run time: no line would carry a code, `computeDocumentTax` would write zeros, `plan.taxLines` would be empty and every box, tie-out and golden assertion in T7/T8/T9 would fail. The addition is **additive and optional**; 3C's, 3D's, 4A's and 4B's own callers are unaffected. **The one edit is 5A's, in Task 3**, and Task 3's own test proves it by drafting a line with `taxCodeId` and reading `document_line.tax_code_id` back. **`fixtures.ts` is therefore opened by two tasks in this slice — T1 for `seedTaxCode` and T3 for this one member — and by no others.** | **T3, T7, T8, T9** |

| **A13** | 4.17.1, 4.2.8 | **The two other shared surfaces this slice extends additively, registered here because A12 registered its twin and leaving these two out is the inconsistency, not the economy.** (a) **4B's `PostFromPackOptions` gains `taxInclusive?: boolean` and `computeTax?: boolean`**, and `postFromPack`'s body gains one block between the draft and the approval path (the `tax_inclusive` `UPDATE`, then `computeDocumentTax`). 4B's own amendment 9 registers `tests/invariants/support/ar-ap.ts` to 4B with `postFromPack(db, s, opts)` and `PostFromPackOptions` by name (phase-4b:250, 1861), so this is the same class of edit as A12's to 3C's `DraftLine`: **additive, both members optional and defaulted `false`, every 4A/4B call site behaves exactly as it did**, and no signature changes. It is registered because **6A owns the next re-run of test 15 and posts taxed `POS_TICKET`s through the same helper** — a plan writer who reads §4.17.1 and does not find `computeTax` there writes a second posting helper, which is hazard 9 exactly. **The one edit is 5A's, in Task 7.** (b) **1A's `DocumentSchema` gains `taxInclusive: z.boolean()`** — the read twin of A7's `CreateDocumentBody` member, in the same PR as the column (0054), so a `GET` round-trips the flag a `POST` accepted. §4.2.8 registers `DocumentSchema` to 1A (contracts:1862), and A7 names only the write body, so the read body needs its own row. Not optional and not defaulted: the column is `not null default false`, so every document has a value. **The one edit is 5A's, in Task 2.** | **T2, T7** |



## 5. Hazards every plan writer must respect

Stated plainly. Each is a review-blocking finding when a plan violates it.

1. **No real statutory rate, threshold, ceiling or formula anywhere** — not in a plan, a test, a fixture, a seed file or a comment (spec:2080 "This document states no rate, threshold, ceiling or formula"; spec:2229). Phase 8 golden tests run on the clearly synthetic `SYNTH` table (§4.12.4). Real tables arrive only through OD-23 as `packages/db/seed/my/statutory/<scheme>/vN.json` with `source`, `loaded_by`, `verified_by`. A number that looks like a contribution rate in a Phase 8 plan is a defect.
2. **No invented MyInvois detail.** No LHDN endpoint, field name, schema version, threshold or deadline appears in any plan until 5B's Task 1 ("fetch the authority's current specification; record ADR 0051") has run. 5B's adapter tasks are written against the abstract `EInvoiceTransmitter` (§4.9.3) and say "per ADR 0051" wherever a concrete value would go (spec:2226, 2467: "do not rely on this document or on training data").
3. **The Firebird version is unknown.** It is probed or declared, never inferred (§4.13.1's `createReader`). **The scoping report — row counts and date ranges per table (§5.1 #10, Part VII #1, #2, #5) — is the first task that reads the owner's data: 9A Task 3; Tasks 1–2 build the driver port and the SQL renderer and touch no customer data** (amended from "9A's Task 1 is the scoping task"; the substance of "scope first, migrate second" is unchanged, and dropping the OD-17 task still leaves every other task green against the committed corpus). The extraction method is ADR 0081; nothing in 9A/9B assumes `gbak`, ODBC or a file reader before that ADR. **No per-table legacy row interface is invented in either slice** until a live catalogue has been read (§4.13.1's closing note) — transcribing column lists nobody has confirmed against the customer's database is the invention this hazard forbids.
4. **Reports ship inside each phase; Phase 7 is the engine.** 1B ships `accounting.trial_balance` + `accounting.ledger`, 3D `inventory.stock_on_hand` + `inventory.sales_by_item` + `inventory.valuation`, 4B `accounting.ageing`, 6D `pos.z_report` + `pos.sales_by_cashier` (spec:2300, §4.16.1); 7A adds the builder and 7B/7C re-express those eight **under the same codes** and complete the catalogue. A Phase 1–6 plan that defers its minimal report to Phase 7 fails its phase's DoD; a Phase 7 plan that renames one on re-expression breaks "ships continuously". **"Sales by item" means different things in Phase 3 and Phase 4, and both are owned:** at 3D it is delivered *quantity and cost* per item (from `DELIVERY_ORDER` movements and `cost_consumption`), because the first revenue-posting type is 4A's `SALES_INVOICE` and there is no sales value to report; **4A extends the same report with revenue and margin** in the PR that ships `SALES_INVOICE`, 4B backs it with the `item_profitability` projection, and 7B re-expresses it as a definition. The same split applies to test 7's "profit": cost-side at 3D, revenue-bearing from 4B.
5. **Owner-account tasks are written as "owner provides X; verify with `<exact command>`" with a local equivalent.** Pattern: *"Owner provides: Supabase staging project URL and `app_rw` password (OD-19). Verify: `bun run --cwd packages/db provision:verify --url "$DATABASE_URL"` prints `rls-forced: ok, bypassrls-probe: refused, app_auth-login: refused, pooler-url: absent`. Until provided: the same script runs against `startDb()` and must print the same four lines."* Every 0C/0E/1B/5B/8D task that touches an owner account follows this pattern; the slice never blocks on it.
6. **Pending owner decisions are isolated tasks** (§2.0, §2.12). One task per OD item, droppable without renumbering neighbours' interfaces; the default written into the plan is the §2.12 default. A plan that spreads a ⚠️ item across several tasks is rejected.
7. **Plans never re-open D1–D27** (spec:114–142) and never re-decide anything in §2.12. A plan needing a deviation writes an ADR proposal and stops (spec:95); it does not implement first.
8. **Plan 0A helpers are cited by their exact names and never renamed:** `startDb`, `Db`, `withTenant` (4-argument test helper), `uuidv7`, `seedTenant`, `Seed`, `draftDocument`, `schemaFingerprint`, `lintSchema`, `AUDIT_EXEMPT`, `IMMUTABLE`, `up`, `down`, `listApplied`, `discover`, `app_meta.enable_tenant_rls`, `app_meta.attach_audit`, `app_meta.attach_stamp`, `app.actor_has`, `app.resolve_principal`, `app.current_tenant`, `app.current_actor` (§4.1). The production `withTenant(sql, ctx, fn)` is a different export path (§4.2.2).
9. **`fixtures.ts` is extended additively, and only with the helpers §4.17 assigns the slice — and the same rule binds the test tier's own shared helpers (§4.17.1).** New helpers get new names and the uniform `(db, s, opts?)` shape; `seedTenant`'s inserts and constants are never edited (§4.1). A plan that changes the 0A JOURNAL fixture policy breaks `ledger.test.ts` and `documents.test.ts`; a plan that invents `createItem` beside §4.17's `seedItem` gives two slices two ways to do one thing.
10. **Per-tenant rows cannot be written by a migration.** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` binds `app_migrator` (spec:1366); a migration file has no `set_config`, so it sees no tenants. Roles, role grants, document types, policies, templates, report definitions, tax codes and rate tables are seed-pack data applied by `bun run seed --tenant` (§3.4.8). Only `app.permission` (global) is migration data.
11. **Enum labels cannot be used in the migration that adds them** (§3.4.4). No slice adds an enum label; new closed vocabularies are `text + CHECK`.
12. **Plan 0A's reversibility test hard-codes `[1]`**; 0B's first task generalises it (§3.4.6) — every later migration relies on that change having merged.
13. **`lint-schema.ts` is a merge hotspot.** Set memberships are pre-declared in §3.5.3; a plan edits the sets to exactly that state and adds nothing else.
14. **Migration and ADR numbers are allocated; never renumber, never borrow** (§3.4.1, §3.9). Parallel phases mean a higher number may be applied before a lower one — no plan asserts `max(version)`.
15. **Two `withTenant`s** — the production one is explicit `READ COMMITTED` with one retry; the test one is not (§4.2.2). Root `tests/` use the production one.
16. **The minimal `employee` table is migration 0064 with fixed text** (§4.6.2); whichever of 6C/8A runs first commits it; the other verifies.
17. **Test 7's "gone negative" is produced only through `inventory.negative_stock.override`** recorded as an `override` `document_event` by a second principal (F-6); a test that toggles a flag or writes a movement directly is invalid (test 18).
18. **Test 22's and test 28's projection set is fixed:** compare `ledger_entry` rows as a multiset on `(account_id, debit, credit, currency, exchange_rate, base_debit, base_credit, effective_date, fiscal_period_id)` and `ledger_entry_dimension` rows on `(dimension_type code, dimension_value_id)`, projecting out `id`, `document_id`, `line_no`, `posted_at`, `posted_by`, `posting_policy_id` (the two documents necessarily pin different policies) — F-31; cost consumptions on `(item_id, warehouse_id, lot_id, quantity, unit_cost, value)`.
19. **`POS_TICKET`: the terminal acts, the cashier is attributed** (spec:1324). `created_by`/`posted_by` = the terminal principal from the signed call; `document.attributed_to` = the cashier; overrides are events with `actor_id` = terminal and `attributed_to` = supervisor. A plan that makes the cashier the acting principal reintroduces SAH-044.
20. **Jobs run as the tenant's system principal** (`systemContext`, §4.2.2; spec:2179), never under a human's id and never from a request path; every job write is audited under the system principal.
21. **`sql.unsafe` has exactly three homes** (§3.3): the migration runner, the pg-boss enqueue adapter, the Firebird reader. Everything else is a `tx` tagged template or Drizzle (test 27).
22. **Nothing outside `packages/db/src/posting/` and `packages/db/src/costing/` writes ledger, movement, layer, projection or tax-transaction tables** (§4.3.2; the `posting-only-tables` lint). Reports, importers, sync apply and payroll all call `postDocument`.
23. **`Money.toBase` rounds `HALF_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` at scale 4** — the only mode that satisfies the `ledger_entry` CHECK `base_debit = round(debit * exchange_rate, 4)` (spec:1816). A plan choosing bankers' rounding for base amounts produces rows the database refuses.
24. **`document_event` is written only by triggers and the override door** (§4.5.2–§4.5.3). No handler inserts it.
25. **The DELETE grant list is pinned** (§3.5.4); **2B is the only slice that extends it** (drafts — the one case spec:2049 admits besides the erasure workflow) and it updates `privileges.test.ts` in the same PR. Everything else, `saved_view` included, is archived with `archived_at`.
26. **The permission vocabulary and module list are closed** (§3.6.1); no new module, no new code beyond spec:2146–2150 (plus the two ⚠️ leave codes). A capability with no code uses the mapping in §3.6.2.
27. **No `service` principal kind in v1** (C10): machine access is terminals only; adding a kind is an ADR proposal, not a plan task.
28. **Phase 8 may run alongside Phases 5–7 but 8D needs 7A and 2C** (F-9b: annual statements use the report engine; payslips are attachments). 8A–8C do not.
29. **The UI is not specified** (spec:79, 108). Every screen task begins with OD-24 ("owner provides screenshots and a two-minute operator description; verify: the description is attached to the task") and targets keyboard parity (spec:2254); no plan invents a workflow.
30. **The PDF engine is decided once, in 0E (ADR 0016)**, on a real Arabic tax invoice (spec:1132); 2C, 7A and 8D consume that ADR and never re-evaluate engines.
31. **Every route needs a probe entry in `tests/invariants/probes.ts`**, keyed by its `RouteModule.path` (§4.2.7), or the tenant-isolation harness fails the build; every job payload carries `tenantId` and is probed the same way (§3.7.2). The probe lives in the test tier and never on `RouteModule` — it uses `Db`/`Seed` from `@dulja/db/test`, and a production route module must not import Testcontainers (§3.1).
32. **No plan invents a literal in a shared namespace.** Five namespaces are registered here and a literal outside them is a review-blocking finding: document-type codes and their `module` (§4.14), **account codes (§4.15)**, report codes and `DatasetId` members (§4.16), `fixtures.ts` helper names (§4.17), and the `ERR_*` space (§4.2.4). The test is mechanical — if the string appears in a seed file or a policy and is not in a register, the plan amends the register first. This is the whole reason for the registers: an account code, unlike a permission code, has no build check behind it and a wrong one fails only at post, at run time, in the slice that did not write it.
33. **The slice that seeds a policy seeds the accounts that policy names by code** (§4.15) — the F-21 rule applied to accounts. 6A seeds the POS tender accounts because it owns the `POS_TICKET` policy; 3C seeds the expiry-loss account 3D posts to; 8B seeds the payroll accounts 8C spends. A slice that consumes a code it did not seed asserts, in its first task in that area, that the account resolves — it never re-seeds it and never falls back to a null account.
34. **A document-type seed file is an envelope, not a bare policy** (§4.3.7). `posting-policy.schema.json` is `additionalProperties: false`, so `nameEn`, `nameAr`, `module`, `policyVersion` and `effectiveFrom` live outside `policy`. **`module` is not the module segment of `approval.post`**: `PAYROLL_PAYMENT` and `EMPLOYEE_ADVANCE` post under `accounting.payment.*` and are `hr`, because the column is the attachment download gate (§4.5.8) and their attachments carry per-employee pay (test 32). Every §4.14 row states its value; the column's default is never the source.
35. **Plans are written to the writing-plans skill:** every task has exact file paths, exact signatures (copied from §4), real code, a failing test first, and a commit; "TBD", "TODO", "similar to Task N", "add appropriate validation" are plan failures. Where this document gives code, the plan repeats it — a task's implementer sees only their own task.

---

Every row appears once as owned. Rows with "—" in the spec's "Proven by" column (1044, 1051, 1053, 1054) are proven by their slice's DoD clause and a named test in the plan (F-20).

**Row 1042 is the one row whose owner and whose only Part VI proof sit in different slices (F-22), and this is how it is closed.** spec:1042's "Proven by" column names test 8 (multi-currency round-trip) alone, and test 8 is **4B's** (§6.1) while the row is **4A's** — so allocation, credit limits and payment terms, three of the row's five capabilities, have no acceptance test anywhere. They are proven the F-20 way, by named tests in 4A's plan, and the plan must carry all three by name:

| Capability of row 1042 | Proof in 4A's plan |
|---|---|
| Allocation | `allocateSettlement` refuses an over-allocation — Σ lines greater than the settlement total, or greater than the settled document's open balance — with `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`, and `openBalance` after `unallocate` returns to the pre-allocation figure (§4.8.1) |
| Credit limits | an outbound sales type at `submitted → issued` over `party.credit_limit` raises `ERR_CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; it issues when a **second** principal has recorded an `accounting.credit_limit.override` `document_event`, and `party.credit_hold` blocks even with the override (§4.8.1, spec:2179) |
| Payment terms | `document.effective_date + payment_term.due_days` is the due date the ageing buckets are cut on — 4A asserts the derivation on the document, 4B's ageing tie-out then depends on it (§4.8.2) |
| Invoices, credit notes, receipts, payments | tests 10, 14 and 31, which 4A re-runs (§6.1) |
| Ageing | 4B, which owns test 8 and the Phase 4 DoD sentence |

Each of the first three is a DoD-bearing clause of 4A's card, so the row closes when 4A is green — the same standard as 1044, 1051, 1053 and 1054, applied to a row whose gap is a missing acceptance test rather than a missing "Proven by" cell.

Task 5 stamps it at claim and clears it the moment the call ends, in either direction _(PR 11 review, 2026-10-07: stamped `date_trunc('milliseconds', now())`, cleared only by a write that still matches the claim — `attempts` and `claimed_at` as the claim wrote them — so a call taken over after the window clears nothing; the claim reads the row `for no key update`)_, and a re-claim is refused only while it is set and younger than §4.2.9's 120-second window, reused rather than re-invented). **The two are separate columns and that is load-bearing:** one column cannot mean both "started and not yet finished" and "last finished", and conflating them refuses the `poll` that legitimately follows a `submit` seconds earlier and swallows every pg-boss retry that arrives inside the window. The fixture layering reflects the current repository: packages/db/test already consumes tax.ts. postFromPack delegates draft writes to postArDocument; the taxInclusive and computeTax options pass through both helpers. DocumentLineInput no longer accepts taxAmount or totalInclTax: those returned fields are server computed. Reversal and partial-credit headers preserve tax_inclusive.

### Phase 5 integration corrections (2026-10-02)

- `accounting.tax.submit` joins `STATELY_JOBS`. It uses `singletonKey = transmissionId` for submit and `<transmissionId>:poll` for poll. A completed/active submission must permit its next poll; the standard queue's 24-hour singleton throttle cannot implement this. The stately adapter collapses queued duplicates and permits one queued follow-up alongside an active job. ADR 0053 records this correction.
- Permission migration tests live in `tests/invariants/tax-permissions-{5a,5b}.test.ts`, where cross-package catalogue checks comply with dependency-rule. The line wire schema checks live in `packages/contracts/test/tax-document.test.ts`.
- Tax-code routes add `GET /{taxCodeId}` and the DB barrel exports `getTaxCode(tx, companyId, id)` for company-scoped reads and archive validation. All return and transmission resource routes validate the path company before acting.
- `postArDocument` passes through `taxInclusive` and `computeTax`; tax fixtures use real partial credit notes against quantity-bearing source invoices. `sourceFiles` supports file roots in addition to directories.
- The DB-tier e-invoice stub exports `postedStubDocument(db, seed)`; transmission tests use posted documents with valid policies and lines. The existing schema fingerprint helper has a test-support home with its old export preserved.


### Phase 5 verification corrections — 2026-10-02

- `loadTaxCodeRefs` accepts an optional historical source document ID. Corrections may resolve archived or expired codes only when immutable tax transactions prove their posted source used them; new invoices still require active, effective codes. Partial credit headers preserve `tax_inclusive`.
- `RegisteredTransmitter` outcomes additionally carry their own redacted `unmapped` status. The shared `lastCall` property is diagnostic only and never used to persist a different call's outcome. Known credential values are removed from response strings, keys, unknown statuses and network errors.
- Filing attachments must belong to the return's company; creating a return also verifies its regime's company. API path-company guards precede every ID-based read or mutation.
- The Phase 5 queue uses the existing stately adapter, with a submission key equal to the transmission ID and a poll key suffixed `:poll`. Active polls may enqueue their successor; duplicate queued polls collapse. The first poll waits 60 seconds and subsequent delays double up to one hour. The durable row bounds total attempts at twelve for automatic polling.
- API idempotency replays the stored JSON value and status; PostgreSQL JSONB may reorder object keys. Canonical return payloads remain strings and retain byte identity.
- The Phase 5A runbook's suggested handoff of a periodic return to `accounting.tax.submit` is reconciled with the frozen document-only job payload: that job transmits documents, while `tax-returns/{id}/file` records periodic filing.
- ADR 0051 is an unresolved requirements record until OD-15 is verified. A production profile requires its accepted verification record; creating a proposed record cannot satisfy the authority gate. No production authority profile or adapter ships in this change.

Additional edited integration surfaces: `apps/edge/src/env.ts` and `container-env.ts` (the enumerated credential binding), `apps/edge/test/containers.test.ts`, `packages/contracts/test/contracts.test.ts` (the four Phase 5 errors), `tests/invariants/role-catalogue.test.ts` (two accountant grants), and existing API write fixtures (server-derived tax fields removed from requests). No job name or report/dataset enum member is added.

- Final integration checks additionally update earlier database fixture expectations for the tax foreign key, two chart leaves and seventh sub-pack (`posting/load.test.ts`, `document-line-generalised.test.ts`, `seed-idempotent.test.ts`). The tax leaves use the existing one-digit group parents. Repeated pending-row insertion preserves the original transmitter; polling/cancellation require the submitted profile version and transmitter, and HTTP deadlines cover body reads.

- Earlier seed/mirror fixture lists (`roles-seed`, `schema-mirror`, `seed-chart`, `seed-packs`, `seed/templates`, `seed/phase4-pack`) include Phase 5 additions while preserving the Phase 3 snapshot in the historical upgrade test. Cross-tenant route probes expect uniform 403 from the existing company-first permission gate; requests using the caller's company with foreign IDs continue to expect 404.

## Phase 5A Task 12 integration reconciliation (2026-10-02)

The owner approved the documented default screen workflow in chat, overriding OD-24's screenshot prerequisite for this task alone. The sample imports do not match the shipped Phase 0 UI: there is no `ar-ap-api.ts`, `api-client.ts`, `DateField`, `MoneyText`, `ProblemAlert`, `Toolbar` or `SelectList`. The screen reuses `createAdminApi`, shared `TextField`/`Select`/`Button`/`DataGrid`, `useShell`, and `formatMoney` (decimal strings). Catalogues live in `packages/i18n/catalogues`, and the existing session provider supplies the company. No frozen shared export is renamed.

Tax browser acceptance runs through 0E’s local `bootLocalStack` with a synthetic tax pack and posted document produced by 5A’s registered `taxFixture`/`postTaxedDocument` helpers; `grantAdminRole` also grants `accounting.tax.manage`. These fixtures do not claim verified statutory tax data or staging acceptance.

## Phase 5B authority transport reconciliation (2026-10-02)

Under the owner's instruction to finish Phase 5 from A to Z, the verified public protocol gaps in ADR 0051 are implemented for review, with production activation still subject to its complete accepted requirement set. No company scope, legal identity, filing regime or certificate ownership is inferred.

- `EInvoiceAuthSpec` gains an explicit `oauth2_client_credentials` alternative with profile-data `tokenUrl` and optional scope. Existing bearer profiles remain unchanged. Token values are process-only, expire according to the response and are redacted alongside client secrets. Concurrent calls share token acquisition per credential identity; a 401 permits one refresh, while redirects carrying credentials are refused.
- `EInvoiceTransmitter.qrPayload` and `QrPayloadBuilder` accept additive optional `raw` receipt data. `submitTransmission` and `pollTransmission` pass their own response through that field. Existing builders need no change. The long validation identifier comes from the returned receipt, never a process-local lookup.
- `createHttpTransmitter` gains an optional protocol codec (request body/path-variable encoding and outcome decoding), using functions rather than a profile templating language. The public MyInvois protocol is supplied by `createMyInvoisTransport`; it requires an explicit canonicaliser, document encoder and verified profile. Company field mapping and signing are not silently replaced by the synthetic canonicaliser.
- MyInvois `externalId` is an opaque, versioned transport reference containing both submission UID and document UUID, encoded as base64url JSON. It occupies the existing text field, so polling/cancellation survive process restart without a new table, migration or in-memory identifier cache. API clients must not interpret external IDs as document UUIDs. The public validation link decodes the document UUID and uses the response's long ID.
- `verifyProfile` validates injected profiles and reports authentication refusal rather than treating any 401/403 as success. OAuth verification requires the client identifier explicitly or through the public `EINVOICE_CLIENT_ID` environment value; the secret remains an enumerated binding.
- Polling a remote `cancelled` outcome records `cancelled_at` so the durable row satisfies its state invariant. A cancellation response that does not confirm cancellation retains the prior accepted state and QR link, records the refusal and releases its claim. A failed cancellation operation does not invalidate the previously accepted invoice.

The reviewable authority profile draft lives in `docs/owner/od-15/`, outside the deployed profile directory. The accepted-ADR guard is retained: no runtime authority profile or automatic registration exists until the complete requirement set and immutable field/signature mapping are accepted. These additions do not alter tax arithmetic or mark OD-15 resolved.

## Phase 5 completion with plan defaults — owner direction, 2026-10-02

The owner instructed: “please refer to the plan of the phase 5, if you did not find something, choose the best practice form your side.” The implementation uses the plan's stated fallback where external facts are absent: `SYNTH-MY-v1`, the synthetic loopback transmitter, e-invoicing disabled by default on companies, and the local PostgreSQL deployment rehearsal. The separate approval of 5A T12's default operator workflow remains in force.

5A T10 explicitly permits omitting the statutory regime and seed pair without dropping any interface. 5B T9 explicitly permits the synthetic port/profile while OD-15 remains pending. 5B T11 Step 4 states that the missing staging target never blocks merge and supplies the local equivalent. Completion of this scope does not assert statutory applicability, accept ADRs 0049/0051, fabricate credentials or enable an authority profile. Live statutory and deployment work remains deferred under those same defaults rather than blocking the default Phase 5 implementation.

The verifier's optional `baseUrl` override and CLI `--base-url` option permit the synthetic loopback stub's actual ephemeral port to be checked without editing its pinned profile file. The override is confined to the `synthetic` code and an explicit `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin; it cannot redirect an authority profile or credentials to a non-loopback URL. It affects the verification probe only, not transmitter registration or application settings.

## Phase 6D owning amendments (2026-10-09)

These implement the authorised Phase 6 defaults. A13, A16 and the conditional portions of A14 remain inactive because OD-10 is excluded; no fourth sync array, banking-link table or 0071 migration is added.

**2026-11-04 — OD-10 answered yes (`docs/owner/od-10/decision.md`); A13, A14 and A16 are now active and implemented** (6D Tasks 9–11, ADR 0064 proposed). Three implementation notes against the amendment text: (1) `TicketBatch.cashEvents` is **optional** on the wire (`cashEvents?: TillCashMsg[]`, Zod `.optional()`), and the till sends the key only when it has a cash event, so a till with none emits exactly the three-array batch a server without A13 accepts; `BatchResult.cashEventResults` is always sent and a reader defaults it to `[]`. (2) The batch order is opens → tickets → till events → **cash events** → closes. (3) A paid-out authorised above `max_paid_out_amount` records the supervisor's `pos.ticket.override` as a `document_event` override on the paid-out (2B's `assert_override_authorised`), as a void's does; a paid-out requires a non-empty `reference` (the owner's fact 4). The `till_banking` `Reconcilable` source lists from `app.till_banking_link`, restricted, like 4B's, to live matches on that bank account's own statements. `5130` is seeded in `6d-till.json` with `parentCode "5"`, as `5120` is. The till's local schema is version 3 (a `cash_event` table and the `cash_event` outbox kind; an older file's outbox is rebuilt under the new CHECK with every row kept).

**A1 — §4.6.5 `app.shift` gains three foreign keys and one index.** *"**6D amendment A1.** §4.6.5's DDL omits three composite keys the §4.6 preamble requires of every register row, and 6D's migration 0070 adds them: `foreign key (tenant_id, branch_id) references app.dimension_value(tenant_id, id)` (the same key `pos_cashier` and `branch_pos_policy` carry, §4.6.3–§4.6.4), `foreign key (tenant_id, over_short_document_id) references app.document(tenant_id, id)`, and the index `shift_branch_opened_idx on app.shift (company_id, branch_id, opened_at desc)` the Z-report-history parameter shape reads. `opened_principal_id` and `closed_principal_id` keep their plain FK to `app.principal`, which is a `GLOBAL_TABLES` member and therefore exempt from `composite_fk` (§4.1). Everything else in §4.6.5 is implemented verbatim, `id uuid primary key` **without** a `default uuidv7()` included — the id is minted at the till, and the `id_column` linter rule checks only that the column exists (plan0A:2748)."*

**A2 — §4.3.4: the `shift_id` column belongs to 6A's 0061, not to 6D's 0070, and 6D adds no foreign key on it.** *"**6D amendment A2.** §4.3.4's header-additions paragraph assigns `shift_id uuid` to **6D (0070)**. That assignment is superseded: **6A's 0061 adds the column**, because 6A's `applyTicket` step (f) writes `document.shift_id` on every `POS_TICKET` it inserts (6A's Task 11) and 6A's own **Task 0 amendment 6** moves the column into **its Task 4, migration 0061**, for exactly that reason — that amendment is 6A's half of this agreement and the two plans land the same words. A 0061 without it cannot pass 6A's batch suite, so '6A merged and green' — which is 6D's phase gate — already implies the column exists; **6D's Task 0 gate asserts it by literal and, if it is absent, raises against 6A rather than adding it in 0070.** §4.3.4's paragraph is corrected to read `6A (0061)` `terminal_id uuid` (FK `pos_terminal`) **and `shift_id uuid` (no FK)**, with the 6D entry removed. **0070 deliberately adds no foreign key to it, and no later migration in this slice's range does either.** Two facts make a validated key impossible at 0070: a migration cannot backfill the missing parents, because `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` binds `app_migrator` and a migration file has no `set_config` (hazard 10); and PostgreSQL's referential-integrity checks **bypass** row security, so the constraint's validation scan would see every pre-6D `POS_TICKET` written between 6B's release and 6D's, each naming a shift that has no row. The reference is enforced instead in the apply path — `assertShiftKnown` in `packages/db/src/sync/shifts.ts` refuses a ticket whose `shiftId` names no shift **of that terminal**, so no new orphan is created — exactly the shape §4.3.4 already uses for the `item_id` and `tax_code_id` slots. The key belongs in a **contract** migration in a later slice (§3.4.7), once every till has re-sent the shift-open messages 6A held in its outbox; this slice does not schedule it and no plan may add it without amending this paragraph."*

**A3 — §4.6.5's `expected_cash` sentence is completed.** *"**6D amendment A3.** §4.6.5 says `expected_cash` is *'derived server-side: opening_float + Σ cash tenders − Σ paid-outs/safe-drops of this shift's posted tickets'*. 6D implements that as **one read of `app.ledger_entry`**, which is both simpler and the thing test 21 actually asserts: `expected_cash = opening_float + Σ(debit − credit)` over `ledger_entry` rows whose `account_id` is the company's `1110` Cash in till, whose `currency` **equals `shift.currency`** (the count is a physical count in one currency, so a base-currency sum would tie in the wrong money), and whose `document_id` belongs to a **posted** document with this `shift_id` and a `document_type.code` other than `TILL_OVER_SHORT`. Every cash movement of the shift is then included by construction — tickets, refunds, and ⚠️ OD-10's paid-outs, safe drops and bankings — and no formula has to be extended when OD-10 lands. `TILL_OVER_SHORT` is excluded because it is posted *from* this figure. `over_short = counted_cash − expected_cash`, **positive is over**, unchanged."*

**A4 — §4.2.5 / §3.6.2: 6A's `POS_PERMISSION` gains two members.** *"**6D amendment A4.** `packages/db/src/sync/authority.ts` (6A) is the one home of the `pos.*` code literals reachable from `packages/db`, which may not import `@dulja/contracts` (§3.1). 6D widens it additively by `shiftOwn: \"pos.shift.own\"` (**6B's** catalogue row, consumed here) and `shiftCloseAny: \"pos.shift.close_any\"` (**6D's** row), and adds the two matching `null` entries to `OVERRIDE_SUBJECT_FOR`, whose type is `Readonly<Record<PosPermissionCode, …>>` and therefore does not compile without them. `null` is the right value in both: no supervisor's override lets a cashier close a shift they may not close — that is an authority gap, not a limit (6C's decision (d))."*

**A5 — §4.16.3 gains 6D's two report readers.** *"**6D amendment A5.** The Phase 1 report surface 7B/7C re-express grows by 6D's two, in `packages/db/src/reports/pos.ts`, exported from `@dulja/db`: `zReport(tx: Sql, params: ZReportParams): Promise<ZReport[]>` with `ZReportParams { companyId: string; shiftId?: string; branchId?: string; from?: string; to?: string; limit: number; cursor?: { openedAt: string; shiftId: string } | null }`, and `salesByCashier(tx: Sql, params: SalesByCashierParams): Promise<SalesByCashierRow[]>` with `SalesByCashierParams { companyId: string; from: string; to: string; branchId?: string; cashierPrincipalId?: string; limit: number; cursor?: { cashierPrincipalId: string } | null }`. The row shapes `ZReport`, `ZReportTender` and `SalesByCashierRow` are §4.16.3 members like `TrialBalanceRow`. **One code, two parameter shapes:** `pos.z_report` with `shiftId` returns exactly one Z-report; with `from`/`to` it returns the shift history §4.16.1 names, which is why the reader returns an array in both cases. 7C re-expresses both codes over these same functions and re-runs 6D's tie-out test unchanged. **6D adds no `DatasetId` member** — `shift` and `till_event` are 7C's rows in the frozen union (§4.16.2)."*

**A6 — §4.17.1: `posFixture` opens a shift.** *"**6D amendment A6.** 6A's `tests/invariants/support/pos.ts` exports a module-level `SHARED_SHIFT_ID` and writes it into every ticket's `document.shift_id`, noting that `app.shift` is 6D's and 'the constant is what keeps 6D's first task from having to re-key every 6A test'. 6D therefore has `posFixture` insert **one open `app.shift` row at that id** — terminal `f.terminal.terminalId`, cashier `f.cashierId`, `opening_float` `\"0.0000\"`, the company's base currency — and exposes it as `PosFixture.shiftId`. Every existing 6A and 6C test keeps passing unchanged, and `assertShiftKnown` (amendment A2) has a parent to find. No other member of `PosFixture` changes."*

**A7 — §4.17.1: `StaffFixture` gains two members.** *"**6D amendment A7.** 6C's `tests/invariants/support/staff.ts` builds branch A and B with three cashiers. 6D adds `shiftA: string` (an open shift at branch A on `terminalA`, opened by `cashierA`) and `openShift(opts: { cashierPrincipalId: string; openingFloat?: string }): Promise<string>`, so a test needing a second shift does not re-derive the insert. Both are additive; no existing member changes."*

**A8 — §3.6.4: the two role grants 6D records.** *"**6D amendment A8.** `pos.shift.close_any` → **`branch_manager`** (spec:2160 gives the branch manager 'closing any shift and the Z-report'). `pos.report.read` → **`branch_manager`** (the same clause) **and `auditor`** (spec:2163 'Read everything financial: ledger, documents, reports, stock and costs … export'; the code is `mutating: false`, so R7 holds and `role-seed` stays green). It is **not** granted to `accountant`, `user` or `cashier`: spec:2161 gives the cashier no report code at all, and the accountant's row names no POS report — a tenant that wants head office to read Z-reports clones a role under `admin.role.manage`, which is what §4.2.1's 'a tenant may clone one' is for. `admin`'s array is computed from `PERMISSIONS` and gains both automatically."*

**A9 — §3.7.3: acceptance test 21's file is `tests/invariants/`, not `tests/e2e/`.** *"**6D amendment A9.** §3.7.3 places tests 20 and 21 in `tests/e2e/`. Test 21 is a **data** assertion — a Z-report compared to `ledger_entry` to the cent — which needs Testcontainers, the real `applyBatch` and the real `postDocument`, and no browser; a Playwright test cannot read `app.ledger_entry` at all. It therefore lives at **`tests/invariants/pos-shift-reconciliation.test.ts`**, beside the other invariant suites, and `tests/e2e/` carries only the screen half, which is 6D's ⚠️ OD-24 task and re-runs **test 23**, not test 21. Test 20 is unaffected and stays where 6A put it."*

**A10 — §4.10.3: a refused shift, till event or cash event writes no `needs_attention` row.** *"**6D amendment A10.** 6A's `app.needs_attention` has `client_ref uuid not null` and `unique (company_id, client_ref)`, and its `payload` is documented as the whole **ticket**. A `ShiftOpenClose` is acked by `\"<shiftId>:<kind>\"`, which is not a uuid, so it cannot be keyed there at all; and for the uuid-keyed message kinds the queue would mix two different objects under one `payload` contract. 6D therefore writes **no** `needs_attention` row for any non-ticket message: a refused message answers `rejected`, `drainOutbox` acks only refs that appear in a result array, and the till's outbox row stays pending (spec:1337) — which is the recovery path, and is 'never lost' without widening 6A's queue. A later slice that wants a shop-visible queue for these adds a `ref text` column and a `kind` discriminator to `needs_attention`, which is a §4.10.3 amendment."*

**A11 — §4.2.7: one new route module.** *"**6D amendment A11.** Append to the module-path register: `/v1/companies/:companyId/shifts` · `shiftRoutes` (module const `shiftRouteModule`) · **6D** · `pos.report.read`. Sub-paths: `GET …/shifts`, `GET …/shifts/{shiftId}`, `GET …/shifts/{shiftId}/till-events`. It gets **one** `PROBES` entry keyed on its `RouteModule.path` (hazard 31). The two report `GET`s — `…/reports/pos.z_report` and `…/reports/pos.sales_by_cashier` — are **sub-paths of 1B's existing `reports` module** and add no key; `reportsRouteModule.permissions` gains `pos.report.read` in the same PR, because that module now evaluates two codes."*

**A12 — §4.6.5: there is no back-office force-close, and the gap is recorded.** *"**6D amendment A12.** A shift is closed **only** by a `ShiftOpenClose { kind: \"close\" }` arriving over `/v1/sync/tickets`, because §4.14 fixes `TILL_OVER_SHORT.approval.post = pos.sync.push` and R8 (spec:2179) keeps a human out of the `pos_terminal` role: a branch manager's request-path close could not post the difference. `pos.shift.close_any` is therefore evaluated **on the sync path** — the closer is `ShiftOpenClose.cashierPrincipalId`, and closing a shift someone else opened requires it while closing one's own requires `pos.shift.own` — which is exactly spec:2161's distinction between the cashier who 'may not close others' shifts' and the branch manager who may. **Known gap:** a till destroyed mid-shift leaves an open shift no one can close. Closing it needs a request-gated route whose posting runs under `systemContext` from a job, and `JOBS` is a closed sixteen-name registry (§4.2.6) — so the fix is a new job name and an amendment there, not a route a plan can add quietly."*

**A13 — ⚠️ §4.10.1 gains a fourth message array (OD-10 only).** *"**6D amendment A13.** If OD-10 = yes, `TicketBatch` gains `cashEvents: TillCashMsg[]` and `BatchResult` gains `cashEventResults: MessageResult[]`, with `export interface TillCashMsg { clientRef: string; shiftId: string; kind: \"paid_out\" | \"safe_drop\" | \"banking\"; amount: { amount: string; currency: string }; cashierPrincipalId: string; supervisorPrincipalId: string | null; occurredAt: string; reference: string | null; fromSafe: boolean }`, acked by `clientRef`. `outbox.kind`'s CHECK in §4.10.6 becomes `('ticket','shift','till_event','cash_event')`. Every edit is additive: a client that sends three arrays and reads three arrays is unaffected, `applyBatch`'s signature is unchanged (`TicketBatchInput.cashEvents?: unknown[]` is optional), and `SyncStore.markAcked` matches a fourth result array the same way it matches the other three. **The alternative — back-office routes for the three till-cash documents — was rejected because §4.14 fixes their `approval.post` at `pos.sync.push`, so only a terminal can post them.** If OD-10 = no, nothing in this amendment is written and §4.10.1 is untouched."*

**A14 — §4.15: what `1130` and `5130` actually carry.** *"**6D amendment A14.** `1130` Cash in transit is debited by ⚠️ `TILL_SAFE_DROP` (cash out of a drawer into the branch safe, still the company's and not yet the bank's) and credited by ⚠️ `TILL_BANKING` when the deposit is made from the safe (`TillCashMsg.fromSafe = true`); a banking straight from the drawer credits `1110` instead. **`TILL_BANKING` always debits `1100` Bank**, which is what makes it visible to 4B's `ledgerLegSource` — that source lists from the ledger leg on the **statement's own** `bank_account_id`, so a banking with no `1100` leg could never be matched and test 39's 'the reconciled balance equals the bank account's ledger balance' clause could not hold. The row for `1130` stays seeded **unconditionally**, exactly as §4.15 already says, so a manual banking journal has an account to clear when OD-10 = no. `5130` Till paid out is debited by ⚠️ `TILL_PAID_OUT`, tagged BRANCH, and is dropped with the type if OD-10 = no."*

**A15 — §4.14: 6A's `resolveSeries` suffixes *every* document that carries a `terminal_id`, so the four till series are `TOS-<terminal code>`, not `TOS`.** *"**6D amendment A15.** §4.14 gives `TILL_OVER_SHORT` the series `TOS` and only `POS_TICKET` the note 'series per terminal'. 6A's `resolveSeries` (`packages/db/src/posting/issue.ts`) is **generic** — it joins `app.pos_terminal` on `document.terminal_id` and returns `` `${policySeries}-${code}` `` whenever that join finds a row, with no test on the document type — so any document 6D posts through the sync path with `terminal_id` set is numbered in a **per-terminal** series. That is the right behaviour and 6D does not change it: two tills closing the same day would otherwise contend on one `document_series` advisory lock for their over/short documents, and a gapless series per terminal is what makes `TOS-<code>` #1…#n a readable audit trail of one drawer. The register's `Series` column is therefore the **policy** series (`policy.numbering.series`), and `document.series` for a terminal-borne document is that string plus `-<pos_terminal.code>`. This binds `TOS` and ⚠️ `TPO`/`TSD`/`TBK` alike. A slice asserting a bare `TOS` on a posted document has read the register and not `resolveSeries`."*

**A16 — ⚠️ §4.6.1 and §3.5.3 gain the `till_banking_link` row (OD-10 only).** *"**6D amendment A16.** §2.7's 6D card names `0071_create_till_banking_link.sql` but neither §4.6.1's register nor §3.5.3's linter table has a row for the table, so 6D fixes both here. **§4.6.1:** `till_banking_link` | 6D / 0071 ⚠️ | `company_id`, `branch_id uuid not null`, `banking_document_id uuid not null unique`, `shift_id uuid not null`, `bank_account_id uuid not null`, `from_safe boolean not null`, `value_date date not null`, `amount numeric(19,4) not null check (amount > 0)`, `currency char(3) not null`, `reference text`; Form A `branch_isolation`; audited; immutable **after** insert is *not* claimed — the row is never updated but carries no `forbid_change` trigger, because 4B's `bank_match` (not this row) records a match and the row has nothing left to change. **§3.5.3:** `till_banking_link` | 6D | `NO_ID_TABLES` — | `NO_CREATED_AT_TABLES` — | `AUDIT_EXEMPT` — | `IMMUTABLE` —. **Why the table exists at all rather than reading the `TILL_BANKING` document:** `Reconcilable` (§4.8.3) needs `bankAccountId` and `valueDate` per banking, and a `TILL_BANKING` document reaches its bank account only through its `1100` ledger leg — which is exactly what 4B's `ledgerLegSource` reads, and 6D's source copies that shape. The link row carries the **shift** the banking came from, which no ledger leg does, and that is the one fact the Z-report's banking line and the DoD's 'ties to the ledger' clause both need. If OD-10 = no, neither row is written and §4.6.1/§3.5.3 are untouched."*

**A17 — §4.17: `seedShift` gains three additive options.** *"**6D amendment A17.** The register's 6D row reads `seedShift(db, s, opts: { terminalId; cashierPrincipalId; openingFloat? }) → string`. 6D ships it as `seedShift(db, s, opts: { terminalId; cashierPrincipalId; openingFloat?; currency?; branchId?; shiftId? }) → string` — three optional additions, no existing parameter or return changed, recorded here in the same PR as §4.17's own rule requires. Each is load-bearing: **`shiftId`** lets amendment A6's `posFixture` open the shift at 6A's `SHARED_SHIFT_ID` rather than minting a new one every ticket would then have to be re-keyed against; **`branchId`** lets amendment A7's `StaffFixture.openShift` open a shift at branch A when the `Seed`'s default is the HQ value; **`currency`** lets Task 3's wrong-currency cases build a shift whose `currency` differs from the message's without touching the company. Defaults are `openingFloat "0.0000"`, `currency "MYR"`, `branchId s.hq`, `shiftId` a fresh `uuidv7`. **The helper inserts under `withTenant(db.migrator, s.tenant, s.system, …)` and not under `db.rw`/`s.human`**, which is the second half of this amendment and is not a style choice: `app.shift` carries Form A's restrictive `branch_isolation` policy, `app.actor_in_branch` is true only for a `kind = 'system'` principal or a principal with a live `role_assignment` in the company, and `seedTenant` grants `s.human` nothing (§4.1, pinned) — a policy declared with `using` alone is also applied as `with check` on INSERT, so an `s.human` insert fails with `new row violates row-level security policy for table \"shift\"`. §4.17's preamble sentence 'helpers insert on `db.rw` inside `withTenant(sql, s.tenant, s.human, …)` unless the row is catalog-level' gains a second exception clause: **or unless the row's table carries a `branch_isolation` policy** (6C's `seedCashier` writes its `app.principal` half the same way, 6C Task 2 Step 8)."*

**A18 — §4.5.8: `MODULE_READ_CODE` lives at the middleware path 2C actually used.** *"**6D amendment A18.** §4.5.8's prose places `MODULE_READ_CODE` in `apps/api/src/routes/accounting/attachments.ts`. **2C shipped it in `apps/api/src/middleware/require-attachment-read.ts`** (2c:133's file tree, 2c:1796's Produces block, 2c:1992's implementation, and 2c:1818 — its own test's import), and 3A added its `inventory` row there. §4.18 makes the written plan the authority for what it exports, so §4.5.8's path is corrected to the middleware file and every later slice that adds a row — **6D's `pos`, 8B's `hr`** — edits that file. A slice following the old path would declare a *second* `MODULE_READ_CODE` in a file that has none, leave the real map without its row, and ship a module whose attachment downloads keep hitting 2C's default deny while every test of the new map passes. That is hazard 32 (one literal, one home) applied to a map rather than to a code."*


The Task 0 seed prerequisite consumes 0C’s actual `seed` export at `packages/db/src/seed/index.ts`; this checkout has no `runSeed` test helper. Pack proofs call the existing seed/loaders with a stub auth administrator rather than adding a second seed entry point.

6D preserves the current 6C all-null `OVERRIDE_SUBJECT_FOR` authority registry; only the two shift entries are added. Its copied permission row has an `action` field absent from the actual table/catalogue, so 0072 uses their existing four-field shape.

A6 implementation correction: the old module-global `SHARED_SHIFT_ID` cannot be inserted once per tenant because `app.shift.id` is globally unique. Each `PosFixture` instead owns a fresh `shiftId`; `buildTicket(f)` defaults to that fixture id. The exported old constant remains for compatibility but is not inserted or used as the default. No existing test must supply its own shift or fake a missing parent. The real batch suite lives in API/acceptance files in this checkout, rather than the nonexistent copied `packages/db/test/sync/apply.test.ts`.

6D shift integrity corrections: a fresh open verifies the company's currency, live branch cashier credential and that cashier's `pos.shift.own` grant. A duplicate is acknowledged only when the persisted shift belongs to this signed terminal/branch; an invisible or other-terminal primary-key collision must be rejected, not silently acknowledged. New tickets require an open shift of the acting terminal; already-posted ticket replays still deduplicate before this check. The copied open-or-closed reference check would allow new ledger movement after `expected_cash` and the Z-report were fixed. POS withholds close until all completed ticket and till-event messages of the shift are acknowledged; refused tickets therefore keep close pending. A close cannot assert it covers tickets the server never received. `ShiftOpenCloseSchema` is strict, like the batch's other messages: a shift message carrying `expectedCash`, `overShort` or any other unknown key is refused 400 `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED` with the whole batch, as ADR 0063 states, rather than stripped and answered `accepted` (PR 12 plan audit, 2026-10-22). The till already sends exactly the eight keys; `openapi.json`'s `shifts` items gain `additionalProperties: false`.

6D Task 5’s real API/stock/ledger close integration runs at `tests/invariants/pos-shift-close.test.ts`, preserving the DB production dependency boundary. The copied DB test imports the API workspace and fails the existing dependency rule. It uses actual branch cashier credentials and the source document’s effective date for reversal, rather than an uncredentialed manager or a January date preceding today’s sale.

6D void correction: inserting a `till_event(kind='void')` alone does not cancel a posted ticket's ledger or stock. A posted-ticket void must invoke the existing `reverseDocument` under the acting terminal, carrying the original shift/terminal through the existing POS reversal path; it then records the immutable event in the same savepoint. It requires the cashier's live `pos.ticket.void` grant, the branch void cap, and a different live override supervisor above that cap. `TillEventMsg` gains optional `reason?: string | null` (required nonblank for void); no-sale/drawer-open remain nonfinancial and require live shift authority. An event may target only a POS ticket of this terminal and shift. Rejected reversal, including prior partial returns, rolls back the event. Batch order becomes opens → tickets → events → closes so a close includes its batch's actual reversals. Event replay deduplicates before checking the now-closed shift, with persisted terminal/branch ownership verified. A local unsubmitted draft cancellation is a separate main-process action: retain its ticket/line/local audit rows, remove only its unsent draft outbox intent atomically, and never pretend that a server document or financial reversal existed.

6D report corrections: sales-by-cashier rows group by cashier and branch, including the branch in revenue, discount and shortfall joins; choosing `min(branch_id)` would mislabel a company-wide total as one branch. Its cursor is therefore `{cashierPrincipalId,branchId}` and orders both fields. Shift history and shift-close attribution use the company timezone for date boundaries, matching ticket effective dates. Database timestamp text is normalised to millisecond ISO timestamps for the wire DTO. A keyset cursor carries the row's instant at the microsecond instead — `to_char(… at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')` — and binds it `::text::timestamptz`, because a `$n::timestamptz` parameter is serialised by postgres.js through a JS `Date` and cut to the millisecond (PR 12 plan audit, 2026-10-22). The precision is defensive, not a repair of till data: the sync write path binds a till's `at` and `occurredAt` the same way (`${msg.at}::timestamptz`, `${msg.occurredAt}::timestamptz`), so every shift and till event a till syncs is stored at a whole millisecond — any finer fraction `TimestampSchema` admits is dropped on write — and for those rows the millisecond cursor, tie-broken by id, was already exact. Only a row whose instant SQL wrote itself (`now()`, as the `seedShift` test helper does, or a later writer that is not the sync path) holds microseconds, and a millisecond cursor would skip (newest first) or repeat (oldest first) such rows within one millisecond. `zReport`'s `openedAt` is that exact key, so a db-tier caller pages by feeding the row's own `openedAt` back. T7's real report integration uses `tests/invariants/pos-reports.test.ts` for the same dependency-boundary reason as T5.

### Phase 6D report directory gates
The five report/shift GETs use the existing `staffBranchGate(pos.report.read)` directory gate, admitting a live branch assignment before the restrictive branch RLS filters rows. A company-only permission question incorrectly refuses the planned branch-manager role. Resource visibility continues to return 404.

### Phase 6D final verification corrections
T13 asserts the existing Form A policy composition: the tenant policy is PERMISSIVE and the branch policy RESTRICTIVE, with FORCE RLS enabled. PostgreSQL requires a permissive policy to admit any row, then ANDs restrictive policies; the copied claim that both policies are restrictive contradicts 0A's enable_tenant_rls procedure. No policy is weakened. The actual JOBS register is in @dulja/db; sharedApi returns {api,a,b}.
Local referenced returns and void intents reserve their source against each other: a till cannot queue a void for a sale with an unfinished/completed return, or queue a return after a void intent. The server reversal service remains the final financial authority. The T12 Z-report is an activated detail pane within the shift register; changing company/branch/date/page clears selection. It uses the accepted default screen scope rather than claiming legacy parity.

The cashier report includes principals who closed a shift even when they sold no tickets, so a manager close_any difference is not dropped. Its row key is still principal plus branch; revenue/discount remain separate ticket aggregates and the cashier filter applies to the combined actor set.

SAH-047 now distinguishes actual HTTP, server apply and till-only gates. pos.price.check is evaluated by the shipped main-process pricing/IPC path; it does not gain a fictional HTTP route permission just to satisfy the old all-server assertion. 6D shift own/close_any are verified in the shifts apply service.

pos.attendance.clock is checked in both the main clock handler and the sync apply attendance loop against the attendance principal, rather than an HTTP route or the ticket code map; SAH-047 verifies both registered locations.

**A2 ⚠️ — §4.16.1, what "re-expresses" does to the route (a settlement).** *"**Re-expression does not rewrite the JSON list route.** For a minimal-set code the owning slice's `GET` handler, its `<Resource>List` envelope and its DTOs **stand byte-for-byte**; the re-expressing slice seeds the `ReportDefinition` at `definitionVersion = 2`, which is what gives the code a PDF/XLSX/CSV render path (7A's `POST …/reports/{code}/runs`) and a designer entry, and adds a **parity** case proving the definition-driven rows (through `rowsForDefinition`) equal the owning slice's read function row for row and figure for figure. **How a wrong field fails — two mechanical checks, not one.** `validateReportDefinition` (`packages/domain/src/reports/validate.ts`) checks `groups[]`, `totals[]` and `sort[]` against the definition's **own** `columns[]` (its rule 4) and never against the dataset, which `packages/domain` cannot see. **The dataset half is 7A's `assertDefinitionFields`** (`packages/db/src/reports/statement.ts`), which throws `ReportError("ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED", "dataset '<source>' has no such field: …")` for any field in `columns[]`, `groups[]`, `totals[]`, `sort[]` or `dataset.filters[]` the dataset's declared list (plus `STATEMENT_EXTRA_FIELDS` for a `STATEMENT_CODES` key) lacks, from both write paths — the definition store and the seed loader. **`assertFieldCoverage` (7B Task 1) is the third check, against the rows the query actually returns**, so a column declared but not selected fails with its name. A definition that passed only one has not been proved.

**A4 — §4.16.3, `ReportCodeSchema` after 7B.** *"**7B widens it by its seventeen** — `accounting.general_ledger`, `accounting.journal_register`, `accounting.account_statement`, `accounting.period_comparison`, `accounting.profit_and_loss`, `accounting.balance_sheet`, `accounting.document_register`, `accounting.audit_log`, `accounting.document_event_log`, `inventory.stock_ageing`, `inventory.movement_register`, `inventory.expiry_list`, `inventory.price_list`, `inventory.promotion_register`, `inventory.transfer_register`, `inventory.count_register`, `inventory.profit_by_item` — **appended after whatever members already exist**. The five codes 7B re-expresses are already members and are not touched. **Membership in this enum is not what makes a code runnable**: 7A's `POST …/reports/{code}/runs` validates `{code}` with `z.string().regex(REPORT_CODE_PATTERN)` and answers 404 when no definition resolves for a caller who has already cleared the export gate; the enum is the *typed* surface and the seeded definition the *runtime* surface. **The route's gate order is `reportExportRequestGate` (`requireReportExport`, route middleware) → `resolveDefinitionForRun` → `requireReportRead` → `assertParameters`**, so a caller with no codes gets **403** whether or not the definition exists, and every 404 case grants first."* **No slice asserts a total member count.** The enum holds eight members when 7B starts (1B 2, 3D 3, 4B 1, and 6D's `pos.z_report` and `pos.sales_by_cashier`, since Phase 6 merged first), so 7B ends at twenty-five; every assertion is membership plus the §4.16.1 register check. **A module list endpoint is not a `ReportCode`, and 7B retires neither of the two reads over `app.stock_on_hand`**: 3A's `GET …/stock-on-hand` (`listStockOnHand` / `StockOnHandRow`) lists the table, 3D's `inventory.stock_on_hand` (`stockOnHand` / `StockOnHandReportRow`) answers "what is on my shelves", both read the projection, and the fact that two functions read one projection is not itself a finding.

**A5 — §4.11.1, `tieOut` made executable (ADR 0068's contract half).** *"**What each `kind` means to the harness that executes it** (7B, `tests/invariants/support/reports.ts`; 7C's and 8D's codes extend it):"*

- **`ledger_sum`** — Σ of the report's **first `totals` entry whose column `format` is `money`**, accumulated with `Money.add`, equals a direct `tx` sum of **the same measure** over `app.ledger_entry` for the test's window, restricted to `account.code = tieOut.account` when present. **The measure map is closed** and is a lookup among four fixed columns of one query, never a SQL fragment: `debit` = `sum(base_debit)`, `credit` = `sum(base_credit)`, `net` = `sum(base_debit − base_credit)`, `credit_net` = `sum(base_credit − base_debit)`. 7B's keys: `base_debit` → `debit`, `base_credit` → `credit`, `base_balance` → `net`, `base_total` → `debit`. Any other first money total is refused naming the field. `debit` and `credit` are gross and unsigned; `net` and `credit_net` are signed, chosen by the natural balance of the account tied against. **A signed field is never mapped to `credit`.** A slice adding a signed measure adds a `credit_net` key, never a fifth arm.
- **`projection`** — `tieOut.projection ∈ account_balance | stock_on_hand | stock_valuation | item_profitability | party_ageing`: the report's rows, grouped on the projection's key, equal the projection's stored figures read by the test's own SQL — except that `stock_valuation` compares against `valuationAsOf`, the one implementation the snapshot stores (spec:1228). **That branch serves two row shapes**: a `stock_valuation`-dataset report compares its `value` column; a `cost_layer`-dataset report — whose `value` is the layer's *receipt* value, not its residue (A3) — has the harness value each layer's residue as `round(value × qty_remaining / qty_in, 4)` with `Money` and an exact `Rational`, which is the per-layer term `valuationAsOf` itself sums since migration 0118 (ADR 0039's approved exact-value amendment). That arithmetic lives in the harness, once, over the layer's own stored facts; no report definition performs it.
- **`none`** — only for a report with no monetary or quantity total, and the harness then requires a **row witness**: an independent `tx` query supplied by the group test whose row set the report's rows must equal on a declared key. **`none` never means "no test"**; a `none` definition with no witness case fails `report-tie-out.test.ts` naming its code.

**A6 — §2.8 (7A card) and §4.16.1, the two financial statements are company-level.** *"**7B's `accounting.profit_and_loss` and `accounting.balance_sheet` are company-level, over `account_balance`, and are not hand-written: each is exactly `statementDefinition(kind, identity)`**"* with `identity = { code, nameEn, nameAr, permission: "accounting.report.read" }`; every other member — the `fiscalPeriodId` parameter, the single `fiscal_period_id eq` filter, the four columns `section` / `account_code` / `account_name_en` / `base_balance`, the `section` group, the `base_balance` sum, the `section, account_code` sort, the A4 layout (`"{title} — {fiscalPeriodId}"` / `"{rowCount} accounts · {generatedAt}"`) and `tieOut: { kind: "ledger_sum" }` — is the return of 7A's `build(opts)`; a definition differing in any member is a defect and 7B's group test asserts deep equality. **`section` is a row annotation, so a statement definition is executed through `rowsForDefinition` (which dispatches a `STATEMENT_CODES` key to `statementRows`), never through `datasetFor("account_balance").run`**; on that branch `dataset.filters` are not consulted, so a local `account_type` filter would be dropped silently, and 7B keeps no code→kind map of its own. The BRANCH cut is 7C's `accounting.branch_profit_and_loss` (`statementDefinition("profit_and_loss", identity, { perBranch: true })`). **Both are one fiscal period's movement, not a cumulative position**: `account_balance` is keyed per period, so the single `eq` filter returns the period's movement, and the declared identity is Σ`base_balance`(balance sheet) + Σ`base_balance`(P&L) = `0.0000` for the period. Two presentation defects in 7A's fragment — the header interpolates the raw period uuid, and the column reads "Balance" where a movement wants "Movement (net)" — are **raised against 7A, not patched**, and a cumulative as-of balance sheet (a period-ordinal `lte` or a `period_ends_on` column on 7A's dataset) is an open item for 7A's file, which 7B does not edit.

**A17 — §3.4.1, the report-filter indexes.** 0077 creates indexes for the report-filter columns 7B's definitions filter by that no existing index serves, and nothing else. A filter column on a table a later slice owns is excluded from 7B's gate by a named entry carrying the owning slice and the reason, never by leaving the gate red. *"**The exemption list is closed at merge**"*: every entry is a row in 7B's Self-Review and in its "what the next slice needs" section.

**A17 as executed (7B Task 10, 2026-11-05).** The gate (`packages/db/test/reports/7b-report-indexes.test.ts`) judges **seekability**, not "the column is in some `Index Cond`" (Postgres pushes a qual on any key column of a chosen index into its `Index Cond`, so `inventory_movement_chrono_idx` "served" a company-wide date range by reading every item) and not "the planner's chosen index" (on a fixture where a table holds one row every index costs the same, so the choice is a tie-break). **Determinative:** a valid, non-partial btree index has the column as a key with every earlier key bound by equality — the scope column (`company_id`; `tenant_id` for `audit_log`; none for `price_list_line`, which has no company column) plus a `with` column only where every definition using the pair requires it by `eq` (`account_balance.currency` with `fiscal_period_id`, `cost_layer.warehouse_id` with `item_id`, `stock_valuation.warehouse_id` with `as_of`; the gate checks each claim). Partial indexes do not count, because a definition filter cannot state `is null`. **Corroborating:** with `enable_seqscan = off` a probe binding an absent value of the column's type plans no `Seq Scan`. The map's key set equals the definitions' filter pairs in both directions. **Twenty pairs were unserved; 0077 holds fourteen indexes**, not the plan's four: `document (company_id, effective_date)`, `(company_id, document_type_id, effective_date)`, `(company_id, branch_id, effective_date)`; `document_event (company_id, occurred_at)`; `inventory_movement (company_id, effective_date, posting_seq)`, `(company_id, warehouse_id, effective_date)`; `cost_layer (company_id, item_id, warehouse_id)`; `stock_on_hand (company_id, warehouse_id)`; `stock_valuation (company_id, as_of, warehouse_id)`; `lot (company_id, expires_on)`; `price_list_line (item_id)`; `audit_log (tenant_id, occurred_at)`, `(tenant_id, table_name, occurred_at)`, `(tenant_id, actor_id, occurred_at)`. **No later slice owns any table the gate reaches**, so the later-slice exemption list is empty. **One closed residual list** is judged by its reason rather than by seekability — low-selectivity enumerations, the class SAH-070's own table names as one an index does not help ("`ItmSite` ~1 distinct value", "`ItmLevel` very low selectivity"), each an optional narrowing of rows a required filter or a company-leading key already bounds: `document.status`, `document_event.event_kind`, `document_event.to_status`, `audit_log.action`, `account_balance.account_type` (`account.type`), `stock_on_hand.warehouse_kind` (`warehouse.kind`), `promotion.kind` — and one not-equal, `stock_on_hand.quantity` (`quantity <> 0`, which no btree seeks on). A new entry on either list is an amendment here. **Phase 7 remediation (2026-11-06, owner direction "complete the phase"):** 0077 — applied to no deployed database — was amended in place, as 0044–0050 were, to hold also the seven indexes 7C's filters needed (round 15, "A17 as executed"), so it carries **twenty-one** indexes and still nothing else.

**Branch isolation is RLS's.** `app.shift`, `app.till_event` and `app.needs_attention` each carry Form A's restrictive `branch_isolation` (0068, 0070), so a principal restricted to one branch reads only that branch's rows through these datasets with no predicate of ours.
