The narrower R7 point 6D's functions make — that `branch_isolation` admits any role's branch — is recorded in A16 item 5 as a raise against 7A's run path, not patched here.

**A2 — §4.16.2, `till_event` is registered and read by no core definition.** *"**A registered `DatasetId` need not be read by a core definition.** `till_event` is registered because §4.16.2 assigns it to 7C and because the report **designer** (7A's clone-and-edit, the Phase 7 DoD's first sentence) enumerates `DATASET_IDS`: a tenant who wants a drawer-open audit builds it with no release. The Z-report's till-event counts reach the page as the three `shift` laterals of A1 rather than through a second definition, and **no new `ReportCode` is added** — §4.16.1 is closed for v1."* 7C's dataset test still exercises the member directly (columns, filters, ordering, two-tenant isolation), so a registered-but-unread member is proven, not merely declared.

**A3 — §4.11.1 / 7B A5, the tie-out vocabulary this catalogue needs.** 7B A5 fixed a closed measure map over four fixed columns of one query (`debit`, `credit`, `net`, `credit_net`) and a five-member `projection` vocabulary. 7C extends both additively, in the tree's terms:

- **`The ledger_sum measure map gains two keys (7C)`: `net_sales_base` → `credit_net` and `tax_base` → `credit_net`.** Both are signed — a refund or a credit note moves the other way — so neither maps to `credit` (7B A5: "A signed field is never mapped to `credit`"). **No fifth column and no new arm**: `net_sales_base` is restricted to income accounts by the existing `LedgerWindow.accountTypes: ["income"]` (and to `POS_TICKET` by the existing `documentTypeCodes`), and `tax_base` by `tieOut.account: "2300"`. `base_total → debit` (7B) is reused unchanged by `accounting.party_statement`.
- **`tieOut.projection` gains three members (7C): `shift`, `allocation` and `bank_statement_line`.** ⚠️ `pdc` is **not** added: OD-09 = not built (A16 item 1). **These three are stored tables rather than async projections, and the branch is still the right one:** what `projection` means to the harness is *"the report's rows, grouped on the source's own key, equal the source's stored figures read by the test's own SQL"*. A settlement allocation posts nothing (§4.8.1), so `ledger_sum` would compare an allocation register against zero and pass for the wrong reason, and `none` is reserved for a report with no monetary total. **No new `tieOut.kind`** — that would change `report-definition.schema.json` and 7A's generated type. **Each branch compares per key AND as a set**: every report row's own key (`shift_id`, `allocation_id`, `line_id`) must be a stored row whose figures equal the report's to the cent, and every stored row the run's own parameters select must be in the report — the stored side reads the run's parameters by the names the 7C definitions declare, exactly as 7B's `stock_valuation` branch reads `itemId`/`asOf` and its `item_profitability` branch `fiscalPeriodId`: `shift` — `shiftId`, `branchId`, `cashierPrincipalId`, `fromDate`/`toDate` over the shift's opening date in the company's timezone; `allocation` — `partyId`, `settlementTypeCode`, `fromDate`/`toDate` over the **settled** document's `effective_date`; `bank_statement_line` — `isMatched` (absent = `"false"`, the unreconciled meaning), `bankAccountId`, `fromDate`/`toDate` over `value_date`. The compared figures are `opening_float`, `counted_cash`, `expected_cash`, `over_short` (shift); `base_amount` (allocation); `amount` and `matched_amount` over live matches only (bank line).
- **`LedgerWindow` gains three optional members (7C): `partyId?`, `branchId?`, `shiftId?`.** Each narrows the ledger side through the `document` join the query already has — `d.party_id`, `d.branch_id`, `d.shift_id` — and each is optional, so 7B's windows are unchanged.

**A4 — §4.17.1, `tests/invariants/support/reports-7c.ts`.** The register row is written in §4.17.1 itself (owner **7C**). `CATALOGUE_7C` holds **ten** codes in §4.16.1 order — the eleven of the 7C card less `accounting.pdc_register` (A16 item 1). `readEnvelope7C` refuses a missing file naming its path, and a file whose `definition.code` disagrees with its name, exactly as 7B's `readEnvelope`. `arApReportFixture(db, name)` seeds its own tenant and builds on 4B's `arApFixture(db, s)`; `posReportFixture(api, name)` builds on 6C's `staffFixture(api, name)` and writes every POS row through 6A's `applyBatch`.

**A5 — §4.16.1, `accounting.branch_profit_and_loss`.** *"**`accounting.branch_profit_and_loss` is exactly `statementDefinition("profit_and_loss", { code, nameEn, nameAr, permission: "accounting.report.read" }, { perBranch: true })`**"* — 7A's `build({ perBranch: true })` fragment composed onto the code's identity, by the rule 7B A6 imposes on the two company-level statements. Its `dataset.source` is `account_balance`, which names the row **shape**; `rowsForDefinition` sees a `STATEMENT_CODES` key and dispatches to `statementRows`, whose `perBranch` variant reads the `ledger_entry` dataset (the only place a branch tag exists on a posted amount) and collapses it to that shape. On the statement branch `dataset.filters` are not consulted, and `assertDefinitionFields` unions `STATEMENT_EXTRA_FIELDS` (`section`, `branch_code`, `branch_id`) for the three `STATEMENT_CODES` keys. **Every test run supplies a real `branchId`** (`s.hq`) and the `LedgerWindow` carries the same `branchId`, so both sides measure one branch; without it `statementRows` takes the `account_balance` fallback, which carries no `branch_id`, and `assertFieldCoverage` fails naming it. 7C writes no layout of its own and edits nothing of 7A's.

**A6 — §4.16.1, `accounting.party_statement`.** *"`accounting.party_statement` declares **`partyId` (party, required)**, `fromDate` and `toDate` (date, required) and `documentTypeCode` (text, optional)."* 7A's `document` dataset carries `party_id`, `party_code` and `party_name_en` and no `party_kind` (7B A3). Its `tieOut` is `ledger_sum` with no `account`, over `LedgerWindow { partyId, fromDate, toDate }` and `base_total → debit`.

**A7 — §4.16.1, `accounting.tax_return_view`.** *"`accounting.tax_return_view` reads the **`tax_transaction`** dataset and declares"* `fiscalPeriodId` (period, required), `taxCodeKind` (enum, required, `options: ["output", "input"]`) and `regimeCode` (text, optional). Its `tieOut` is `ledger_sum` with `account: "2300"` and the `tax_base → credit_net` key of A3, executed with `taxCodeKind: "output"`; the input side renders against `1350` and is proven by a row witness in the same test. **It names no authority form, no box number, no rate and no deadline** (hazard 2): it renders `tax_code`, `tax_code_kind`, `tax_rate`, `regime_code`, `base_base` and `tax_base` as 5A's engine stored them.

**A8 — §4.16.1, `accounting.unreconciled_items` is a filter, not a query.** It is the `bank_statement_line` dataset filtered `is_matched eq` a required `isMatched` enum (`options: ["false", "true"]`), plus `bankAccountId` (account, optional) and `fromDate`/`toDate` (date, optional) over `value_date`. Its `tieOut` is `projection: "bank_statement_line"` (A3). It stays gated `accounting.bank.reconcile`.

**A9 — §4.6.1 and §3.5.3, `app.export_job`'s DDL.** The register row is amended in place to carry `check (format in ('csv','json','both'))`, the recorded-gate columns `readable_modules text[]` and `lot_attachments boolean`, `include_attachments`, the three counts, `manifest jsonb` and `started_at`. **`format` has three values** because spec:2186 requires "CSV + JSON + a documented schema"; `'both'` is the default. **`readable_modules` and `lot_attachments` are columns** because the attachment read gate (`MODULE_READ_CODE`) lives in `apps/api` (A16 item 6), `apps/worker` and `packages/db` may not import an app (§3.1), and the job runs as the system principal, which holds every code — so the route records the requester's readable modules at request time and the job filters by them (ADR 0070). **Linter sets:** `export_job` joins none of `NO_ID_TABLES`, `NO_CREATED_AT_TABLES`, `AUDIT_EXEMPT` or `IMMUTABLE`, and receives **no** `branch_isolation` policy: it has no `branch_id`, and an export is company-wide by construction.

**A10 — §4.2.6, the job payload.** `JobPayload` gains `"admin.export.run": { exportJobId: string }` (written into the §4.2.6 block). `JOBS` already carries the name with `owner: "7C"`.

**A11 ⚠️ — §3.6.3, a permission-seed task closes its own `permission-catalogue` gap. A PROPOSAL awaiting the architect.** *"**The task that adds a catalogue code ships a `PERMISSION[…]` reference in the same commit.** The reference need not be a finished handler: a route module registered in `buildRoutes` with its `permissions: [PERMISSION["<code>"]]` array and one `createRoute` gated by `requirePermission` satisfies `permission-catalogue` (§3.6.3) and `assertRouteGates` (R7) while the handler body is a stub the same slice replaces two tasks later."* 7C's Task 6 does exactly this, so `bun run lint:rules` is green at every 7C commit. 7A's Task 3 → Task 12 gap is recorded, not retro-fixed. **This changes a sequencing rule a merged slice relied on**, so it is adopted under the owner's standing direction to choose best-practice defaults (2026-10-02, 2026-10-22) and awaits ratification like every implemented-ahead proposal; if it is refused, 7C's Task 6 leaves `lint:rules` red until Task 9 and says so in its commit body.

Sub-paths: `POST …/exports`, `GET …/exports`, `GET …/exports/{exportJobId}`, `GET …/exports/{exportJobId}/content`. **One `PROBES` key** (`"/v1/companies/:companyId/exports"`); the sub-paths inherit it. The download route does not join `REPLAY_BY_RERUN`. **The `POST` is an export request, so it joins 7A's R7 widening** (A16 item 7): `admin.data.export` is a read-side code (`mutating: false` — an export changes no business record), R7 refuses a non-mutating code on an unsafe method, and `assertRouteGates` admits one only through `markExportRequestGate` on a path `EXPORT_REQUEST_ROUTES` lists for a code `EXPORT_REQUEST_CODES` lists. Task 9 adds the exports path to the first and `admin.data.export` to the second, in the PR that mounts the route, and ADR 0070 records it as the widening it is.

**A15 — §4.16.3, `ReportCodeSchema` after 7C.** *"**7C widens it by its seven new codes** — `accounting.party_statement`, `accounting.allocation_register`, `accounting.unreconciled_items`, `accounting.branch_profit_and_loss`, `accounting.tax_return_view`, `pos.sales_by_branch`, `pos.needs_attention` — **appended after whatever members already exist**."* (The plan's text read "7C widens it by its eight new codes", the eighth being ⚠️ `accounting.pdc_register`; OD-09 drops it.) The three codes 7C re-expresses (`accounting.ageing`, `pos.z_report`, `pos.sales_by_cashier`) are already members. **No slice asserts a total member count** (7B A4); for the record the enum holds twenty-five after 7B and thirty-two after 7C.

**A16 — the tree as Phase 6, 7A and 7B merged it.** Every place 7C's plan text disagreed with the repository; the repository's spelling is the contract and 7C's tasks consume it:

1. **OD-09 = not built.** Migration `0051` is reserved and unused, so 7A shipped **twenty-five** `DatasetId` members (no `pdc`) and 7C closes the registry at **twenty-eight**, not twenty-nine; `accounting.pdc_register`, the `pdc` projection branch and 7C's Task 11 are dropped whole. `CATALOGUE_7C` has ten codes, the harness has three new projection branches, and 7C's tie-out roll-up is **nine and one**: five `ledger_sum` (`accounting.party_statement`, `pos.sales_by_cashier`, `pos.sales_by_branch`, `accounting.branch_profit_and_loss`, `accounting.tax_return_view`), four `projection` (`accounting.ageing` → `party_ageing`, `accounting.allocation_register` → `allocation`, `accounting.unreconciled_items` → `bank_statement_line`, `pos.z_report` → `shift`) and the one `none`, `pos.needs_attention`, with its row witness.
2. **7B's measure map is `debit`/`credit`/`net`/`credit_net`** over one query, not the plan's `base_debit`/`base_credit`/`base_balance` columns plus a fourth `net_sales_base` column; A3 above is written in those terms, and the income restriction is the existing `LedgerWindow.accountTypes`.
3. **6D buckets a shift's date in the company's timezone**, not UTC: `zReport`'s history and `salesByCashier`'s shortfall both read `date(s.opened_at at time zone company.timezone)` / `closed_at`. The two date companions (`shift.opened_on`, `needs_attention.created_on`) therefore use the company's timezone, so the definition-driven `pos.z_report` history selects the same shifts as 6D's function for the same `fromDate`/`toDate`; every *timestamp* field stays RFC 3339 UTC (7B A3). The plan's `(… at time zone 'UTC')::date` would disagree with 6D for a shift opened in the hours either side of UTC midnight.
4. **`app.till_event` carries `reason`** (0070) — the supervisor's stated reason for a void — which the plan's A1 omitted; it is a column of the dataset. `app.pos_terminal.code` is 6A's nullable column (0061) and `app.principal.display_name` the name every dataset uses.
5. **Report runs execute as the tenant's system principal** (7A's `reporting.render`, ADR 0066/0067), so neither RLS's `branch_isolation` nor an `app.actor_has` predicate inside a dataset bounds a *run* to the requester's branches; the run path's request-time gate does. This is 7A's design, applies to every dataset, and is recorded here as a raise for whoever next changes the run path, not patched in 7C's three datasets. The test-tier harness runs definitions as the reader, where `branch_isolation` does hold.
6. **There is no exported `readableModules()` in `apps/api`.** `apps/api/src/middleware/require-attachment-read.ts` exports `MODULE_READ_CODE` and applies it per row; the list route filters in its handler. Task 9 computes the requester's readable modules from `MODULE_READ_CODE` (one place, in the export route's own `authorise.ts`) rather than importing a function that does not exist.

Task 6's skeleton route (A11) must already be admitted by `assertRouteGates`, so Task 6 either mounts a safe-method stub or lands the two list entries with the skeleton.
8. **The tax fixture uses 5A's real pack loader.** `tests/invariants/support/tax.ts` exports `seedTaxPack(db, s)` (the shipped `tax/` pack through `taxLoader`), and the AR/AP fixture uses it rather than the plan's hand-inserted `seedTaxCode`, so `accounting.tax_return_view` renders figures the shipped synthetic regime produced. `postTaxedDocument` credits only against a posted invoice line carrying the **same** tax code, so the fixture's credit note is taxed.
9. **4B's `importStatement` and `match` are as merged**: `importStatement(tx, ctx, { companyId, bankAccountId, csv, mapping: { statement: { statementDate, openingBalance, closingBalance }, columns: { valueDate, description, reference, amount }, dateFormat, hasHeader } })` and `match(tx, ctx, { companyId, statementLineId, reconcilable: { kind, documentId }, amount })`.
10. **6D's pins test carried a 7C-only guard**: `packages/db/test/phase-6d-pins.test.ts` asserted `datasets.ts` quotes neither `"shift"` nor `"till_event"` "until 7C adds the members". 7C's Task 1 retires that clause in the same commit that adds the members (§3.7.3: the slice that changes a shared registry updates its pin), and re-points the case at what remains true — 6D added no dataset file.
11. **The phase gate.** The plan's gate waits on "7B merged and Phase 6's definition of done green in CI". On this branch 7B is complete (head `35cfab0`) and Phase 6 is implemented but has not exited (its open items are owner-supplied, `AGENTS.md`); 7C proceeds under the same owner direction that started Phases 4–7 ahead of their predecessors' exits.
12. **7A's boolean filter bound "true" as false.** `datasetWhere` cast a boolean value as `${value}::boolean`; postgres.js serialises a parameter the server types as boolean with `x === true ? 't' : 'f'`, so the string `"true"` arrived as `false` and every `eq "true"` filter (`is_open`, `is_matched`, `credit_hold`) silently returned the false set — `is_matched eq "false"`, the only boolean filter 7A's and 7B's tests used, passed by accident. 7C's Task 1 binds a boolean as `::text::boolean` (and an `in` list as `::text[]::boolean[]`) in `packages/db/src/reports/query.ts`, with the regression in `packages/db/test/reports/7c-datasets.test.ts`. The fix is 7A's file; it changes no signature and no row any correct run returned.
13. **7B's harness had no `party_ageing` branch.** 7B A5 names `party_ageing` among the five `projection` members, but no 7B code ties to it, so `assertTieOut`'s switch carried four cases and its `default` arm. 7C's `accounting.ageing` is the first reader, so Task 2 adds the branch beside its three: the report's rows keyed `(party_id, currency, bucket)` against the stored `app.party_ageing` snapshot for the run's required `asOf` (narrowed by `partyKind` and `currency` when given), comparing `amount` and `base_amount`. `arApReportFixture` rebuilds that snapshot with 4B's `rebuildPartyAgeing` for `2026-01-31`, as the nightly job would; the parity against the live `agedBalance` stays Task 3's.
14. **(7C Task 3) A column `width` of 0 is not a format-version-1 definition.** `report-definition.schema.json` bounds `width` to `8 … 400`, so the plan's `"width": 0` "minimum" columns (`document_id`, `posting_seq`, `line_id`, `shift_id`, `cashier_principal_id`, `opened_at`, `created_at`) are declared at **`width: 8`**, the schema's own minimum — the same intent, a valid file. Two id columns the plan did not declare are added the same way because a sort key must be a declared column: `allocation_id` (the allocation register's tie-break) and the ageing's third sort key `bucket` (`party_code`, `currency` alone leave the five bucket rows of one party unordered; the order is the bucket's text, since the dataset carries no bucket ordinal).

The tax view's type column is labelled `نوع المستند` so its two "Type"/"Kind" columns no longer share one Arabic label.
17. **(7C Task 4) 4B and 6D shipped no definition file.** Their reports are JSON routes, so `accounting.ageing`, `pos.z_report` and `pos.sales_by_cashier` are seeded at `definitionVersion` 2 with **no** version-1 row beside them; the plan's "each re-expressed code now has BOTH rows" is not the tree, and the loader case asserts the three version-2 core rows alone.
18. **(7C Task 4) The definition-driven Z-report carries the shift's totals and counts, not 6D's tender and cash-control lines.** A1 gives the `shift` dataset one row per shift and no per-tender or per-document-type figure, so those two sections — including OD-10's paid-outs, safe drops and bankings (ADR 0064) — stay `zReport`'s. The parity case compares every shift of the day field by field (float, count, expected, over/short and its document, the two ticket counts, the three till-event counts, terminal, cashier, closer) and posts a `TILL_PAID_OUT` on the open shift: 6D lists it in `cashControl`, and it moves neither a count nor `net_sales_base`, which is `POS_TICKET` income only. The `pos.sales_by_cashier` parity is per `(cashier, branch)` — 6D's grouping — over `netSalesBase`, `ticketCount`, `returnCount` and `overShortBase`; the last agrees because one cashier opens and closes each shift (6D attributes the over/short to the closer, the dataset to the opener — the raise the plan's Self-Review names). `discountBase` and `cashRoundingBase` have no dataset field (A1) and are not compared.

Its `PROBES` key asks for the victim company's list and expects **403**, not the plan's unrouted sub-path and 404: the company gate answers before any row is read, exactly as the `report-runs` probe does, and the answer does not change when Task 9 adds the sub-paths.
22. **(7C Task 7) The registry classifies every table.** Every `app` base table is either an `EXPORT_TABLES` row or pinned `["*"]` in `NEVER_EXPORTED` (secrets: `terminal_enrolment`, `idempotency_key`; plumbing: `terminal_request_guard`, `catalogue_tombstone`, `cost_booking`, `export_job`, the global `permission`), and `tables.test.ts` fails on a table that is neither. Gates beyond the plan's six tables: `inventory.cost.read` on `inventory_movement` (its `value` is cost), `cost_consumption`, `stock_valuation`, `landed_cost_allocation`, `item_profitability`; `accounting.tax.manage` on `tax_regime`, `tax_return`; `accounting.tax.file` on `einvoice_transmission`; `hr.employee.read` on `employee`, `attendance_event`, `pos_cashier`; `pos.report.read` on `till_banking_link`; `pos.needs_attention.resolve` on `needs_attention`; `admin.audit_log.read` on `document_event` (7B's `accounting.document_event_log` gate); `accounting.report.export` on `report_run`. `document_line.cost` is omitted (the figure `inventory_movement.value` carries behind its gate). ADR 0069 records all of it as a proposal.
23. **(7C Task 8) The archive and the job as merged.** `ExportManifestAttachment` carries **no `objectKey`** — the manifest is in the archive and on the status resource, and a store key never reaches the wire (SAH-038, `NEVER_EXPORTED.attachment`); `path` locates the bytes. `attachmentsOmitted[].reason` gains a third value, **`digest_mismatch`**, for stored bytes that no longer hash to the row's recorded SHA-256 (the manifest states the recorded digest, so such bytes are named, not shipped). A lot attachment is recognised by `lot_id is not null`, not `document_id is null`. The handler stamps `generatedAt` with the claim's own `started_at` rather than a second clock read, so a job's archive is reproducible from its row; on failure it fails the **row** and returns without re-throwing, as `reporting.render` does (a pg-boss retry would find the row no longer queued). `tarGz` fixes gzip header byte 9 (OS) to 255, so the digest does not depend on the platform zlib was built for; the deflate stream itself is zlib's, so the digest is reproducible by the same build (ADR 0069 decision 1, which now states exactly what is and is not deterministic — two different jobs always differ in `manifest.json`, and `tables/audit_log.*` by the earlier exports' own audited status writes). `ExportSchemaDocument` gains `tableJson: "newline-delimited, one object per row"`. Task 7's registry ordered five numeric keys by their **text** output alias (`audit_log.seq`, `document.posting_seq`, `inventory_movement.posting_seq`, `cost_layer.sequence`, `document_number_void.number` — `order by seq` binds to `seq::text as seq`, so 201 sorted before 21); each is now qualified with its table, and `run.test.ts` pins the audit trail's numeric order. The `JOB_PROBES` entry hands the attacker's job the victim's queued id (the `reporting.render` probe's shape) and counts queued rows plus `export_job` update audits.
24. **(7C Task 9) The routes as merged.** (a) **The export-request marker carries one code per route.** 7A's `markExportRequestGate(handler)` stamped every `EXPORT_REQUEST_CODES` member on every marked gate, so adding `admin.data.export` there would have let 7A's report-run `POST` claim it too. `EXPORT_REQUEST_ROUTES` entries are now `{ method, path, code }`, `markExportRequestGate(handler, code)` stamps only `code`, `EXPORT_REQUEST_CODES` is derived from the routes, and `assertRouteGates` refuses any other export code on a listed route (`require-permission.test.ts`). (b) **An export is its requester's**: the list, the status resource and the download answer only `requested_by = caller` — another principal's job is `404 ERR_NOT_FOUND` — because the archive carries its requester's table gates and a colleague lacking one must not download it (test 32's side channel; ADR 0070 decision 5). `listExportJobs` gains an optional `requestedBy`. (c) The contracts module uses plain `zod` like its neighbours; `ExportJobSchema` carries **no `objectKey`** (SAH-038, as the Task 6 list did) and `ExportJobQuery` is a `strict` object of `cursor`, `limit` (1–200, default 50, Task 6's bounds) and `filter[status][eq]` — not `ListQuery.extend`, whose `sort`/`fields` nothing implements. `CreateExportBody` is `strict`, so no body field can name a principal or opt out of the audit. (d) The download recomputes the stored bytes' SHA-256 against the row's and answers `ERR_INTERNAL` on a mismatch, as 7A's run download does; it sends `X-Content-Sha256` and `cache-control: private, no-store`. (e) The status-snapshot helper is `exportGateSnapshot(c, companyId)` in `apps/api/src/export/authorise.ts`, beside `exportRequestGate`; with no `readableModules()` in the tree (item 6) it reads `MODULE_READ_CODE` and `LOT_READ_CODE` at company scope with a null branch. (f) The route-test harness's stub job client accepts `admin.export.run`. ADR 0070 is **Proposed**, not the plan's "Accepted": it decides who may take data out of the system (spec:95).
25. **(7C Task 10) Tests 13, 32 and 36 over the export, as merged.** `tests/invariants/export-audit.test.ts` drives the worker's own `exportRun` handler (relative import, under `systemContext`) so test 13 sees the claim and the completion audited under the system principal, not only the request under the requester; `verifyChain` returns `ChainResult { rows, brokenLinks, badHashes }`, so the chain case asserts zero broken links and bad hashes rather than the plan's `[]`; and a body field that would opt out (`audit: false`) is a 400, the `strict` body's proof that no flag suppresses the row. In `apps/api/test/routes/admin/exports-gates.test.ts` the staff fixture's `seed.human` already holds 6A's tax codes, so the plan's expected exclusions `tax_code`/`tax_transaction` were wrong for this fixture: the case asserts `audit_log`, `document_event`, `employee` and `pos_cashier` excluded, every excluded gate NOT held and every included gated table's gate held (through `app.principal_has` in the tenant), and the registry partitioned exactly into included and excluded. Two cases beyond the plan: a principal holding every registry gate gets an archive with nothing excluded in which no live value of a pinned secret column (`pin_hash`, `device_public_key`, `auth_subject`, the e-invoice credentials, the two `object_key`s) appears in any file's bytes; and a table gate held only at one branch does not admit its table (the gate is resolved with a null branch).
26. **(Phase 7 review, 2026-11-06; ADR 0065 amendment, proposed) A definition's gate is bounded by its dataset and by its writer.** 7A's `validateReportDefinition` checked `permission` and `dataset.source` only for membership of their closed sets, and a run executes as the system principal, so a clone could re-gate any dataset on any code — the review's case cloned `accounting.audit_log` onto a weaker code with the `before`/`after` images. Three rules: (a) `DATASET_READ_CODES` (`packages/db/src/reports/datasets.ts`) names the read codes each `DatasetId` admits — the codes the 32 shipped definitions use, `accounting.ledger.read` beside `accounting.report.read` on the ledger reads, the module read code otherwise; `document` and `item_profitability` admit two because the shipped catalogue does — and `assertDatasetGate`, inside `assertDefinitionFields`, refuses any other at `/permission`, at save and at seed; (b) a create, clone or edit keeps the `dataset.source` of the code's existing versions in the company (`/dataset/source`), and the writer must hold, by `app.actor_has(code, company, null)`, the new `permission` and every `permission` the code's versions carry (`ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN` otherwise) — `admin.company.manage` is necessary, no longer sufficient; (c) no dataset serves a column `NEVER_EXPORTED` pins, so `audit_log` loses `before`/`after` (no shipped definition printed them). Residual: within one gate a clone may still widen a filter (`inventory.count_register`'s caller-supplied `countTypes` already admits any document type under `inventory.stock.read`).
27. **(Phase 7 review, 2026-11-06; ADR 0067 and 0069 amendments, proposed) The run and export lifecycles, as reviewed.** (a) `listReportRuns` keeps a run only when the acting principal holds its definition's own `permission` (`app.actor_has(…, company, null)`), the gate the single-run and content routes apply; (b) a claim is a lease: `app.report_run` gains `started_at` and `attempts` and `app.export_job` gains `attempts` (0075 and 0078 amended in place — never applied outside a test database), a claim older than `REPORT_RUN_LEASE_SECONDS` (600) or `EXPORT_JOB_LEASE_SECONDS` (3,600) is reclaimed, `attempts` fences a superseded worker's writes, the claim past `*_MAX_CLAIMS` (3) fails the row, and both jobs are enqueued with stated options (`REPORT_RUN_JOB_OPTIONS`, `EXPORT_JOB_JOB_OPTIONS`: `expireInSeconds` = the lease, `retryLimit` = claims + 2; `EnqueueOptions` gains `expireInSeconds`); (c) a run never renders short: `rowsForDefinition` reads one row past its cap on the dataset branch too and refuses `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED`; (d) `runExport(read, store, input)` takes an `ExportReadTransaction` runner, reads every row in one short transaction and fetches the attachment bytes after it commits; (e) `apps/worker/src/jobs/failure.ts` owns `failureDetail` and `FAILURE_DETAIL_MAX` (2,000) for both handlers, and `failExportJob` caps as `failReportRun` does.
28. **(Phase 7 second review, 2026-11-06; ADR 0065, 0067 and 0069 amendments, proposed) The gates and the lease, as re-reviewed.** (a) **A live claim schedules its follow-up**: a delivery that finds a live claim no longer throws (each throw spent a pg-boss retry, and the budget ended before the export's 3,600 s lease); it enqueues ONE follow-up of the same payload with `startAfterSeconds` = the claim's remaining lease (`leaseState`, database clock) + `LEASE_FOLLOW_UP_MARGIN_SECONDS` (30) and `singletonKey` `<id>:lease:<attempts>` (`leaseFollowUpOptions`; `reportRunFollowUpOptions`/`exportJobFollowUpOptions`, `reportRunLeaseState`/`exportJobLeaseState`; worker `deferPastLease` in `apps/worker/src/jobs/lease.ts`), and a refused duplicate (`JobNotInsertedError`, now exported by `@dulja/db`) is "already scheduled". (b) **Object keys carry the claim**: `reportObjectKeyFor(tenantId, runId, extension, attempt)` → `<tenant>/reports/<run>/<attempt>.<ext>` and `exportObjectKeyFor(tenantId, exportJobId, attempt)` → `<tenant>/exports/<job>/<attempt>.tar.gz`; `completeReportRun`/`completeExportJob` return `Promise<boolean>` (the fenced write landed) and a superseded worker deletes its object; the downloads read the stored key. (c) **The export's `report_run` table is gated on `admin.audit_log.read`** (it was `accounting.report.export`, item 22), and `NEVER_EXPORTED.report_run` adds `started_at` and `attempts` (plumbing). (d) **A gate may bound rows**: `DATASET_ROW_BOUNDS` / `datasetRowBound(source, permission)` in `packages/db/src/reports/datasets.ts`, applied by `rowsForDefinition` through the new optional `DatasetParams.rowBound`; `document` under `inventory.stock.read` reads only `document_type.module = 'inventory'`. (e) **A column may require a code**: `DatasetColumn.requires?: string`; `assertDatasetGate` (now taking the definition's columns, groups, totals, sort and filters) refuses a definition naming such a column under another code; `document_line.cost`, `cost_layer`/`cost_consumption` `unit_cost`/`value` and `stock_valuation.value` require `inventory.cost.read`; `inventory_movement.value`, `item_profitability.cogs_base`/`margin_base` and the count register's `document.base_total` stay readable under `inventory.stock.read` by recorded design (a known limit). (f) **`listReportRuns` resolves the caller's codes once** (distinct definition permissions × `app.actor_has`, compared as `= any($held::text[])`). (g) **One lease helper**: `packages/db/src/jobs/lease.ts` exports `Lease`, `LeaseJobOptions`, `LeaseState`, `claimLeased`, `leaseFence`, `leaseJobOptions`, `leaseState`, `leaseFollowUpOptions`, `leaseFollowUpKey` and `FAILURE_DETAIL_MAX` (2,000), superseding item 27(e)'s owner: the worker's `failure.ts` re-exports the db constant. (h) **The gate is re-checked at run time**: `rowsForDefinition` runs `assertDatasetGate` before reading, and `POST …/reports/{code}/runs` runs it after the definition's read code (400, no run, no job). `DATASET_READ_CODES`, `DATASET_ROW_BOUNDS`, `assertDatasetGate` and `datasetRowBound` are exported from `@dulja/db`.

**A17 — 7B A17 / SAH-070, the index gate over 7C's filters.** `packages/db/test/reports/7b-report-indexes.test.ts` reads every `CATALOGUE_7C` definition beside 7B's (through `readEnvelope7C`), so every 7C filter pair joins `COLUMN_OF` and is judged by the same seekability rule. Three closed lists say why a pair is not: **`RESIDUAL`** (low-selectivity enumerations, 7B's list) gains `party_ageing.party_kind`, `party_ageing.currency`, `needs_attention.error_code` and `tax_transaction.tax_code_kind`; **`COMPUTED`** holds the two-valued fields that are expressions, not columns — `bank_statement_line.is_matched` and `needs_attention.is_open`; and **`UNSERVED`** records a filter no index seeks on — `document.party_id` (`accounting.party_statement`, wants `document (company_id, party_id, effective_date)`), `allocation.party_id` (wants `allocation (company_id, party_id)`), `shift.opened_on` (the POS reports' date range is `(opened_at at time zone company.timezone)::date`, which no btree seeks — it wants a sargable rewrite to `opened_at` bounds and `shift (company_id, opened_at)`; 6D's `zReport` filters the same expression), `shift.cashier_principal_id` (wants `shift (company_id, opened_principal_id, opened_at)`), `needs_attention.branch_id` (0060's only branch index is partial), `needs_attention.created_on` (a timezone date expression) and `tax_transaction.fiscal_period_id` (wants `tax_transaction (company_id, fiscal_period_id)`). The 7C pairs the existing indexes do serve are judged like 7B's: `party_ageing.as_of`, the document date and type joins, `bank_statement.bank_account_id`, `bank_statement_line.value_date`, `shift.id`, `shift.branch_id`, the statement's `document.branch_id` and `tax_regime.code`. **`UNSERVED` is a gap recorded, not a pass**: 7C's range 0078–0079 is allocated to `export_job` and its permission seed, and 7B A7 gives an index on a spent range's table no lawful home, so each index waits on a migration number the owner allocates; the gate fails if an `UNSERVED` pair becomes seekable, so the PR that adds the index must remove the entry.

**A17 as executed (Phase 7 remediation, 2026-11-06).** Under the owner's direction of 2026-11-06 ("make sure phase 7 is implemented entirely … choose the best suggestion"), the seven `UNSERVED` indexes were given 7B's migration rather than a new number: 0077 has been applied to no deployed database, and amending an unapplied migration in place is the 0044–0050 precedent. 0077 gains `document (company_id, party_id, effective_date)`, `allocation (company_id, party_id)`, `shift (company_id, opened_at)`, `shift (company_id, opened_principal_id, opened_at)`, `needs_attention (company_id, branch_id, created_at)` (non-partial, unlike 0060's), `needs_attention (company_id, created_at)` and `tax_transaction (company_id, fiscal_period_id)`, with their Drizzle mirrors and down-migration lines — twenty-one indexes in all, still indexes only. **The two timezone date companions are now sargable:** `DatasetColumn.localDateOf` (`packages/db/src/reports/query.ts`) declares `shift.opened_on` and `needs_attention.created_on` as an instant's date in the company's timezone, and `eq`/`ne`/`lt`/`lte`/`gt`/`gte` on them compile to bounds on `opened_at` / `created_at` — a local day `d` runs from its first instant in the zone to the first instant of `d + 1` (`least(d::timestamp at time zone tz, ((d::timestamp − 1 hour) at time zone tz) + 1 hour)`, exact where a DST change repeats local midnight), the zone read by an uncorrelated subquery over the run's company so the bound is an InitPlan constant (amended 2026-11-14: under RLS PostgreSQL 18.7 will not seek a qual holding a SubPlan, so `localTimezoneFor` reads the zone once on the run's transaction and the bound carries it as a bound value); `in` and `like` keep the expression. The fragments are literal in the dataset file; a definition still contributes only a field name and a bound value. `packages/db/test/reports/7c-datasets.test.ts` proves the rows identical to the expression's for every operator one microsecond either side of local midnight in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and on America/Havana's skipped and repeated midnights. **`UNSERVED` is gone**: `packages/db/test/reports/7b-report-indexes.test.ts` keeps only `RESIDUAL` and `COMPUTED`, so a new selective filter with no seekable index fails the seekability case, and a new case requires every DATE field over a `timestamptz` column to declare `localDateOf` and the planner to put the instant in an `Index Cond`.

**A sort key need not be a displayed column (Phase 7 remediation, 2026-11-06; ADR 0065 amendment, proposed).** Round 15 A16 item 16 records 7A's rule "a sort key must be a declared column". It is relaxed for `sort` only: `validateReportDefinition` still requires every `groups` and `totals` field to be a column, and `assertDefinitionFields` refuses a sort key the dataset (or, for the three statement codes, `STATEMENT_EXTRA_FIELDS`) lacks, at save and at seed. Two definitions use it: `accounting.ageing` sorts `party_code, currency, bucket_rank` — `party_ageing.bucket_rank` is `0 … 4` in 4B's vocabulary order, so `current` no longer prints between `61_90` and `over_90` — and the three statements sort on `section_rank`.

**Statement presentation (Phase 7 remediation, 2026-11-06).** The statements printed their sections as raw tokens in alphabetical order (asset, equity, liability; expense before revenue) and their header as the fiscal period's uuid. Superseding round 14's consumed-export lines for these names: `STATEMENT_EXTRA_FIELDS = ["section", "section_rank", "section_label", "branch_code", "branch_id"]`; `STATEMENT_SECTION_RANK` (asset 0, liability 1, equity 2; revenue 0, expense 1, net_result 2) and `statementSectionFields(kind, accountType, lang) → { section, section_rank, section_label } | null` are new in `packages/domain/src/reports/statement.ts`; `StatementParams` and `rowsForDefinition`'s params gain an optional `lang: ReportLang` (default `en`), in which `statementRows` writes `section_label` from `STATEMENT_SECTION_LABELS`. The layout's section column, and its section group, are `section_label`; its sort is `section_rank, account_code`, led by `branch_code` per BRANCH. The three statement seed files are regenerated from `statementDefinition`, so the deep-equality pins (7B A6, 7C A5) still hold, and the `ledger_sum` tie-outs are unchanged. **The header prints the period's code:** `reportDisplayParameters(tx, definition, { companyId, parameters })` (`packages/db/src/reports/statement.ts`) returns the run's parameters with every `period`-kind value replaced by that company's period code, `to_char(starts_on, 'YYYY-MM')` (a value that is not one of the company's periods prints as given), and the `reporting.render` handler passes it to `renderReport` — so every definition whose header names `{fiscalPeriodId}` (the three statements, `accounting.trial_balance`, `accounting.period_comparison`, `accounting.tax_return_view`, `inventory.sales_by_item`, `inventory.profit_by_item`) prints `2026-03`, not a uuid. The rows are still read with the raw parameters.

**A1 — §2.9 (8A card), §2.12, the 8A owner gates.** *"The 8A owner gates are OD-28, OD-14, OD-23 and OD-24 — not OD-13."* §2.12 gates OD-13 (the leave register) to **8D** and the 8A card names OD-28 in its place. 8A builds no `leave_type`, `leave_entitlement`, `leave_record`, `public_holiday` and no `hr.leave.*` code.

**A2 — §4.6.1, the payroll account columns ship nullable.** *"`statutory_scheme.payable_account_id` ships NULLABLE, not `not null`."* §4.12.2 and §4.15 give `2411`…`2414` and `5311`…`5314` to **8B**'s seed and hazard 33 forbids 8A an account literal. `statutory_scheme.payable_account_id`, `employer_expense_account_id`, `authority_party_id`, `pay_component.expense_account_id` and `pay_component.payable_account_id` are all nullable at 0083/0084; 8B's seed fills them and 8B's `PAYROLL` policy fails closed with `ERR_POLICY_REQUIRES_MISSING` until it has.

**A8 — §4.2.7, §4.2.12, §4.2.3, §3.11, the HR key ring.** *"`AppDeps` gains `hrKeys: HrKeyRing`"* on 2C's `objectStore` precedent — a route never reads a key out of `process.env`, and `startApi()` mints a deterministic test ring. `ApiConfig` gains `hrFieldEncryptionKey: string` and `hrFieldEncryptionKeyPrevious: string | null`. §3.11's `HR_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `HR_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` are **base64 of exactly 32 bytes**; `readConfig()` refuses any other length with a `ConfigError` naming the variable; both are optional when `APP_ENV=dev` (a deterministic all-zero dev key, `DEV_HR_KEY`) and the current key is required otherwise. **A1 — §2.9 (8B card), §3.4.1, migration 0090.** *"Migration 0090 is not spare."* R3 (spec:2174) — a compensation change effective in the period of a run in `submitted` or `approved` status returns that run to `draft` — is a data-layer rule on 8A's `compensation_line`, which is a trigger, which is a migration: **`0090_create_compensation_change_returns_run.sql`**. Applied to the §2.9 card in this round.

**A3 — §4.12.2, §4.4.1, §4.4.2, §4.3.4, BRANCH per line on PAYROLL.** *"Every `PAYROLL` policy rule declares `dimensions: { "from": ["line.dimensions", "line.employee"] }` and omits `document.branch`."* 2A's `dimensionsFor` gives `document.branch` the last word over the line's bag, so a rule naming it would stamp every employee's line with the run's branch and spec:2101's "the employee's home branch" would be false. `dimensions.required: ["BRANCH", "EMPLOYEE"]` makes the omission safe rather than silent. The two other sections that said otherwise are corrected in place in this round: §4.3.4's `document_line.dimensions` comment now reads "BRANCH is never here except on PAYROLL lines …", and §4.4.1's semantics paragraph now reads "the evaluator adds `document.branch` as `BRANCH` and `line.employee` as `EMPLOYEE` to a line exactly when that rule's `dimensions.from` names them".

**A4 — §4.12.2, §4.14, no reversal of a PAYROLL.** *"`PAYROLL` declares `reversal: { "allowed": false, "producesType": null }`"* and a posted run is corrected by a `supplementary` run (ADR 0076, **Proposed** — money semantics, spec:95). Two independent mechanics forbid the reversal path: `reverseDocument` posts a fresh **draft** mirror, which §4.5.1 admits to `issued` only when `approval.required = false`; and it copies no `payroll_line`, so every mirrored line would match no rule and raise `ERR_DOC_NO_LINES`.

**8D A1 — §3.11, §4.12.5.** **`HR_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION` joins §3.11** — holder api + worker, set by 8D, meaning "the integer `key_version` the current `HR_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` seals under; default `1`". 8A's Self-Review left it open in terms, because `createHrKeyRing` requires a `currentVersion` and nothing in §3.11 supplied it. It is **optional everywhere and defaults to `1`**, so no existing environment changes; `HR_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS_VERSION` is **not** added — `createHrKeyRing` derives it as `currentVersion − 1`. The name joins `containerSecrets(env, entrypoint)`'s optional list for **`api` and `worker`** in the PR that introduces the rotation job (8D Task 7). Applied to §3.11 in this round.

**8D A2 — §4.6.1, the `employee` row.** **`app.employee` gains `contract_ends_on date`** (migration **0098**, 8D, expand-only). spec:2091 requires a "contract and permit expiry list" and neither §4.6.2's minimal DDL nor 8A's 0080 carries a contract end date. It is a plain column beside `hired_on` and `terminated_on`, **not** an `employee_sensitive` field: an employment end date is an operational fact of the same class as a hire date. Applied to §4.6.1 in this round.

**9B C1 — §4.13.3.** **"a dedicated series `LEGACY`" reads "the dedicated cut-over series `OB` and `OS` of §4.14".** `LEGACY` is a literal in a shared namespace (hazard 32) that no register carries, and `issueDocument` takes the series from `policy.numbering.series` (`resolveSeries`, `packages/db/src/posting/issue.ts`), so honouring it would change a frozen function (hazard 8). Two series used by no other type and never re-used after cut-over meet the sentence's own purpose. ADR 0085 records it. Applied to §4.13.3 in this round.

**9B C2 — §4.2.7, §4.18 (a settlement that narrows a ratified row).** Round 3's row, quoted so no reviewer is asked to overturn a settlement they were not shown: “**`statusUrl` becomes `"/v1/companies/<companyId>/report-runs/<runId>"`** (ADR 0067), and the 202 body carries `jobId` for log correlation. **No slice mounts `/v1/jobs/{jobId}`** — §4.2.7 lists the path and assigns it to no module, and 6A dropped its own `statusUrl` for the same reason.” Its last sentence now reads: **9B mounts `/v1/jobs/{jobId}` as the generic job-status resource; a slice with a resource of its own (7A's `report-runs`, 7C's `exports`) still uses that, and no slice's 202 body points at `/v1/jobs` unless it has no resource of its own.** The precondition was re-verified on the tree (C16 item 3): 7C's 202 body carries `statusUrl: "/v1/companies/${companyId}/exports/${exportJobId}"` and 7A's `/v1/companies/${companyId}/report-runs/${runId}`, so no other slice's behaviour changes. 9B's own need: the 9B card names the status resource, spec:2206 requires one for a bulk endpoint, and an `admin.import.run` run is not a `report_run`. 9B ships `jobStatusRoutes` at `/v1/jobs`, `permissions: []`, `auth: "human"`, membership only (the precedent of `accounts`, `fiscal-periods` and `documents/{id}`), scoped by the job envelope's own `tenantId`; one `PROBES` key; not in `TENANT_FREE`. **This reverses part of a ratified row: it is implementation authorization under the owner's direction of 2026-11-13, recorded in `docs/review/2026-11-13-phase-9-decisions.md`, and awaits the owner's acceptance.** The plan's fallback — `GET …/imports/{runId}` alone, round 3 untouched — stays available to the owner at no cost to the rest of 9B. 4. **C1's premise holds**: §4.14 carries `OPENING_BALANCE`/`OB` and `OPENING_STOCK`/`OS`, and `issueDocument` resolves the series from the policy.
5. **The six `legacy_ref` tables keep the plan's names** — `app.document`, `app.party`, `app.item`, `app.account`, `app.employee`, `app.lot` — none carries the column yet, and `app.lot` carries `company_id`. The Drizzle mirrors declare indexes in the **array** form `(table) => [index(…).on(…)]`, not the object form the plan's Task 1 wrote; `account.ts` has an extra-config callback and `employee.ts` none (each gains one). `packages/db/test/schema-mirror.test.ts` pins the mirror count — **90** at 8D's head, **91** with `import_batch` (Task 2).
6. **Since 7C every `app` table is classified for the tenant export** — registered in `EXPORT_TABLES` or pinned whole in `NEVER_EXPORTED` (`packages/db/src/export/tables.ts`; `packages/db/test/export/tables.test.ts` fails on a table that is neither), and a live column a registered row does not list is reported `omitted` in `schema.json`. The plan predates 7C and classifies neither. **`legacy_ref` joins the column lists of the six registered rows** (the customer's own historical identifier, SAH-051, is part of their books and leaves with the row it describes — `employee`'s still behind `hr.employee.read`); **`import_batch` is pinned whole in `NEVER_EXPORTED` as plumbing**: its business half leaves as each master row's `legacy_ref`, and `source_hash`/`run_id` describe how a cut-over was rehearsed, not the books (ADR 0069's determinism).
7. **`import_batch` as built (Task 2)**: `loaded_by` references `app.principal(id)` (8C's `employee_ytd_opening.loaded_by` precedent); and `app_rw` holds **SELECT and INSERT only** — 0102 revokes the default UPDATE, so "a legacy key's mapping never moves" is a data-layer invariant, not only `recordBatch`'s behaviour. No DELETE (§3.5.4's list is unchanged). It joins no `lint-schema` set (§3.5.3), as the plan says.
8. **`ERRORS` rows are written `def(status, title, remedy)`** and pinned by name in `packages/contracts/test/contracts.test.ts`'s `CODES_AFTER_0B` with the total; `ERR_IMPORT_DUPLICATE_SOURCE_KEY` lands at Task 2 (409), `ERR_IMPORT_UNBALANCED_SOURCE` at Task 5 (422), each with the raise that `error-codes` demands.
9. **`packages/db` raises import refusals through `ImportBatchError`** (`code: "ERR_IMPORT_DUPLICATE_SOURCE_KEY"`, `detail`), on 8C's `OpeningError` shape — `packages/db` may not import `AppError` (§3.1) — rather than the plan's bare `Error` carrying the code in its message. It is N13's ninth name.
10. **The test tiers.** `packages/db/test/harness.ts`'s `withTenant(sql, tenantId, actorId, fn)` is the 4-argument helper Tasks 1–2's DB tests use; the `tests` tier's is the production one taking a `TenantContext` (8D A13 item 9). A slice appends to a 0B regression file through **`sliceRegression(sah, heading, slice, title, body)`** (`tests/support/regression.ts`), which hands `withTenant` and `expect` to the body — the plan's bare `describe` blocks with module-scope imports would shadow the 0B block's destructured parameters (`no-shadow`).
11. **The consumed predecessor surfaces are present with the plan's spelling**: `seedEmployee` (6C, 8A A17), `createHrKeyRing` and `DEV_HR_KEY` (8A), `upsertEmployeeYtdOpening`, `OpeningError` (8C), `sharedApi()` (0B), `JOBS["admin.import.run"]` (0B, owner 9B); `JOB_NAMES` stays sixteen.
12. **Commit attribution**: the plan's trailer line is superseded by the session's attribution lines (AGENTS.md).
13. **`NEVER_READ` is not in the `@dulja/importer` barrel.** The plan says 9A re-exports it; 9A T14 kept it in `packages/importer/src/snapshot.ts` (`new Set(["USERS.PASSWORD", "USERS.PIN"])`, upper case as the plan says), because §4.13.1's barrel list names the snapshot planner and its rules as 9A-internal. 9B Task 12's source-scan imports it inside the package (`../src/snapshot`); nothing outside `packages/importer` needs it.

**9B C17 — §3.4.1, §4.2.7, §4.6.1, §4.13.2 (9B Task 9, 2026-11-13).** Task 9's plan text keeps no record of a run beyond pg-boss's job row and `import_batch`, and three things it needs cannot live there: the owner's **account map** (the loaders that read it — `account`, `opening_balance`, `open_item` — need it in the job, and `pgboss.job` has no RLS, §4.2.6); a **dry run's** outcome (it writes no `import_batch` row, so `GET …/imports/{runId}` over `batchCounts` alone would 404 a run that succeeded); and the plan's **one-load-per-company** rule (its `singletonKey: companyId` on a standard queue takes pg-boss's 24-hour slot, which a FINISHED job still holds, so a dry run would refuse the real run that follows it the same day). So 9B takes its spare **`0103_create_import_run.sql`** (§3.4.1) for **`app.import_run`** (§4.6.1's row above), with full §3.3 treatment, a Drizzle mirror (`importRunTable`, the mirror count 91 → 92), `NEVER_EXPORTED` (plumbing, `export_job`'s reason) and 7A/7C's lease (`claimLeased`, `leaseFence`, `IMPORT_RUN_LEASE_SECONDS` = 14,400, `IMPORT_RUN_MAX_CLAIMS` = 2, `IMPORT_RUN_JOB_OPTIONS`). The store is `packages/db/src/import/run.ts`: `createImportRun`, `getImportRun`, `liveImportRun`, `listImportRuns`, `claimImportRun`, `importRunLeaseState`, `importRunFollowUpOptions`, `completeImportRun`, `failImportRun` and the types `ImportRunRow`, `ImportRunStatus`, `ImportRunLoaderCounts`, `NewImportRun`, `CompleteImportRun`, `ImportRunQueryParams`. C3's payload is **unchanged**; the row is authoritative and the handler fails a run whose payload disagrees with it. The wire adds `AccountMapSchema`, `AccountMapEntrySchema`, `ImportRunStatusSchema`, `ImportRunQuery`, `ImportRunDto` and `JobStatusDto` beside N12's names; `ImportRunSchema` carries the row (status, per-loader counts, skips, error) and `JobStatusSchema.output` is the job's **subject** `{ resourceUrl, status, error }`, never pg-boss's raw output. **The job-status gate as built** narrows C2's "membership only, scoped by the envelope's `tenantId`": the route answers only a job whose name has a registered subject (`admin.import.run`; 7A's and 7C's jobs keep their own resources and get the 404), and only to that run's **requester** while they still hold `admin.company.manage` in its company; every other id — unknown, another tenant's, another requester's — is one indistinguishable 404. `@dulja/importer` gains `ACCOUNT_MAP_TARGETS` and `SENSITIVE_TARGETS` (the CLI's two lists, moved to the registry so the worker reads the same ones), and `apps/worker` gains `@dulja/importer` as a dependency (`dependency-rule`, the runtime image). The gates and the job-status resource are **Proposed** (ADR 0084's Task 9 amendment) — implementation authorization under the owner's direction of 2026-11-13, not acceptance.

**9B C18 — §4.12.8, §4.16.2 (the Phase 8 raise; round 18 B14, round 19 item 16; 2026-11-14).** The `employee_ytd` dataset now reads the projection **plus** `app.employee_ytd_opening`, added at read time over the union of both tables' (company, employee, year) keys — gross and net exactly as `ytdFromEmployeeYtd` adds them, and each scheme's `employee`/`employer` share summed over the union of both `by_scheme` bags. B14 is unchanged: the opening is never a row of `app.employee_ytd`, the step-12 MERGE and the nightly rebuild never read it. The dataset's id, columns, read code (`hr.payroll.read`, the opening's export gate too) and the registry's count (34) are unchanged; a new dataset was not an option because a code's `dataset.source` is fixed across its versions (7A's review). `hr.annual_statement` moves to **`definitionVersion` 2**, its footer naming the opening, so a run records which basis it printed; `tieOut: projection: employee_ytd` stays, and its executed arm (`tests/invariants/support/reports.ts`) reads the projection and the opening independently and adds them as `Money`, both directions per scheme. Round 19 item 16's last sentence ("The statement reads the `employee_ytd` projection only") is superseded by this row.

**9B C19 — §3.11, §4.2.4, §4.13.2 (9B review, finding 1; 2026-11-14).** `LEGACY_ODBC_DSN` is read process-wide by a worker that serves every tenant, and nothing bound it to a tenant or company: any holder of `admin.company.manage` in any company could `POST …/imports` and have the worker load the one configured legacy database — employees' sensitive fields included — into their own. **`LEGACY_IMPORT_TARGET=<tenantId>:<companyId>`** (§3.11's new row) names the one company it may be loaded into. `@dulja/importer` gains `ImportTarget`, `IMPORT_TARGET_ENV`, `importTargetFromEnv` and `assertImportTarget` (`packages/importer/src/load/target.ts`); **`LoadSourceFactory` becomes `(target: ImportTarget) => Promise<LoadSource>`** and `loadSourceFromEnv(target)` refuses before it connects (an injected factory may ignore the argument, so existing callers are unchanged in behaviour). The `admin.import.run` handler asserts the binding for every run before the source is opened, whatever factory `runLoad` holds; a refusal is the run's `ERR_IMPORT_SOURCE_NOT_BOUND` (403, §4.2.4's new row), and its words never name the bound tenant or company. **The API does not refuse up front**: it never holds the binding (`containerSecrets(env, "api")` does not pass it), the worker's refusal precedes any read, and a refused run is legible on the status resource. **The CLI** asks the binding of `load` and `reconcile-cut-over` whenever the DSN comes from `LEGACY_ODBC_DSN`; an explicit `--dsn` or `--fixture` names the source on the same command line as the target and needs none. ADR 0084 decision 21 (Proposed).

**9B C20 — §4.2.7, §4.13.2 (9B review, finding 4; 2026-11-14).** The load runs as the system principal, so `admin.company.manage` — the route's gate — was the only authority a run was ever asked for, and that code alone posted an `OPENING_BALANCE` (whose policy posts under `accounting.journal.post`), an `OPENING_STOCK` (`inventory.receipt.post`), sealed employee fields and YTD openings. On 7A's "the writer holds the permission" (`assertDatasetGate`), `packages/db/src/import/gates.ts` adds **`IMPORT_LOADER_WRITE_CODES`** (one row per registered loader, pinned by `@dulja/importer`'s registry test: masters `inventory.item.manage`, accounts `accounting.account.manage`, parties `accounting.party.manage`, employees `hr.employee.manage` + `hr.compensation.manage` + `hr.employee.read_sensitive`, both openings and the open items their policies' `approval.post`, the YTD opening `hr.payroll.post`), `importWriteCodes`, `unmappedImportTargets` and `missingImportWriteCodes` (`app.principal_has(…, company, null)`). `POST …/imports` keeps `admin.company.manage` as its gate and refuses (403 `ERR_RBAC_FORBIDDEN`, naming each code) a requester lacking any code of a loader the run executes, `only` respected; the handler asks the same of `requested_by` when it claims the run, before the source is opened, and fails closed on a registered loader with no row. The trial-balance opening and the open items also refuse a company holding a posted or reversed document no document loader's `import_batch` row (nor its reversal) points at (`refuseForeignPostings`); opening stock keeps its own movement guard. **A tightening of a gate**; ADR 0084 decision 22 (Proposed).

**9B C21 — §4.13.2 (9B review, finding 5; 2026-11-14).** `LoadContext` gains optional **`heartbeat?: () => Promise<void>`**, called by `runLoad` before every page's transaction — an additive widening like C14. `packages/db/src/jobs/lease.ts` gains **`renewLeased(tx, lease, id, attempt, minAgeSeconds)`** → `"renewed" | "fresh" | "superseded"` (the row locked; 7A's and 7C's leases are unchanged), and the import store `renewImportRunLease` and `IMPORT_RUN_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` (300). The worker's heartbeat renews its claim, so a load longer than `IMPORT_RUN_LEASE_SECONDS` keeps it and pg-boss's redelivery at its expiry defers past the live claim instead of reclaiming and loading beside it; a load whose claim was superseded after a genuine lapse stops before its next page and records nothing. `expireInSeconds` stays the lease. ADR 0084 decision 23 (Proposed).

**9B C22 — §4.2.7 (9B review, finding 7; 2026-11-14).** A delivery that finds a load already running in its worker process schedules a follow-up job (`importRunBusyFollowUpOptions`: key `<runId>:busy`, due after `IMPORT_RUN_BUSY_RETRY_SECONDS` = 300, the lease's retry budget) instead of throwing and spending a retry. `POST …/imports` first calls **`supersedeStaleImportRuns`**: a run still `queued` with no claim (`attempts = 0`) more than `IMPORT_RUN_LEASE_SECONDS` after it was requested has lost its job, and is failed with a stable `ERR_INTERNAL` reason as the requester, so `import_run_one_live_per_company` can never block a company for ever. A claimed run is never superseded. No new route (the smaller correct fix than a cancel verb). ADR 0084 decision 24 (Proposed).

**9B C23 — §4.13.1 (9B review, finding 8; 2026-11-14).** 9A's reconciliation rules were written in the dossier's unprefixed spelling (`ACCTOTALS.ACCOUNT`/`DEBIT`/`CREDIT`), 9B's loaders and cut-over corpus in the prefixed one (`ACTACC`/`ACTDEBIT`/`ACTCREDIT`), so `aggregate_drift` was `source_absent` against every source the trial-balance load accepts and `reconcileCutOver`'s `explain()` could never name the part of `3900` that is `ACCTOTALS`' own drift. **`AggregateRule` gains optional `storedSpellings?: readonly AggregateSpelling[]`** (`AggregateSpelling { key: readonly string[]; column: string }`, exported from `legacy/aggregates.ts`, not the barrel) — an additive widening of a barrel type; every existing rule is unchanged. `reconcile/probe.ts` gains `firstSpelling(reader, table, spellings)`, which answers the first COMPLETE spelling the table has, so a key of one spelling is never joined to a figure of another. `ACCTOTALS.DEBIT`/`CREDIT` (drift), `ACCTOTALS` and `BILLITEMS.QNT` (null_poison), `ACCTOTALS` (duplicate_aggregates) and `BILLITEMS.MATERIAL`/`WAREHOUSE` (orphans) take the 9B spellings, and a drift row read under one says so in its `derivation`. Rules with no 9B spelling, or whose 9B column means something else (`BILLITEMS.BTMQNT` is a magnitude beside a direction flag, so `MATOBJECTS`/`MATQUANTITY` drift is not respelt), are unchanged and recorded in the decisions file. Which spelling the live catalogue holds stays OD-17's.

**9B C24 — §4.13.2, §4.14 (9B review, finding 3; 2026-11-14).** §4.13.2's `runLoad` hands `load` only the rows no earlier run recorded, and `import_batch` admits neither UPDATE nor DELETE (0102), so the two `wholeTable` loaders (C13) — the trial-balance `OPENING_BALANCE` and `OPENING_STOCK` — cannot be "reversed and loaded again" as their refusals advised: a re-run computed the opening from the late rows alone. **Both are one-shot**: `refusePriorOpening` (package-internal, `load/document.ts`) refuses `ERR_IMPORT_DUPLICATE_SOURCE_KEY` whenever any earlier run recorded a row of the loader, its document posted, reversed or never posted; a correction after cut-over is a JOURNAL or a STOCK_COUNT, and a full re-import goes into a fresh company. Opening stock refuses a company holding any stock movement. Every "reverse" remedy is withdrawn (the openings', `refuseForeignPostings`' and the changed-row conflict's). §4.13.2's rule for skips is stated whole: a `map` skip is not recorded and is retried; a skip `load` reports (C15) is recorded and final; a row that maps late into a recorded whole-table opening is refused. `reconcileCutOver` explains a stock position the load read (every row recorded) and did not open by the skip register, and only that. ADR 0084 decisions 26–27, ADR 0086 decision 9 (Proposed).

## Round 21 — the 2026-11-15 full review's fixes

Rows here come from the fix branches of the 2026-11-15 full review (`docs/review/2026-11-15-full-review.md`); each names its finding ids. They are proposals until the owner accepts the ADR each one cites.

**R21 UI-03/UI-11 — §4.2.7, a new membership-scoped selector (ADR 0089, Proposed; branch `claude/fix-company-lookup`).** A new module **`/v1/me`** (`meRouteModule`, router `meCompanyRoutes`, `apps/api/src/routes/me.ts`) mounts **`GET /v1/me/companies`** behind `membershipOnly()` with `permissions: []`, so `assertRouteGates` admits it as a safe-method membership route. It answers `MyCompaniesSchema` (`@dulja/contracts/admin/my-companies`, `.strict()`): `{ companies: [{ id, code, name, branches: [{ id, code, nameEn, nameAr }] }] }` — every company in which the caller holds a role assignment that has not expired, and in each, the unarchived `BRANCH` values `app.actor_in_branch` admits (all of them for a company-wide assignment, the assignment's own otherwise). A member with no live role gets `{ companies: [] }`, never a refusal. It grants nothing: no permission code is added or widened, and every screen opened with a company from it still asks its own gate at that company. The back office's `useCompanyId` (`COMPANY_QUERY_KEY` unchanged) and the report parameter form's `branch` lookup read it instead of `GET /v1/companies` (gated `admin.company.manage`) and `/v1/staff-context` (seven staff codes). `GET /v1/companies` and `/v1/staff-context` are unchanged. No migration: `app.company`, `app.dimension_value` and `app.role_assignment` carry tenant RLS only, so the caller's own transaction reads them.
